title: 'Bursa Sheds 2.4% For Week As Yields, Foreign Selling Hit Sentiment
body: 'Bursa Malaysia ended the Sept 28-Oct 2 week sharply lower, with the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) losing 40.75 points, or 2.4%, to 1,630.87 from the previous Friday’s 1,671.62, as rising global bond yields, elevated oil prices and persistent foreign selling weighed on sentiment.  The benchmark started the week marginally lower, slipping 0.09% to 1,670.02 on Sept 28, as investors remained cautious amid a lack of fresh catalysts and continued external headwinds.  Selling intensified the next day, when the FBM KLCI tumbled 26.06 points, or 1.56%, to 1,643.96, pressured by surging bond yields and Brent crude prices around US$107 a barrel, which reignited inflation concerns and dampened risk appetite.  The market rebounded 0.43% to 1,651.17 on Sept 30 as bargain hunters returned following the sharp sell-off, although broader sentiment remained cautious ahead of key US inflation data.  That recovery proved short-lived, with the index plunging another 1.26% to 1,630.36 the following day, dragged by selling in heavyweights including Maybank, Public Bank, CIMB, TNB and IHH Healthcare. Weak domestic manufacturing activity and continued foreign outflows added to the pressure.  Bursa eked out a 0.03% gain to 1,630.87 to close out the trading week as bargain hunting cushioned the recent sell-off, but the rebound remained muted amid weakness across regional markets and caution ahead of US labour data.  Overall, the FBM KLCI recorded losses in three of the five sessions, with external rate and inflation concerns dominating trading despite intermittent bargain hunting.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia dijangka pulih sederhana minggu ini
body: 'PETALING JAYA: Bursa Malaysia dijangka memasuki fasa pemulihan sederhana minggu ini selepas mengalami tekanan jualan ketara minggu lalu, dengan indeks FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) dijangka bergerak dalam julat 1,620 hingga 1,650 mata. Pensyarah Kanan i-CATS University College, Kuching, Profesor Madya Dr. Abu Sofian Yaacob berkata, indeks penanda aras itu berpotensi ditutup sekitar 1,640 hingga 1,650 mata sekiranya sentimen pasaran global bertambah baik. Katanya, paras 1,620 mata merupakan tahap sokongan penting, manakala 1,650 mata pula menjadi paras rintangan utama. “Sekiranya paras 1,650 mata berjaya ditembusi secara kukuh, terdapat ruang untuk FBM KLCI menguji paras 1,660 mata. “Bagaimanapun, kenaikan dijangka tidak berlaku secara agresif kerana pelabur masih berdepan beberapa ketidaktentuan luaran. “Antaranya termasuk hasil bon Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang masih tinggi, turun naik harga minyak mentah serta ketegangan geopolitik yang boleh meningkatkan semula risiko inflasi,” katanya kepada Utusan Malaysia. Menurut Abu Sofian, data pekerjaan AS yang lebih lemah memberikan sedikit kelegaan kepada pasaran kerana mengurangkan kebimbangan terhadap kemungkinan pengetatan dasar monetari yang lebih agresif oleh Rizab Persekutuan (Fed). “Pada masa sama, perkembangan Wall Street dan hala tuju kadar faedah AS akan terus menjadi antara pemacu utama sentimen Bursa Malaysia minggu ini. “Di peringkat domestik, tumpuan juga akan diberikan kepada prestasi sektor perbankan, teknologi, utiliti dan tenaga, selain aliran dana asing,” katanya. Beliau berkata, secara keseluruhannya, pergerakan pasaran minggu ini lebih mencerminkan pemulihan teknikal dan pengumpulan saham secara selektif, berbanding permulaan satu rali kukuh. “Pelabur masih dijangka mengambil pendekatan berhati-hati sehingga terdapat isyarat lebih jelas mengenai hala tuju kadar faedah global, harga minyak dan perkembangan geopolitik,” katanya. Sementara itu, CIMB Securities berkata, FBM KLCI susut 4.33 peratus bulan ke bulan atau 74.71 mata kepada 1,651 mata pada September 2026, sekali gus mencatatkan prestasi bulanan terburuk setakat tahun ini. “Penurunan itu menjadikan prestasi FBM KLCI bagi tempoh sembilan bulan pertama 2026 susut 1.72 peratus. “Tekanan jualan berterusan oleh pelabur asing dan peningkatan mendadak hasil bon global mengatasi prestasi ekonomi domestik Malaysia yang kekal berdaya tahan. “Pelabur asing merekodkan jualan bersih dianggarkan RM1.69 bilion pada September 2026, manakala pegangan asing dalam ekuiti Malaysia susut ke paras terendah sepanjang masa iaitu 17.8 peratus pada akhir September 2026 berbanding 18.1 peratus pada akhir Ogos 2026,” katanya. –UTUSAN The post Bursa Malaysia dijangka pulih sederhana minggu ini appeared first on Utusan Malaysia.

title: 'MUFG Sees Ringgit Dipping Below RM4 Against US Dollar by 3Q 2027
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): The ringgit is expected to outperform most Asian currencies in the final quarter of 2026, supported by Malaysia’s strong electronics exports despite pressure from higher oil prices, according to MUFG Bank. It also expects Bank Negara Malaysia to maintain the overnight policy rate at 2.75% until the third quarter of next year as inflation remains contained. The ringgit was trading around 4.09 against the US dollar on Monday morning. MUFG expects it to strengthen to 4.03 by end-2026, before advancing further to 3.98 by the third quarter of 2027. MUFG expects the ringgit to be the strongest performing Asian currency covered in its latest foreign-exchange outlook. “Malaysia’s electronics surplus continues to cushion the oil shock,” MUFG said, adding that Malaysia's trade position remains relatively resilient amid elevated energy prices. “This means higher oil prices are likely to remain a headwind for the ringgit rather than derail its medium-term outlook,” MUFG said. Malaysia is also benefiting from continued investment in information and communications technology, including data centres and cloud computing. Services investment approvals rose more than 20% year-on-year in the first half of 2026, supported largely by ICT-related investments. MUFG said stronger US spending on computers and related equipment has also helped support demand for Malaysian electrical and electronics exports. “MYR fundamentals remain intact despite higher oil prices and the recent bond sell-off,” the bank said. While near-term volatility could persist as investors watch higher fuel-subsidy costs and global bond yields, MUFG said Malaysia’s resilient external position, improving capital flows and attractive valuations should continue to support the ringgit over the medium term. The bank also pointed to Malaysia’s stronger economic growth, with gross domestic product expanding 6% year-on-year in the second quarter, compared with an average pre-pandemic growth pace of 4.9%. title: 'Oct 23 ruling on bid to restrain RHB from closing Maritime Network's accounts
body: 'Oct 23 ruling on bid to restrain RHB from closing Maritime Network's accounts KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 24): The High Court here on Thursday fixed Oct 23 to rule on a shipping company's bid to restrain RHB Bank Bhd (LK:RHBBANK) from closing two of its long-standing accounts, pending the disposal of its full suit. Judicial Commissioner Elesabet Paya Wan set the date after hearing submissions from P Taneswaran, acting for Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, and the bank's counsel, Gan Khong Aik. Taneswaran submitted that the bank had failed to establish any breach of terms or requirements by the plaintiff, Maritime Network, that would justify closing its accounts. He further argued that the bank owed Maritime Network both a fiduciary duty and a duty of care. Gan countered that no fiduciary relationship or duty of care arose between the bank and the shipping company, submitting that the relationship between a bank and its customer is that of debtor and creditor. In October last year, the High Court granted a temporary injunction restraining RHB from closing the two long-standing accounts, pending the hearing of the company's application for a full injunction. According to court documents, the company has held a multi-currency account and a current account with RHB since 2005. On Oct 6, 2025, it received a termination notice dated Oct 1, 2025, stating that the bank intended to close both accounts and terminate all related services within 14 days, citing breaches of its internal policies and guidelines. The company, however, claimed that RHB had failed to specify which policies or guidelines were allegedly breached. The plaintiff said an ongoing dispute over the accounts had earlier led to its pre-trial discovery application being dismissed by the High Court on July 2, 2025. The company subsequently appealed to the Court of Appeal, which in December last year allowed its appeal against the dismissal of the pre-trial discovery application. The appellate court then ordered RHB to produce its minimum due diligence guidelines governing foreign-exchange transactions to the company within 45 days. Maritime Network further alleged that the bank's vague allegations placed it in a position of uncertainty, depriving it of any opportunity to defend itself. This conduct, the company asserted, amounted to an abuse of power that prejudiced its rights. It also claimed that the bank's conduct demonstrated an intention to oppress rather than protect its legitimate banking interests. Uploaded by Tham Yek Lee The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: 'Smoky Singapore gears up to talk money ahead of F1
body: 'SINGAPORE, Oct 5 (Reuters) - Regional, business, cryptocurrency and sports leaders are meeting in Singapore for a slew of finance-focused conferences ahead of this weekend's Grand Prix as haze continues to shroud the city-state. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, famed investor Ray Dalio and Eric Trump, co-founder of the family-backed cryptocurrency business, are expected, while hundreds of thousands of Formula 1 fans will converge on the island. The night race through the city streets and some 40 sideline events are typically a global showcase for Singapore and hotel room rates have soared. The Fullerton Bay Hotel next to the race track is charging S$5,030 ($3,933) a night for a room that typically costs $1,460. This year the pall from Indonesia's most intense fires in more than a decade will probably form part of the backdrop. Air quality was forecast at the "high moderate to low unhealthy" range on Monday by Singapore's environment agency. No longer-range forecast was provided for Sunday's Grand Prix. Singapore's tourism board said F1 and its surrounding events had "strong momentum" reflecting confidence despite economic and geopolitical uncertainty. Jitters in financial markets where bond prices are slumping and sentiment around on AI is shifting from euphoric to cautious will occupy investors and business chiefs at the Forbes CEO Conference andMilken Asia Summit, which runs from Wednesday. Trump, a co-founder of crypto venture World Liberty Financial, is due to speak at the TOKEN2049 cryptocurrency event with digital asset markets fragile following a bruising 12 months. A hoped-for regulatory framework failed last month to clear the US Senate, in part as President Donald Trump's personal crypto dealings became a flashpoint for Democrats. Despite a recent bounce, the total value of the cryptocurrency market is down about a quarter over the last 12 months to $3 trillion, according to data aggregator CoinGecko. Still, organisers say their event is nearly sold out with 25,000 attendees expected, the same as last year. The Straits Times reported that about 90,000 "c-suite," or top ranking, executives will be in town. F1 generates around S$145 million in incremental tourism receipts for Singapore each year, according to official estimates. Maybank economistChua Hak Bin expects it to hit S$160 million this year, along with "wider economic benefits" from deals struck at sideline events. ($1 = 1.2794 Singapore dollars) (Reporting by Xinghui Kok and Tom Westbrook; Editing by Kim Coghill)

title: 'Accelerating earnings and returns under Acceler8
body: 'Accelerating earnings and returns under Acceler8 This article first appeared in The Edge Malaysia Weekly on October 5, 2026 - October 11, 2026 Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd (KL:ABMB) has made a clean sweep this year, bagging all three awards under the financial services (below RM10 billion market capitalisation) category. The awards are for the Highest return on equity (ROE) over three years, the Highest growth in profit after tax over three years and the highest returns to shareholders over three years. This also marks the banking group’s first wins in The Edge Billion Ringgit Club (BRC) Awards. Alliance Bank’s net profit growth over the past three years has been impressive. It registered a three-year compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 11.8% between FY2022 and FY2025. Net earnings hit successive record highs as the banking group made significant strides under its Acceler8 2027 transformation strategy. From RM572.8 million in FY2022, net profit grew 18.33% to RM677.8 million in FY2023 and 1.87% to RM690.5 million the following year. Net profit continued to grow in FY2025, rising 8.7% year on year (y-o-y) to a record RM750.7 million, supported by a record revenue of RM2.3 billion arising from a 13.2% growth in net interest income. Net interest margin in FY2025 stood at 2.45%, while other operating income increased 7.7% y-o-y, largely due to higher revenue from treasury and investment income as well as trade fees. Alliance Bank, whose financial year ends on March 31, again posted a record net profit and revenue of RM826.5 million and RM2.5 billion respectively for FY2026. Achieving a top-quartile ROE in the banking industry is one of Alliance Bank’s goals under the Acceler8 2027 programme. Between FY2023 and FY2025, its ROE averaged between 9.9% and 10.3%, resulting in an adjusted weighted ROE of 10.1% over the period. Meanwhile, Alliance Bank’s net profit growth momentum has caught investors’ attention. Its share price rose from RM2.82 on March 31, 2023, to RM3.26 on March 31, 2024. The upward trajectory continued over the following two years, with the stock reaching RM4.82 on March 31, 2026 — the final date of the review period for the BRC awards. This translated into a three-year shareholders’ return CAGR of 19.5%. Its share price slipped slightly to a low of RM4.42 on April 13, 2026, before rebounding to close at RM4.92 on Aug 28. Alliance Bank paid a lower dividend of 19.1 sen per share in FY2026, compared with 19.4 sen in FY2025, 22.3 sen in FY2024 and 22 sen in FY2023. The group has started FY2027 on a strong note. Its 1QFY2027 net profit rose 25% y-o-y to RM248.3 million, mainly due to a 98.7% decline in loan loss provisions following the recovery of a corporate loan in the construction sector. In a report, CGS International Securities anticipates that the normalisation of loan loss provisions will result in a drop in 2QFY2027 net profit, bringing it back in line with the levels recorded between 2QFY2026 and 4QFY2026. CIMB Research, which has a “hold” call on the stock, pointed out that the banking group has demonstrated a steadier asset quality trend on a y-o-y basis, with its gross impaired loan (GIL) ratio edging down to 1.83% from 1.96% a year earlier, driven by credit recovery in its books. However, GIL ratios for its consumer and small to medium enterprises portfolios continued to deteriorate, rising to 2.2% and 2.1% respectively. The 30 days-past-due ratio also continued to creep up, although the research house noted that the stress was isolated to certain higher-risk borrowers. CGS also said Alliance Bank could see an enhancement of 60 to 70 basis points in its common equity Tier-1 (CET1) capital ratio following the Basel III reforms. “The bank does not expect to pay out any excess capital from the above as special dividends. Instead, the enhancement in its CET1 capital ratio would enable the bank to increase its dividend payout ratio (from 40%-50% guided for FY2027) in the longer term,” according to the bank. CGS has an “add” call on the banking group with a target price of RM5.70, citing potential rerating catalysts including strong growth in non-interest income, above-industry loan growth, potential write-back in management overlays and its expectation of a higher dividend payout ratio from FY2027 to FY2029. title: 'You can prove the other side was wrong, win the case, and still end up with almost nothing - Newswav
body: 'That is basically what happened in a recent Court of Appeal case. A buyer successfully proved that RHB Bank had wrongly terminated an auction sale. So you might think the next part was easy. The bank was wrong. Pay the buyer. The Sessions Court awarded the buyer RM863,795.37. The High Court agreed. But the Court of Appeal later cancelled almost the entire award and ordered the money to be returned to RHB. Why? Because saying, “You caused me a loss” is not enough. You still have to prove exactly how much you lost. For example, the buyer claimed RM350,000 based on the difference between the property price and a valuation done many years later. The problem was that the breach happened in 2007, but the valuation was from 2020. The buyer also claimed more than 15 years of rental payments. But there were gaps in the documents, and problems showing that all of that rent was actually caused by the bank’s actions. There was also a RM5,000 legal fee claim, but again, there was not enough basis to simply make the bank pay it. The RM26,000 deposit was different. The Court agreed the buyer was entitled to it, but the money had already been sent to the Registrar of Unclaimed Moneys, so it had to be claimed from there. The lesson is simple. Winning the argument is only step one. You must also be able to show: What exactly did you lose? How did you calculate it? Did the other side actually cause that loss? Do you have documents to prove it? Did you do anything to reduce the loss? If you cannot prove those things properly, even a very large damages award can disappear on appeal. Case: RHB Bank Berhad v Tee Ban Tiong, Court of Appeal, decided on 27 August 2026. title: 'Private Deal: Celebrity-founded nasi padang restaurant chain Bumbu Babah aims to raise RM20 mil
body: 'Private Deal: Celebrity-founded nasi padang restaurant chain Bumbu Babah aims to raise RM20 mil This article first appeared in Wealth, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 28, 2026 - October 4, 2026 Transitioning from the entertainment industry to the food and beverage (F&B) sector is not easy, but when comedian Ajak Shiro heard his child express a desire to start a fried chicken business, he thought of making the idea a reality. Ajak, whose real name is Mohd Hanaffi Razak, looked for a business partner. This ended up being Aliey Othman, an F&B industry veteran with 20 years of experience and involvement in many notable brands. Starting with fried chicken as the foundation, their conversation gradually evolved into a discussion on nasi padang, a Minangkabau meal of steamed rice and a variety of side dishes. “In Malaysia, nasi padang hasn’t become mainstream yet. Moreover, it is considered expensive, so we thought of coming up with a large-scale nasi padang brand, but with low prices,” says Ajak. He went on to start Babah Ventures Sdn Bhd (BBV) and opened its first stall, named Bumbu Babah, at a food court in Giant Batu Caves in November 2024. There are now more than 50 outlets across Peninsular Malaysia and the company is on track to reaching 60 outlets this year. Delivering affordable and accessible food is important to Ajak. So, a plate of nasi padang can be priced as low as RM9.90. The uncompromised value the company offers in terms of price point and flavour has become Bumbu Babah’s unique selling point, he says. “At this time, we understand the current economic situation. If we look at the customers now, they value the experience of eating in restaurants more, they like good food, but they’re quite sensitive to price,” says Ajak. To accelerate its next stage of growth, BBV will launch an equity crowdfunding (ECF) campaign on pitchIN to attract institutional investors with its numbers, create a fundraising exercise with customer engagement and possibly look at fast-tracking to an initial public offering (IPO) by 2028 at the earliest. On the ECF platform itself, the company aims to raise between RM5 million and RM20 million, with shares issued at RM10 each. BBV plans to allocate 40% of the funds from the ECF campaign to acquiring its top-performing licensed outlets. Two activities, the setting up of corporate-owned outlets in malls and supporting the rollout of the new concept, will be allocated 25% each, while the final 10% will go to enhancing technology and its working capital. Behind the quick expansion The business has been able to expand quickly because its licensees have shown interest in opening more outlets. “We call it a licensed-and-managed concept because we are very mindful that we don’t want licensees or franchisees to run the outlets their own way and steer away from the standard operating procedures (SOPs). So, we came up with a structure where they provide the funding and become a passive investor in the outlet,” says BBV corporate finance manager Chan Eu-Jinn. This is how the system works: the licensee fully owns the outlet, but BBV continues to run it as if it belonged to the company. BBV also charges a management fee based on a percentage of the licensed outlet’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) on a monthly basis. “If the outlet is not profitable, we do not charge the management fee, so we have to ensure that it is run properly,” he notes. There are currently seven corporate-owned Bumbu Babah outlets. The remaining outlets are owned by licensees. BBV aims to continue expanding, but with a strategy centred more on mall outlets. “Our MyTown, Melawati Mall and IOI City Mall outlets are doing well, but we are still not in a lot of the major malls in the market yet. With the funds raised, we can then invest in this,” says Chan. BBV acknowledges that F&B brands have a tendency to overexpand, and Chan says the company has addressed this by setting a target number of outlets for Bumbu Babah restaurants so as to retain operational quality. “When we hit our target number [we may look more into] maintenance, but we will not be growing for the sake of opening and then cannibalising ourselves.” Bumbu Babah was also able to grow quickly with the introduction of a centralised kitchen to ensure the quality of the food across its licensed outlets remains consistent. Chan says the curry, sambal, proteins and sides are prepared in advance and sent straight to the outlets. This contributes to the efficiency of its operations, as the staff are able to run the basic equipment at the outlets by following the SOPs. Ajak plans to develop more offerings beyond Bumbu Babah’s nasi padang menu. Reflecting this resolve is BBV’s recent collaboration with local music group KRU to open a fine-casual-dining restaurant called KRU Cafe. “We will also have stalls where we will have food menus that include Chinese and Indian food. This is one of the projects that we will implement in time to come, and I think this is one of the reasons why Bumbu Babah will continue to grow in the F&B industry for many more years,” he says. On solid operational and financial ground Based on its audited financial statements, BBV is in a strong financial position. The company has four income streams: retail sales at corporate-owned outlets, central kitchen supplies, monthly management fees and turnkey outlet set-ups involving the building and selling of completed outlets to licensees. For its financial year 2025 (FY2025) ended on Dec 31, the parent company made RM10.4 million in revenue, while the consolidated group revenue came up to RM25.9 million. As for net profit, the parent company recorded RM2.5 million, while the group registered RM3.2 million. This gives the group a net profit margin of 12.5%, which Tradeview Capital research analyst Tan Jia Hui says sits at the higher end of the F&B industry norm of 5% to 12%. “The normalised margin is more likely to settle at around 10% in the upcoming years, given the margin mix [of all four income streams],” she adds. The margin is also anchored by a low marketing spend of roughly 1.3% of its revenue due to the marketing pull of Ajak. The group’s FY2025 earnings quality can be considered clean with only RM24,000 coming from one other source of income, which is the interest from its fixed deposits. Tan notes that liquidity was BBV’s clearest improvement in FY2025, with the current ratio moving from 0.21 times to 1.71 times and the quick ratio from 0.20 times to 1.70 times. Working capital swung from -RM560,000 to RM1.52 million, while its return on assets rose sharply from 6.6% to 74%. The company has also fully repaid shareholder advances in FY2025, leaving the group free of debt or borrowings. “In FY2024, the business leaned on RM600,000 of shareholder and director advances and stretched trade payables to fund itself, so its total liabilities-to-equity ratio stood at 13.9 times. In FY2025, those advances were repaid, so there are no borrowings and no non-current liabilities. The group holds net cash of RM1.47 million, taking the liabilities-to-equity ratio down to 0.97 times,” he says. Gordon Low, founder and managing partner of management consulting firm PiValue Strategy, agrees with Tan. He notes that the company’s financial improvements are backed by positive cash flow rather than being just profit on paper. “This is a company entering its next fundraising round from a position of real financial substance, which is a reasonable and encouraging starting point for the growth questions that follow,” he says. On the operational aspects, Low sees that BBV is signalling a strong early product market fit, although the goals set alongside its projected pace of growth may pose a challenge if not met with a grounded strategy. The affordability and everyday-meal positioning allow Bumbu Babah’s nasi padang to be embedded in local eating habits and food that consumers can enjoy regularly. “This naturally supports higher purchase frequency and repeat sales than non-local or occasion-based cuisines,” he says. Zooming in on the numbers Supported by its milestones, such as the record for selling the highest number of nasi padang servings sold in a day (23,674 plates), the business’ traction is generated by genuine consumer acceptance rather than hype alone, says Low. However, to maintain a returning customer base amid the competitive F&B space, the company must be able to align its marketing and promotional activities with its forecast growth. BBV’s projections show its system-wide revenue jumping to RM102 million in FY2026 from RM50 million in FY2025, with a forecast of 80 outlets. It also expects the figure to rise to RM232.4 million in FY2027. Low says this implies a growth of roughly 104% in FY2026, then a further 128% jump in FY2027. He notes that reaching the FY2027 target would require the group to double its footprint again in a single year. “Using the FY2026 target of 80 outlets as a base, a rough per-outlet run rate of around RM1.3 million suggests BBV would need somewhere in the region of 150 to 180 outlets to support the 2027 projected figure at a similar productivity level,” he says. “This indicates nearly doubling the outlet count again within a single year, an even faster pace than the 50 to 80 outlets planned for 2026. It is a mildly aggressive projection, and the credibility of the entire plan rests heavily on the growth strategy behind it.” Looking at its valuation for the ECF campaign, BBV currently has a reasonable trailing price-to-sales ratio of 3.09 times, based on a valuation of RM80 million against the FY2025 group revenue, which will drop to 1.11 times if its FY2026 forecast of RM72 million is met. However, the trailing price-earnings ratio (PER) of 24.7 times, based on its FY2025 net profit, reflects a premium valuation as it comes in higher than peer Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd’s (KL:KOPI) trailing PER of 20 times at IPO. “This could ease as outlet count and sales scale, giving operating leverage and central production efficiencies room to lift net margins and bring the multiple down over time,” says Low. Tan cautions investors that BBV is materially smaller than the entire system. The audited FY2025 group revenue of RM25.9 million is roughly half the cited system-wide revenue of RM50 million because licensed outlets only contribute to the group through management fees and supply payments, rather than their full retail turnover. This means a huge chunk of the RM50 million earned by its network of 52 stores belongs to the individual licensed store owners rather than the company issuing the shares. The group revenue of RM25.9 million reflects the actual audited revenue recorded on the parent company’s books, which is the pool of money that generates profit for shareholders. Also seen in the financial statements is the parent company’s operating profit for FY2025, which appears to be cushioned from non-operational income. “The parent company’s profit after tax of RM2.5 million is flattered by RM1.5 million of intra-group dividends and a RM280,000 disposal gain. Strip out both and the standalone operating profit is closer to RM900,000,” says Tan. Put simply, intra-group dividends are distributions of profit paid by a subsidiary company to its parent company or another related entity in the same corporate group. Chan offers an explanation for the disposal gain, saying that BBV began reorganising its activities into two new subsidiaries established in the second quarter of FY2025. The subsidiaries are BBV Restaurants Sdn Bhd (BBVR), which handles store management, and BBV Trading Sdn Bhd, which is in charge of supply, trading and store set-up. This internal restructuring led to a transfer of assets and businesses related to the Melawati Mall and TF Value outlets from BBV to BBVR, and created a one-time gain on disposal on BBV’s standalone financial statements. “These dividends are eliminated upon consolidation because they represent intercompany transactions between entities of the same group. Accordingly, these dividend payments have no impact on BBVs consolidated revenue, profit or profit margins. The same principle applies to the one-off gain arising from the disposal of assets,” says Chan. Another accounting flag lies in the brand’s intangible assets that fell from RM590,000 in FY2024 to RM530,000 in FY2025. The figure, which equates to 12% of its total assets, had its amortisation period shortened from 60 years to 10 years and reclassified, posing a potential impairment risk. 'Private Deal: Celebrity-founded nasi padang restaurant chain Bumbu Babah aims to raise RM20 mil This article first appeared in Wealth, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 28, 2026 - October 4, 2026 Transitioning from the entertainment industry to the food and beverage (F&B) sector is not easy, but when comedian Ajak Shiro heard his child express a desire to start a fried chicken business, he thought of making the idea a reality. Ajak, whose real name is Mohd Hanaffi Razak, looked for a business partner. This ended up being Aliey Othman, an F&B industry veteran with 20 years of experience and involvement in many notable brands. Starting with fried chicken as the foundation, their conversation gradually evolved into a discussion on nasi padang, a Minangkabau meal of steamed rice and a variety of side dishes. “In Malaysia, nasi padang hasn’t become mainstream yet. Moreover, it is considered expensive, so we thought of coming up with a large-scale nasi padang brand, but with low prices,” says Ajak. He went on to start Babah Ventures Sdn Bhd (BBV) and opened its first stall, named Bumbu Babah, at a food court in Giant Batu Caves in November 2024. There are now more than 50 outlets across Peninsular Malaysia and the company is on track to reaching 60 outlets this year. Delivering affordable and accessible food is important to Ajak. So, a plate of nasi padang can be priced as low as RM9.90. The uncompromised value the company offers in terms of price point and flavour has become Bumbu Babah’s unique selling point, he says. “At this time, we understand the current economic situation. If we look at the customers now, they value the experience of eating in restaurants more, they like good food, but they’re quite sensitive to price,” says Ajak. To accelerate its next stage of growth, BBV will launch an equity crowdfunding (ECF) campaign on pitchIN to attract institutional investors with its numbers, create a fundraising exercise with customer engagement and possibly look at fast-tracking to an initial public offering (IPO) by 2028 at the earliest. On the ECF platform itself, the company aims to raise between RM5 million and RM20 million, with shares issued at RM10 each. BBV plans to allocate 40% of the funds from the ECF campaign to acquiring its top-performing licensed outlets. Two activities, the setting up of corporate-owned outlets in malls and supporting the rollout of the new concept, will be allocated 25% each, while the final 10% will go to enhancing technology and its working capital. Behind the quick expansion The business has been able to expand quickly because its licensees have shown interest in opening more outlets. “We call it a licensed-and-managed concept because we are very mindful that we don’t want licensees or franchisees to run the outlets their own way and steer away from the standard operating procedures (SOPs). So, we came up with a structure where they provide the funding and become a passive investor in the outlet,” says BBV corporate finance manager Chan Eu-Jinn. This is how the system works: the licensee fully owns the outlet, but BBV continues to run it as if it belonged to the company. BBV also charges a management fee based on a percentage of the licensed outlet’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) on a monthly basis. “If the outlet is not profitable, we do not charge the management fee, so we have to ensure that it is run properly,” he notes. There are currently seven corporate-owned Bumbu Babah outlets. The remaining outlets are owned by licensees. BBV aims to continue expanding, but with a strategy centred more on mall outlets. “Our MyTown, Melawati Mall and IOI City Mall outlets are doing well, but we are still not in a lot of the major malls in the market yet. With the funds raised, we can then invest in this,” says Chan. BBV acknowledges that F&B brands have a tendency to overexpand, and Chan says the company has addressed this by setting a target number of outlets for Bumbu Babah restaurants so as to retain operational quality. “When we hit our target number [we may look more into] maintenance, but we will not be growing for the sake of opening and then cannibalising ourselves.” Bumbu Babah was also able to grow quickly with the introduction of a centralised kitchen to ensure the quality of the food across its licensed outlets remains consistent. Chan says the curry, sambal, proteins and sides are prepared in advance and sent straight to the outlets. This contributes to the efficiency of its operations, as the staff are able to run the basic equipment at the outlets by following the SOPs. Ajak plans to develop more offerings beyond Bumbu Babah’s nasi padang menu. Reflecting this resolve is BBV’s recent collaboration with local music group KRU to open a fine-casual-dining restaurant called KRU Cafe. “We will also have stalls where we will have food menus that include Chinese and Indian food. This is one of the projects that we will implement in time to come, and I think this is one of the reasons why Bumbu Babah will continue to grow in the F&B industry for many more years,” he says. On solid operational and financial ground Based on its audited financial statements, BBV is in a strong financial position. The company has four income streams: retail sales at corporate-owned outlets, central kitchen supplies, monthly management fees and turnkey outlet set-ups involving the building and selling of completed outlets to licensees. For its financial year 2025 (FY2025) ended on Dec 31, the parent company made RM10.4 million in revenue, while the consolidated group revenue came up to RM25.9 million. As for net profit, the parent company recorded RM2.5 million, while the group registered RM3.2 million. This gives the group a net profit margin of 12.5%, which Tradeview Capital research analyst Tan Jia Hui says sits at the higher end of the F&B industry norm of 5% to 12%. “The normalised margin is more likely to settle at around 10% in the upcoming years, given the margin mix [of all four income streams],” she adds. The margin is also anchored by a low marketing spend of roughly 1.3% of its revenue due to the marketing pull of Ajak. The group’s FY2025 earnings quality can be considered clean with only RM24,000 coming from one other source of income, which is the interest from its fixed deposits. Tan notes that liquidity was BBV’s clearest improvement in FY2025, with the current ratio moving from 0.21 times to 1.71 times and the quick ratio from 0.20 times to 1.70 times. Working capital swung from -RM560,000 to RM1.52 million, while its return on assets rose sharply from 6.6% to 74%. The company has also fully repaid shareholder advances in FY2025, leaving the group free of debt or borrowings. “In FY2024, the business leaned on RM600,000 of shareholder and director advances and stretched trade payables to fund itself, so its total liabilities-to-equity ratio stood at 13.9 times. In FY2025, those advances were repaid, so there are no borrowings and no non-current liabilities. The group holds net cash of RM1.47 million, taking the liabilities-to-equity ratio down to 0.97 times,” he says. Gordon Low, founder and managing partner of management consulting firm PiValue Strategy, agrees with Tan. He notes that the company’s financial improvements are backed by positive cash flow rather than being just profit on paper. “This is a company entering its next fundraising round from a position of real financial substance, which is a reasonable and encouraging starting point for the growth questions that follow,” he says. On the operational aspects, Low sees that BBV is signalling a strong early product market fit, although the goals set alongside its projected pace of growth may pose a challenge if not met with a grounded strategy. The affordability and everyday-meal positioning allow Bumbu Babah’s nasi padang to be embedded in local eating habits and food that consumers can enjoy regularly. “This naturally supports higher purchase frequency and repeat sales than non-local or occasion-based cuisines,” he says. Zooming in on the numbers Supported by its milestones, such as the record for selling the highest number of nasi padang servings sold in a day (23,674 plates), the business’ traction is generated by genuine consumer acceptance rather than hype alone, says Low. However, to maintain a returning customer base amid the competitive F&B space, the company must be able to align its marketing and promotional activities with its forecast growth. BBV’s projections show its system-wide revenue jumping to RM102 million in FY2026 from RM50 million in FY2025, with a forecast of 80 outlets. It also expects the figure to rise to RM232.4 million in FY2027. Low says this implies a growth of roughly 104% in FY2026, then a further 128% jump in FY2027. He notes that reaching the FY2027 target would require the group to double its footprint again in a single year. “Using the FY2026 target of 80 outlets as a base, a rough per-outlet run rate of around RM1.3 million suggests BBV would need somewhere in the region of 150 to 180 outlets to support the 2027 projected figure at a similar productivity level,” he says. “This indicates nearly doubling the outlet count again within a single year, an even faster pace than the 50 to 80 outlets planned for 2026. Tan cautions investors that BBV is materially smaller than the entire system. The audited FY2025 group revenue of RM25.9 million is roughly half the cited system-wide revenue of RM50 million because licensed outlets only contribute to the group through management fees and supply payments, rather than their full retail turnover. This means a huge chunk of the RM50 million earned by its network of 52 stores belongs to the individual licensed store owners rather than the company issuing the shares. The group revenue of RM25.9 million reflects the actual audited revenue recorded on the parent company’s books, which is the pool of money that generates profit for shareholders. Also seen in the financial statements is the parent company’s operating profit for FY2025, which appears to be cushioned from non-operational income. “The parent company’s profit after tax of RM2.5 million is flattered by RM1.5 million of intra-group dividends and a RM280,000 disposal gain. Strip out both and the standalone operating profit is closer to RM900,000,” says Tan. Put simply, intra-group dividends are distributions of profit paid by a subsidiary company to its parent company or another related entity in the same corporate group. Chan offers an explanation for the disposal gain, saying that BBV began reorganising its activities into two new subsidiaries established in the second quarter of FY2025. The subsidiaries are BBV Restaurants Sdn Bhd (BBVR), which handles store management, and BBV Trading Sdn Bhd, which is in charge of supply, trading and store set-up. This internal restructuring led to a transfer of assets and businesses related to the Melawati Mall and TF Value outlets from BBV to BBVR, and created a one-time gain on disposal on BBV’s standalone financial statements. “These dividends are eliminated upon consolidation because they represent intercompany transactions between entities of the same group. title: 'Smoky Singapore gears up to talk money ahead of F1
body:
'

SINGAPORE (Oct 5): Regional, business, cryptocurrency and sports leaders are meeting in Singapore for a slew of finance-focused conferences ahead of this weekend's Grand Prix as haze continues to shroud the city state.

Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, famed investor Ray Dalio and Eric Trump, a co-founder of the family-backed cryptocurrency business, are expected, while hundreds of thousands of Formula One (F1) fans will converge on the island.

The night race through the city streets and some 40 sideline events are typically a global showcase for Singapore and hotel room rates have soared.

The Fullerton Bay Hotel next to the race track is charging S$5,030 (US$3,933 or RM16,054) a night for a room that typically costs US$1,460.

This year, the pall from Indonesia's most intense fires in more than a decade will probably form part of the backdrop. Air quality was forecast at the "high moderate to low unhealthy" range on Monday by Singapore's environment agency. No longer-range forecast was provided for Sunday's Grand Prix.

Singapore's tourism board said F1 and its surrounding events had "strong momentum" reflecting confidence despite economic and geopolitical uncertainty.

Jitters in financial markets where bond prices are slumping and sentiment around artificial intelligence is shifting from euphoric to cautious will occupy investors and business chiefs at the Forbes Global CEO Conference and Milken Asia Summit, which runs from Wednesday.

Trump, a co-founder of crypto venture World Liberty Financial, is due to speak at the TOKEN2049 cryptocurrency event with digital asset markets fragile following a bruising 12 months.

A hoped-for regulatory framework failed last month to clear the US Senate, in part as President Donald Trump's personal crypto dealings ​became a flashpoint for Democrats.

Despite a recent bounce, the total value of the cryptocurrency market is down about a quarter over the last 12 months to US$3 trillion, according to data aggregator CoinGecko.

Still, organisers say their event is nearly sold out with 25,000 attendees expected, the same as last year. The Straits Times reported that about 90,000 "c-suite", or top-ranking, executives will be in town.

F1 generates around S$145 million in incremental tourism receipts for Singapore each year, according to official estimates. Maybank economist Chua Hak Bin expects it to hit S$160 million this year, along with "wider economic benefits" from deals struck at sideline events.

title: 'High Court to rule Oct 23 on Maritime Network’s bid to keep RHB accounts open
body:
'

KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court here today fixed Oct 23 to rule on a shipping company’s bid to restrain RHB Bank Berhad from closing two of its long-standing accounts, pending the disposal of its full suit.

Judicial Commissioner Elesabet Paya Wan set the date after hearing submissions from P. Taneswaran, acting for Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, and the bank’s counsel, Gan Khong Aik.

Taneswaran submitted that the bank had failed to establish any breach of terms or requirements by the plaintiff, Maritime Network, that would justify closing its accounts.

He further argued that the bank owed Maritime Network both a fiduciary duty and a duty of care.

Gan countered that no fiduciary relationship or duty of care arose between the bank and the shipping company, submitting that the relationship between a bank and its customer was that of debtor and creditor.

In October last year, the High Court granted a temporary injunction restraining RHB from closing the two long-standing accounts, pending the hearing of the company’s application for a full injunction.

According to court documents, the company has held a multi-currency account and a current account with RHB since 2005.

On Oct 6, 2025, it received a termination notice dated Oct 1, 2025, stating that the bank intended to close both accounts and terminate all related services within 14 days, citing breaches of its internal policies and guidelines.

The company, however, claimed that RHB had failed to specify which policies or guidelines had allegedly been breached.

The plaintiff said an ongoing dispute over the accounts had earlier led to its pre-trial discovery application being dismissed by the High Court on July 2, 2025.

The company subsequently appealed to the Court of Appeal, which in December last year allowed its appeal against the dismissal of the pre-trial discovery application.

The appellate court then ordered RHB to produce its Minimum Due Diligence guidelines governing foreign exchange transactions to the company within 45 days.

Maritime Network further alleged that the bank’s vague allegations placed it in a position of uncertainty, depriving it of any opportunity to defend itself.

The company asserted that this conduct amounted to an abuse of power that prejudiced its rights.

It also claimed that the bank’s conduct demonstrated an intention to oppress rather than protect its legitimate banking interests.

title: 'Maybank, Asian Banking School Collaborate to Raise Wealth Advisory Standards in Malaysia | Maybank
body: 'Maybank to serve as Founding Industry Partner in developing an industry-recognised certification for wealth advisory professionals Maybank and the Asian Banking School (ABS) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to explore the development of a professional certification framework for wealth advisory in Malaysia, aimed at introducing an industry-recognised benchmark for advisory capability. The proposed certification framework, to be known as the ABS Wealth Advisory & Management Certification Programme, is intended to establish competency standards specifically for wealth advisory professionals in banking. Upon its launch, it will be Malaysia’s first industry-wide professional certification framework dedicated to wealth advisory. As wealth management needs grow more complex, clients increasingly require advice that connects different aspects of their financial lives. This initiative therefore aims to establish a consistent benchmark for the advisory capabilities required to serve clients holistically. Maybank will serve as the Founding Industry Partner, contributing insights and its experience in developing wealth talent, while ABS will bring its expertise in professional banking development and certification. ABS will retain independence over the standards and how they are assessed and certified. “Maybank has continuously invested in developing our wealth professionals through Maybank Wealth Academy, building advisory capabilities that complement technical expertise and enable a holistic approach that meets the financial needs of clients. This collaboration with the Asian Banking School allows us to contribute that experience beyond our organisation, to raise professional standards for wealth advisory in Malaysia, with the opportunity to extend elements of the programme across the region over time,” said Syed Ahmad Taufik Albar, Group CEO, Community Financial Services, Maybank. “Malaysia has an opportunity to further develop wealth advisory as a profession through independent and industry-relevant standards. By combining ABS’s expertise in professional banking development with Maybank’s practitioner experience as Founding Industry Partner, we aim to create a credible pathway that gives wealth professionals a clearer benchmark as they progress in their careers while raising the quality of wealth advisory across Malaysia,” said Professor Dr. Manivanan Saman, Chief Executive Officer, Asian Banking School. (L-R) Prof. Dr. Manivanan Saman, CEO of Asian Banking School & Syed Ahmad Taufik Albar, Group CEO, Community Financial Services, Maybank The programme’s first intake is expected in the second half of 2027, and Maybank intends to incorporate the programme into Maybank Wealth Academy, connecting it with structured learning and career development through practical workplace application. The parties will also explore opportunities to extend relevant certification pathways to wealth professionals across the region. This initiative builds on the Bank’s established wealth management franchise, which was named Malaysia’s Best Private Bank 2026 by Euromoney, and recognised as the Best Wealth Management Bank in Malaysia by Alpha Southeast Asia for the 10th consecutive year.

title: 'Maybank fully acquires Etiqa’s holding company
body: 'Maybank fully acquires Etiqa’s holding company KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 11): Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK) has bought the remaining 30.95% interest in Maybank Ageas Holdings Bhd, making it a wholly-owned subsidiary of the bank. Maybank signed the share purchase agreement with Ageas Insurance International NV on Sept 8. Maybank Ageas is the holding company for Malaysian and Singaporean life and general insurance and takaful company Etiqa. “With MAHB (Maybank Ageas Holdings Bhd) being a wholly owned subsidiary of Maybank, it strengthens Etiqa’s position as a national insurance and takaful companion, driving deeper penetration of Maybank’s customer base,” said president and group CEO of Maybank Datuk Khairussaleh Ramli in a statement on Friday. This agreement comes after 25 years of partnership with Ageas. Moving forward, Maybank intends to expand Etiqa’s footprint across Southeast Asia, leveraging Maybank’s customer base. Khairussaleh added that, following this purchase, Maybank will push for faster product innovation, expand takaful propositions and enhance operational efficiency across the group. Maybank’s shares fell by 0.2% to RM10.44 per share on Friday, with a market capitalisation of RM126.3 billion. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: '57,000 migrants at risk: Time to end whipping in Malaysia
body: 'Malaysians Against Death Penalty and Torture (Madpet) calls for the abolition of whipping, a form of corporal punishment that is inherently cruel, inhumane and degrading and often amounts to torture. In Malaysia, it has even caused death. Physical trauma Judicial whipping, commonly known as caning in Malaysia, is carried out using a heavy rattan cane on a prisoner’s bare buttocks under strict legal and medical supervision. The offender is stripped and made to lean forward against a specialised wooden or padded frame, with their hands and legs securely shackled. Comparatively, Sharia caning is a lighter, symbolic or non-scarring form of corporal punishment focused on religious deterrence and public repentance rather than severe physical trauma. The offender is typically clothed. In many cases, the person being whipped faints after several strokes. It can also result in death, as happened in the case of Zaidi Abd Hamid, who passed away on 7 October 2025 in Pokok Sena prison at the age of 49 after receiving a sentence of 12 strokes of the cane (whipping). An investigation by the Malaysian human rights commission Suhakam confirmed that before he died, Zaidi’s whipping wounds became infected, and he did not receive proper medical care. It is sad that Zaidi, whose death penalty was recently commuted, ultimately died after receiving his alternative sentence of whipping. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Towards abolition of whipping We appreciate that Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s Pakatan Harapan government is still actively considering the abolition of whipping in Malaysia. On mandatory caning, Kulasegaran, the deputy law and institutional reform minister, said the issue was still under consultation following a recent meeting he chaired on a study into its impact and effectiveness in Malaysia. He said discussions with the Attorney General’s Chambers and other relevant parties were ongoing. It must be noted that, since the Immigration Act was amended in August 2002 to include whipping as a sentence for those found to be in Malaysia without proper documents, the majority of those being whipped are undocumented foreigners. This may also sadly have included refugees, asylum seekers and human trafficking victims. For the offence of illegally being in Malaysia, section 6(3) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 states: Any person who contravenes subsection (1) shall be guilty of an offence and shall, on conviction, be liable to a fine not exceeding ten thousand ringgit or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years or to both, and shall also be liable to whipping of not more than six strokes. According to Prisons Department records, 47,914 foreigners were found to have violated the Immigration Act from 2002 to 2008. Of these, 34,923 were caned or whipped. There are no current records provided by the government, but it is estimated that about 5,000 to 10,000 are still being whipped in Malaysia annually. Media reports prove that whipping has failed to deter illegal presence in Malaysia. The Immigration Department recently disclosed that in 2026 alone, a total of 57,161 undocumented migrants were detained in various enforcement operations nationwide between 1 January and 13 September. Does this mean that whipping has failed as a deterrent? It also means that about 50,000 new foreigners are at risk of being whipped. Wrongfully convicted? One case of a person being wrongfully convicted and whipped was Sabri Umar, an Indonesian migrant worker with valid documentation. He was convicted and whipped despite a pending appeal. Malaysian law explicitly prohibits whipping if there is a pending appeal. Here the error was also made by the Immigration Department, which provided wrong documents, claiming it had no record of entry, although Sabri had been a documented migrant worker for many years, as also reflected in his passport. In Sabri’s case, thankfully, High Court judge Justice Lim Hock Leng, on becoming aware of this injustice, called up his case for revision and acquitted Sabri Umar in 2022. Sabri’s gross miscarriage of justice came to light because his trade union and civil society groups raised it, and the media covered it. How many other foreign workers would have ended up being whipped wrongly in similar situations? Human trafficking victims? Foreigners who are victims of human trafficking cannot be charged for the crime of illegally being in Malaysia. Did the prosecution or the courts even take this into consideration? Did they confirm that the accused is not a victim of human trafficking or do they simply not bother – and convict and sentence them to be whipped? Section 25 of the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 (Atipsom), which deals with immunity from criminal prosecution, states: A trafficked person shall not be liable to criminal prosecution in respect of: (a) his illegal entry into the receiving country or transit country; (b) his period of unlawful residence in the receiving country or transit country; or (c) his procurement or possession of any fraudulent travel or identity document which he obtained, or with which he was supplied, for the purpose of entering the receiving country or transit country, where such acts are the direct consequence of an act of trafficking in persons that is alleged to have been committed or was committed. We wonder how many victims of human trafficking have been wrongly charged and sentenced to whipping. Repeal section 6(4) Now, section 6(4) of the Immigration Act states: The burden of proof that a person entered Malaysia without contravening subsection (1) shall lie upon that person, and in any prosecution for an offence under subsection (1), it shall not be necessary to specify in the charge the date, time, place or manner of the entry of such person into Malaysia, or by means of travel used for such entry, and such prosecution may be held at any place in Malaysia. But all these details are most important in determining whether he or she is a victim of human trafficking, or even a refugee/asylum seeker. This Section 6(4) is a bad law that must be repealed if Malaysia wants, by law, to ensure that no victim of human trafficking is ever charged with the offence of being illegally in Malaysia, which would cause them to suffer whipping. Malaysian law says that a victim of human trafficking cannot be criminally liable for illegally being in Malaysia where his or her presence in Malaysia is “the direct consequence of an act of trafficking in persons”. It is rightly for the prosecution or the courts to determine whether any accused is a victim of human trafficking and thus cannot be criminally liable under section 25 of Atipsom. It is unjust and wrong to push the burden onto foreigners who generally are not literate in the local languages or in Malaysian law. It is unacceptable and invites injustice. It is most important for the prosecution or the courts to determine how the foreigner came to be in Malaysia. Was it due to deception, etc? If the foreigner was once a registered migrant worker, suspicion should naturally arise over why he or she is still in Malaysia, since our law places the burden on employers to send them back to their country of origin. If the worker is still here because he or she has been cheated of the wages promised, then reasonably he or she is also a victim of human trafficking, as ‘trafficking in persons’ means all actions of recruiting, conveying, transferring, acquiring, maintaining, harbouring, providing or receiving, a person, for the purpose of exploitation. Thus, workers brought to Malaysia on a promise of work and certain wages, who then end up with different jobs and wages, are clearly victims of human trafficking. The same applies to workers whom employers still have not paid the wages and money due. Refugees and asylum seekers On 1 January 2026, Malaysia started its own asylum seeker and refugee assessment and recognition programme through the refugee registration document programme. But it is moving too slowly, as the number of refugees and asylum seekers, based on the UN refugee agency and others, may be over 300,000. “Until June 2026, 128 Myanmar nationals of Rohingya ethnicity, comprising 127 adult men and one adult woman, were transferred to PPKPPS (a special detention centre for refugees and asylum seekers) Bidor, Perak,” Home Minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said. “Following the status determination process, 78 individuals comprising 77 men and one woman have been approved as refugees under the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) programme. The release process will only be carried out after all related procedures have been completed.” Based on the principle of non-refoulement (not forcing people back to a country where they face danger), refugees and asylum seekers cannot be deported back to their country of origin. These refugees and asylum seekers also cannot be held in detention for being illegally in Malaysia. Reasonably, they cannot also be convicted for the crime of illegally being in Malaysia, as a conviction also may result in a sentence of whipping. Therefore, whipping must be abolished now, and, pending abolition, the Malaysian government must impose a moratorium on whipping. Even documented migrants can be wrongfully whipped because of the fault or negligence of the authorities, the prosecution and the courts, as happened in Sabri Umar’s case. Gross injustice can also be suffered by victims of human trafficking because of the failure of the prosecution or the courts to consider whether section 25 of Atipsom will be violated. Likewise, refugees and asylum seekers may also end up being wrongly whipped. In Malaysia this year alone, 57,161 undocumented migrants were detained in various enforcement operations nationwide between 1 January and 13 September. This means most of these 57,000 are at serious risk of being convicted and whipped. This alone makes the abolition of whipping a priority that needs urgent action by the Malaysian government. As such, Madpet calls for the immediate abolition of whipping and, pending abolition, a moratorium on whipping to avoid the innocent, including victims of human trafficking and refugees or asylum seekers, from being wrongly and unjustly whipped. Madpet calls for the repeal of section 6(4) of the Immigration Act, which now removes the onus or duty of the prosecution or the courts to determine whether the foreign national is a victim of human trafficking or not, or whether he or she is a refugee or asylum seeker who also should not be criminally liable for illegally being in Malaysia. Madpet also reiterates its call for Malaysia to ratify the UN Convention against Torture and Other Cruel, Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment. – Madpet Charles Hector issued this statement on behalf of Malaysians Against Death Penalty and Torture (Madpet). title: 'Bursa Malaysia Opens Higher Amid Easing US Treasury Yields
body: 'Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia saw a marginal increase at the opening on Friday, buoyed by the easing of US Treasury yields and a tempered tone from the Federal Reserve, which brought some relief to the market sentiment. According to BERNAMA News Agency, at 9.10 am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose by 1.49 points, or 0.09 per cent, to reach 1,631.85, up from Thursday's close of 1,630.36. The index had initially opened 3.51 points higher at 1,633.87. Across the broader market, gainers surpassed losers with 239 counters rising compared to 137 declining, while 270 counters remained unchanged, 2,127 were untraded, and 24 were suspended. The turnover was reported at 173.94 million shares valued at RM95.98 million. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd's vice-president of equity research, Thong Pak Leng, noted that the index's recent decline had pushed it into oversold territory, inviting bargain hunting after a sharp correction. Despite foreign selling pressures, Thong suggested any initial rebound might be modest but highlighted opportunities to selectively accumulate fundamentally sound stocks, particularly in established banks, utilities, and semiconductor sectors. Thong also mentioned that sustained recovery would require stronger participation from heavyweight counters and broader market improvement. He expected trading to remain cautious within the 1,625-1,640 range. In the heavyweight category, Maybank remained unchanged at RM9.95, while Public Bank and CIMB each fell by one sen to RM4.66 and RM7.68, respectively. Tenaga Nasional rose by four sen to RM12.94, and IHH Healthcare gained one sen to RM7.71. Among the active counters, Zetrix AI, Jaks Resources, and Genetec remained unchanged, while V.S Industry rose by one sen to 28 sen, and Kinergy Advancement dropped by half a sen to 39.5 sen. Top gainers included Malaysian Pacific Industries, which advanced by 58 sen to RM41.70, Hengyuan Refining, which increased by 19 sen to RM3.83, and Petronas Chemicals, which climbed by 15 sen to RM4.28. UWC and MI Technovation each firmed by 10 sen to RM7.20 and RM5.36, respectively. MISC led the decliners, falling by 14 sen to RM7.54, with LPI Capital, Hong Leong Industries, MNRB, and RHB Bank each shedding four sen to RM12.80, RM16.10, RM2.78, and RM7.43, respectively. Regarding index performance, the FBM Mid 70 Index rose by 75.93 points to 17,434.91, the FBM Emas Index increased by 17.18 points to 12,160.71, and the FBM Top 100 Index gained 21.58 points to 11,954.73. The FBM Emas Shariah Index accumulated 34.76 points to 12,047.77, while the FBM ACE Index improved by 18.61 points to 5,501.58. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index grew by 1.10 points to 178.83, and the Energy Index increased by 9.45 points to 844.46, while the Financial Services Index fell by 26.33 points to 19,034.58 and the Plantation Index ticked up by 2.75 points to 9,029.32.

title: 'Daily Newswatch - 23 Sep 2026
body: 'The FBM KLCI rallied 1.0% to 1,683.5 points on Tuesday, as strong buying in banking, semiconductor and technology stocks lifted the broader market in tandem with gains across regional markets. Technology (+2.3%), Utilities (+1.7%) and Financial Services (+1.3%) led sectoral gains, led by Hong Leong Bank (+0.5%), IHH Healthcare (+0.4%) and CIMB Group (+0.3%). Market breadth, however, was positive, with gainers outnumbering losers 678 to 458, and 572 counters unchanged. Asian markets closed mostly higher on Tuesday, supported by renewed optimism over the AI trade, easing oil prices and expectations of progress at the upcoming US-China summit. South Korea's KOSPI rose 0.2% to 7,017.9, followed by Hong Kong's Hang Seng (+0.2%) at 25,087.8, Taiwan's TAIEX (+0.2%) at 47,800.2 and China's Shanghai Composite (+0.1%) at 3,952.1, while Japan's Nikkei 225 was closed for a public holiday. In South Korea, semiconductor stocks led the regional gains as investors returned to AIlinked trades following the rally in US chipmakers and technology stocks, with strong September semiconductor exports further supporting expectations for sustained chip demand. In China, sentiment was supported by technology and AI-related stocks, while investors remained focused on the upcoming Trump-Xi meeting and the potential extension of the US-China trade truce. European stocks closed slightly higher on Tuesday, extending the previous session’s gains, supported by strength in technology and consumer staples. The Euro STOXX 50 rose 0.2% to 6,332, while the STOXX Europe 600 gained 0.3% to 643.6. AI-related stocks advanced alongside their US counterparts following positive sentiment around Meta’s Muse AI, boosting AI infrastructure and technology shares. Meanwhile, banks and insurers pared earlier gains as Eurozone sovereign yields and natural gas prices rose amid heightened tensions in the Middle East. US stocks closed mixed on Tuesday, with the Nasdaq reaching a record high on renewed optimism over AI and semiconductor stocks. The Nasdaq CI gained 0.5%, while the S&P 500 was essentially flat and the Dow Jones fell 0.4%. Technology stocks led gains, with Micron Technology rising 5.0% and Sandisk nearly 7.0%, supported by optimism over AI demand. Meanwhile, financial stocks weakened, with JPMorgan Chase and Wells Fargo falling more than 3%, as investors remained cautious over inflation and further rate hikes. Investors also monitored Middle East developments and the upcoming Trump-Xi meeting. US: Oil Falls for 6th Session Crude oil slipped below $90 per barrel on Wednesday, extending its decline to a sixth consecutive session as signs of progress emerged in renewed US-Iran talks and efforts continued to restore operations at a key pipeline in Saudi Arabia. President Donald Trump said officials held a “very productive” meeting with Iranian envoys, adding that he is weighing whether to pursue a negotiated agreement or “annihilate the Islamic Republic.” (Trading Economics) US: Fifth District Manufacturing Unexpectedly Declines Fifth District manufacturing activity edged down in September, according to the most recent survey from the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond. The composite manufacturing index dropped to −2 from 4 in August. Two of its three component indexes decreased in September: shipments to −5 from 11 and new orders to −6 from 3. Meanwhile, the employment index increased to 7 from −2. (Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond) US: Treasury Yields Edge Up to 4.97% on Tuesday The yield on the US 10-year Treasury wavered before settling slightly higher at 4.97% on Tuesday, as traders continued to assess developments in the Middle East, oil prices and comments from Fed officials. In his speech to the UN General Assembly, US President Trump defended his decision to join Israel in launching military action against Iran but added that he believes the US would reach a deal with Iran right after the midterm elections in November. (Trading Economics) US: Borrowing overshoots in fresh budget setback for Healey Britain borrowed more than forecast in the first five months of the fiscal year, piling fresh pressure on Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey ahead of his debut budget next month. The fiscal deficit climbed to £77.3 billion — £8.1 billion more than the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) predicted in March. In August alone, borrowing came in higher than forecast at £18.3 billion. The OBR had predicted a deficit of £14.8 billion. (Bloomberg) EU: ECB's Lane sees inflation returning to target from mid-2027 - paper An energy shock pushing up oil and gas prices is likely to last longer than the European Central Bank (ECB) had anticipated in March, with geopolitical risks now looking elevated again, ECB chief economist Philip Lane was quoted as saying on Tuesday. title: 'Pelabur asing jual RM1.6 bilion saham di Bursa Malaysia pada September 2026 - CGS International - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 6 Okt - Pelabur asing kekal sebagai penjual bersih ekuiti Malaysia pada September 2026 dengan aliran keluar bersih RM1.6 bilion, susut 17.1% berbanding RM2 bilion pada Ogos, menurut CGS International. Aktiviti dagangan kasar meningkat bagi kedua-dua belian dan jualan sepanjang bulan itu, namun pembelian asing meningkat lebih pantas sebanyak 12.1% bulan ke bulan kepada RM22.1 bilion berbanding kenaikan 9.5% dalam jualan kepada RM23.7 bilion. Bagaimanapun, tekanan jualan semakin meningkat menjelang akhir September apabila aliran keluar bersih terkumpul pelabur asing melebihi RM1 bilion antara 23 hingga 30 September. Peningkatan jualan pada penghujung bulan itu berlaku ketika Dewan Undangan Negeri Melaka dibubarkan. Perkembangan itu menjadikan jualan bersih terkumpul pelabur asing sebanyak RM6.5 bilion bagi sembilan bulan pertama 2026. Jumlah aliran keluar sejak 2024 pula mencecah RM33.1 bilion, manakala pegangan asing dalam ekuiti Malaysia susut ke satu lagi paras terendah baharu sebanyak 17.8% pada September. Pegangan asing susut kepada 17.8% Pelabur institusi tempatan turut mengambil pendekatan lebih berhati-hati pada September apabila pembelian bersih mereka merosot mendadak kepada RM206 juta daripada RM1.6 bilion pada bulan sebelumnya. Pelabur runcit tempatan pula meningkatkan pembelian bersih kepada RM1.4 bilion daripada RM375 juta pada Ogos, paras bulanan tertinggi sejak Januari 2025. FBM KLCI merosot 4.3% pada September untuk ditutup pada 1,651 mata, sekali gus menyebabkan prestasinya sejak awal tahun bertukar negatif. Prestasi itu lebih lemah berbanding Indeks MSCI All Country Asia ex-Japan yang susut 0.7% bulan ke bulan dan Indeks MSCI Emerging Markets yang turun 1%. Pasaran global secara keseluruhannya berdepan bulan yang mencabar, dengan hanya KOSPI Korea Selatan yang meningkat 0.7% dan Nikkei Jepun naik 0.5%. Dalam kalangan pasaran MIST iaitu Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapura dan Thailand, Straits Times Index Singapura mencatat prestasi terbaik dengan penurunan 0.4%, sekali gus menamatkan kenaikan selama lima bulan berturut-turut. Tenaga dan pembinaan mengatasi kelemahan pasaran SET Index Thailand pula susut 1.8% walaupun Fitch Ratings pada 18 September menyemak semula prospek negara itu kepada “stabil” daripada negatif, dengan menyatakan peningkatan keyakinan terhadap penstabilan hutang. FBM KLCI yang merosot 4.3% dan Jakarta Composite Index Indonesia yang jatuh 6.9% merupakan dua pasaran berprestasi paling lemah dalam kalangan negara MIST. Sentimen terhadap pasaran Indonesia merosot pada pertengahan bulan susulan kebimbangan fiskal selepas kemas kini belanjawan menunjukkan defisit sebanyak Rp240.1 trilion sehingga Ogos. Kelemahan turut berlaku secara meluas di Bursa Malaysia apabila hanya empat daripada 13 indeks sektor mencatat kenaikan pada September. 3 sektor berprestasi terbaik Tiga sektor berprestasi terbaik ialah tenaga yang meningkat 8.6%, pembinaan 7.1% dan utiliti 2.9%. Tiga sektor berprestasi paling lemah pula ialah hartanah yang susut 7.5%, pengguna 6.5% dan kewangan 5.1%. Kelemahan itu turut ketara dalam kalangan konstituen FBM KLCI apabila hanya lima daripada 30 saham mencatat kenaikan. Gamuda menjadi saham berprestasi terbaik dengan kenaikan 14.9%, diikuti Telekom Malaysia sebanyak 3.8% dan YTL Power sebanyak 2.8%. IOI Properties pula mencatat kejatuhan terbesar sebanyak 14.6%, diikuti Sunway yang susut 13.8% dan RHB Bank 13.6%. - DagangNews.com

title: 'Oct 23 ruling on bid to restrain RHB from closing Maritime Network's accounts
body:
'

KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 24): The High Court here on Thursday fixed Oct 23 to rule on a shipping company's bid to restrain RHB Bank Bhd (LK:RHBBANK) from closing two of its long-standing accounts, pending the disposal of its full suit.

Judicial Commissioner Elesabet Paya Wan set the date after hearing submissions from P Taneswaran, acting for Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, and the bank's counsel, Gan Khong Aik.

Taneswaran submitted that the bank had failed to establish any breach of terms or requirements by the plaintiff, Maritime Network, that would justify closing its accounts.

He further argued that the bank owed Maritime Network both a fiduciary duty and a duty of care.

Gan countered that no fiduciary relationship or duty of care arose between the bank and the shipping company, submitting that the relationship between a bank and its customer is that of debtor and creditor.

In October last year, the High Court granted a temporary injunction restraining RHB from closing the two long-standing accounts, pending the hearing of the company's application for a full injunction.

According to court documents, the company has held a multi-currency account and a current account with RHB since 2005.

On Oct 6, 2025, it received a termination notice dated Oct 1, 2025, stating that the bank intended to close both accounts and terminate all related services within 14 days, citing breaches of its internal policies and guidelines.

The company, however, claimed that RHB had failed to specify which policies or guidelines were allegedly breached.

The plaintiff said an ongoing dispute over the accounts had earlier led to its pre-trial discovery application being dismissed by the High Court on July 2, 2025.

The company subsequently appealed to the Court of Appeal, which in December last year allowed its appeal against the dismissal of the pre-trial discovery application.

The appellate court then ordered RHB to produce its minimum due diligence guidelines governing foreign-exchange transactions to the company within 45 days.

Maritime Network further alleged that the bank's vague allegations placed it in a position of uncertainty, depriving it of any opportunity to defend itself.

This conduct, the company asserted, amounted to an abuse of power that prejudiced its rights.

It also claimed that the bank's conduct demonstrated an intention to oppress rather than protect its legitimate banking interests.

title: 'Are Chinese Malaysian-owned SMEs being ‘killed’ by the China onslaught?
body: 'The Gut Shot Podcast is joined by its geopolitical and economic consultant to governments and companies, Jason Leong. Signals from the ground have now raised alarm among segments of the Chinese Malaysian community. Malaysia’s private sector economy is largely driven by local ethnic Chinese businesses. Unlike the ecosystem of government-linked firms and investment companies, the private sector economy has none of the protection that bumiputra monopolies and oligopolies enjoy. The retail, mechanic workshops, construction services and supply chains, food and beverage and other service businesses are not abstract figures on an economist’s spreadsheet. They are livelihoods that have survived for decades. They have employed workers, paid taxes, supported families and funded the education of the next generation. Now a wave of imported competition from China, at scaled-down and even cut-throat prices, has reached our shores with devastating effect. When businesses across very different sectors begin telling the same story at the same time (vanishing margins, slowing customers, rising costs, price competition that cannot be met and a daily struggle to survive), we should not dismiss it as a series of isolated failures or a lack of competitiveness. This podcast explores the damage to local ethnic Chinese-driven small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in both macro and micro terms, calmly and without sentiment and makes some policy recommendations. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member It examines why, however efficient our supply chains become, resistance on scale alone will be futile: massive state subsidies, fierce internal competition within China that no other country can replicate, and a capital structure built to chase market share at any cost. The official macro numbers may not have captured this yet. Perhaps no one has measured it properly or raised the alarm. But the signals are real. By the time everyone agrees there is a crisis, many of these businesses could already be gone. If we fail to recognise the systemic forces behind China’s global dominance and act accordingly, we may be witnessing the beginning of the end of the traditional, generations-old Chinese Malaysian SMEs ecosystem.
