title: 'AG cautions on use of AI, effective human oversight is still essential
body: 'AG cautions on use of AI, effective human oversight is still essential KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): While the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) has been used extensively and relied upon in the last few years, Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar cautioned for the need for human oversight in its usage. Dusuki said there is no doubt that AI offers significant opportunities in various sectors. For instance, he said, in healthcare, it can assist clinical judgement while in the corporate sphere, it can support decision-making, improve efficiency, and help professionals process increasingly complex information. “But as our reliance on these systems grows, so, too, does the importance of understanding how they are used and how they are governed. We need to ask some very practical questions: How reliable is the information produced by an AI system? What are the limits of its capabilities? Who is responsible for checking its output?” he said. He questioned what would happen when the AI system does not perform as expected. “These are not merely questions about technology. They are questions of governance, professional responsibility, and human oversight. Increasingly, they may also have consequences for legal liability and insurance. “For any institution adopting AI, it is therefore important to understand why the technology is being used, what risks may arise from its use, and what safeguards are necessary. Technology may assist professional judgement, but effective human oversight remains essential,” he reminded. Dusuki was delivering his keynote address at the Inaugural Financial Lines Forum at a hotel here. Also present were Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman and RHB Bank founder Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussin, who delivered a special address, and former Federal Court judge Tan Sri Zainun Ali, former Chief Judge of Malaya Tan Sri Hasnah Mohamed Hashim, as well as former and current judges. The AG said that while there are continuing issues in the usage of AI, there is a need to use it responsibly. Dusuki said the use of AI requires engagement among those who develop the technology, those who deploy it, those who rely on it, and those who assess and manage the risks associated with its use. Hence, he welcomed the organisation of such a forum like the Financial Lines Forum as it brings together legal professionals, healthcare practitioners, corporate leaders, insurers, brokers, and other stakeholders. “We have an opportunity to learn from one another, to better understand the risks and opportunities before us, and to consider how our respective professions can respond responsibly to a rapidly changing environment. “Ultimately, the question is not simply what artificial intelligence can do. The more important question is, how we, as professionals, choose to use it responsibly,” he added. The one-day forum gathers medical experts, insurers, lawyers, and judges in exchanging views on medical negligence, governance, and AI. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: 'Maybank Gets BNM Approval for RM4.83 Billion Ageas Deal
body: 'Maybank is moving ahead with its RM4.83 billion Ageas deal after securing Bank Negara Malaysia’s approval. The bank signed an unconditional agreement on 8 September to acquire Ageas Insurance International’s remaining 30.95% stake in Maybank Ageas Holdings. Maybank will carry out the acquisition through its wholly owned subsidiary Etiqa International Holdings, which currently owns 69.05% of the company. The deal will give the bank full control of Etiqa’s insurance and takaful businesses in Malaysia and Singapore. BNM granted the required approvals on 1 September. The Monetary Authority of Singapore had approved the transaction in March. Maybank will fund the purchase entirely through internally generated funds. It will also pay Ageas a RM34.17 million fee accrued from 1 August until the targeted completion date. Maybank Ageas Holdings will distribute a RM799.99 million dividend to its existing shareholders upon completion. Etiqa International Holdings will receive RM552.38 million, while Ageas will receive RM247.61 million. The bank expects the acquisition to support its regional expansion and allow closer integration between its banking and insurance services. The deal does not require approval from Maybank shareholders and is expected to be completed on 11 September 2026. title: 'Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera maintains five sen per unit income distribution for year ended September
body: 'Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera maintains five sen per unit income distribution for year ended September KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) has maintained its income distribution at five sen per unit for the financial year ended Sept 30, 2026 (FY2026), benefitting over 82,000 unitholders. Pelaburan Hartanah Bhd (PHB), together with its fund manager, PHB Asset Management Bhd (PHBAM), said the final income distribution for the six months ended Sept 30, 2026, comprises 2.1 sen per unit, with an additional bonus distribution of 0.4 sen per unit declared by PHB as the fund's sponsor. "The bonus distribution will be applied to the first 1,000,000 units held by each unitholder. Including the interim income distribution of 2.5 sen per unit declared in April 2026, AHB’s total income distribution for the financial year ended FY2026 amounts to five sen per unit," the statement said. PHB said RM120.13 million will be distributed in the final round, bringing the total annual payout to RM236.41 million. PHB group managing director Mazuki Abdullah @ Muhammad said the full-year income distribution reflects AHB’s continued resilience and the strength of its underlying property portfolio, supported by PHB’s disciplined approach to asset and investment management. “AHB’s performance this year reaffirms our commitment to delivering competitive returns to our unitholders. At the same time, we remain focused on strengthening AHB as an investment avenue for Bumiputera investors through prudent capital management, active portfolio optimisation and strategic growth," he said. Meanwhile, PHBAM chief executive officer Zulkifli Ishak said the fund manager remains focused on managing AHB responsibly while ensuring the fund continues to serve as an accessible investment option for Bumiputera investors. PHB said income distribution will be paid in the form of AHB units, credited directly into unitholders' AHB accounts by Oct 13, 2026 and automatically reinvested, allowing unitholders to increase their unit holdings and potentially benefit from the long-term compounding effect. "Bumiputera investors who wish to subscribe to AHB may do so at a fixed price of RM1 per unit, with a minimum investment of RM100 and a maximum of RM1 million. "Subscriptions are available through the respective branches of authorised distributors nationwide, namely Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), AmBank Bhd, AmBank Islamic Bhd, Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd, and Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia Bhd," it said. title: 'Bursa Malaysia Midday Losses Continue Amid Selling Pressure
body: 'Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia extended its downtrend at midday, influenced by selling pressure and a mixed global market performance, as risk sentiment remained restrained by the continuous rise in United States Treasury yields. According to BERNAMA News Agency, at 12.30 pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) dropped 15.36 points to 1,635.81 from the previous day's close of 1,651.17. The benchmark index opened 1.30 points lower at 1,649.87 and ranged between 1,634.39 and 1,649.87 during the morning session. On the broader market, decliners outnumbered gainers by 583 to 305, with 464 counters unchanged, 1,421 untraded, and 12 suspended. The turnover was 1.65 billion shares worth RM1.18 billion. Apex Securities Bhd noted that market sentiment was further dampened by stronger-than-expected US private-sector hiring, which increased by 90,000 in September. This situation offset the relief from softer core Personal Consumption Expenditures inflation. Investors are now looking towards the upcoming September non-farm payrolls for guidance on the US Federal Reserve's next steps, while stalled US-Iran negotiations keep oil prices volatile, and mainland Chinese markets remain closed for the Golden Week holiday. The stockbroking firm anticipates that the FBM KLCI will trade cautiously ahead of the US jobs data report, with a more sustained recovery contingent on a pullback in US bond yields and progress in US-Iran talks. Among the heavyweights, Maybank and Tenaga Nasional both decreased by six sen to RM9.93 and RM12.90, respectively. Public Bank lost four sen to RM4.66, CIMB fell five sen to RM7.74, and IHH Healthcare declined 19 sen to RM7.64. In active trading, Zetrix AI and V.S Industry both rose half a sen to 16.5 sen and 28.5 sen, respectively. Jaks Resources decreased half a sen to 20 sen, ACE Market debutant GB Bond fell 2.5 sen to 22.5 sen, and Dagang Nexchange increased 1.5 sen to 50 sen. Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries advanced RM1.26 to RM41.66, MI Technovation rose 13 sen to RM5.33, Ta Ann gained 12 sen to RM5.92, Malayan Cement increased 11 sen to RM5.56, and Genting Plantations improved 10 sen to RM5.63. Kuala Lumpur Kepong led the decliners, dropping 76 sen to RM21.44. Allianz Malaysia shed 62 sen to RM21, while Fraser and Neave, Hong Leong Industries, and Batu Kawan all fell 42 sen to RM21.32, RM16.04, and RM20.10, respectively. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index fell 87.65 points to 17,487.02, the FBM Emas Index declined 94.18 points to 12,197.83, and the FBM Top 100 Index lost 99.00 points to 11,985.44. The FBM Emas Shariah Index weakened 87.69 points to 12,088.65, while the FBM ACE Index contracted 31.14 points to 5,503.14. In sectoral performance, the Industrial Products and Services Index slipped 1.16 points to 178.80, the Energy Index eased 7.79 points to 837.91, the Financial Services Index fell 148.77 points to 19,067.72, and the Plantation Index retreated 121.85 points to 9,074.82.

title: 'Maybank Supports Digital Learning At SMK Santubong | Sarawak Tribune
body: 'KUCHING: SMK Santubong received four Smart TVs from Maybank Sarawak to support digital learning and enhance teaching and learning at the school. The contribution was made in conjunction with Maybank Group’s 14th Global Corporate Responsibility (CR) Day 2026 and Cahaya Kasih Challenge 2026-2027 programme held at the school today. Santubong Member of Parliament, Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri, said the initiative was in line with the changing needs of education, particularly as technology continued to play a greater role in learning. She said such support was especially important for schools located away from urban centres, where students could benefit from greater access to digital learning facilities. “This event is to ensure that students are able to gain the knowledge they need through education. Especially for schools far from the city, they really need education like this,” she said. Nancy emphasised that education remained a key priority as it could open pathways to employment, improve incomes, and help families build better lives. “Do not let your place of residence or family backgrounds become a barrier. I believe that with knowledge and continuous effort, all of you can achieve the aspirations you dream of,” she said. Nancy said the collaboration between Maybank and the Santubong parliamentary constituency was not new, with the bank having previously supported Pusat Aktiviti Kanak-Kanak (PAKK) Bandar Baru Samariang in 2024 and 2025. Maybank Sarawak’s Regional Director, Abang Jamili Abang Julai, said the initiative reflected the bank’s role in contributing to the community through education and knowledge-sharing. “This is our opportunity in the banking sector to contribute to the children in school. We hope to share our knowledge in financial literacy, business planning and digital technology to help the community,” he said. More than 60 Maybank employees from its regional office, branches and centres in Sarawak took part in the programme, which also featured sharing sessions on financial literacy and scam awareness. The initiative, guided by the theme ‘Impacting Society Positively: Enabling Well-being For All’, focuses on education, community empowerment and environmental sustainability.

title: 'Daily Newswatch - 22 Sep 2026
body: 'The FBM KLCI edged up 0.1% to 1,666.9 points on Monday, snapping a threesession losing streak, as bargain hunting in selected blue-chip counters lifted the index amid easing concerns over the West Asia conflict and retreating oil prices. Energy (+3.0%), Utilities (+1.9%) and Transportation & Logistics (+0.5%) led sectoral gains, led by Hong Leong Bank (+0.4%), YTL Power (+0.3%) and Petronas Dagangan (+0.2%). Market breadth, however, was positive, with gainers outnumbering losers 654 to 552, and 517 counters unchanged. Asian markets closed mostly higher on Monday, supported by renewed strength in technology and semiconductor stocks, easing oil prices and improved sentiment ahead of the upcoming US-China summit. South Korea's KOSPI led regional gains, rising 1.7%, followed by Hong Kong's Hang Seng (+1.2%), Taiwan's TAIEX (+1.1%) and China's Shanghai Composite (+1.0%), while Japan's Nikkei 225 was closed for a public holiday. In South Korea, chipmakers led the gains, with Samsung Electronics rising 5.0% after US semiconductor stocks rallied, while semiconductor exports surged 259% YoY to USD34.1 bn in the first 20 days of September, reinforcing expectations of strong chip demand and earnings. In China, sentiment was supported by gains in technology and healthcare stocks, while the PBOC maintained its key lending rates and investors awaited the Trump-Xi meeting. European stocks closed firmly higher on Monday, supported by lower sovereign yields and easing ongoing pressures from an adverse macroeconomic backdrop. The Euro STOXX 50 gained 1.3% to 6,318 and the STOXX Europe 600 rose 1.0% to 642. Natural gas and fuel prices pulled back following the weekend amid signs that GCC nations are chasing diplomatic ways with Iran to restart tanker flows through the Persian Gulf. The drop in yields aided the outlook of credit and supported banks, with UniCredit, Nordea, and BBVA adding between 3.2% and 2%. Lastly, a global rally for the AI infrastructure sector supported Infineon with a 4.3% jump, while ASML added 2.5%. US stocks rallied on Monday, supported by falling oil prices and lower Treasury yields, while optimism over the upcoming Trump-Xi summit further lifted sentiment. The Nasdaq CI surged 2.26%, while the S&P 500 and Dow gained 1.49% and 0.71%, respectively. Meta jumped 11.3% on optimism over its AI offering, Muse, while AMD and Intel surged 10% and 12.1%, respectively. Investors now await earnings from AutoZone and KB Home, along with speeches from Federal Reserve officials. US: Treasury Yields Edge Down 4.95% on Monday The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note fell 4bps to 4.95% on Monday, as traders started the new week with another decline in oil prices, amid hopes that diplomatic efforts could lead to a resolution to the conflict with Iran. Oil prices have now fallen for four consecutive sessions, easing some concerns over renewed inflationary pressures (Trading Economics) US: Gold Slips on Dollar Strength Gold prices edged lower toward $4,350 on Monday, pressured by a stronger US dollar and profit-taking after last week’s rally, while investors continued to monitor developments in the Middle East. Bullion reached its highest level in more than a week on Friday as falling oil prices eased concerns over prolonged inflationary pressures. Oil prices extended their decline at the start of the week as investors looked for signs of diplomatic progress on the Iran conflict around this week’s UN meetings, although tensions remained elevated as Iran and the US exchanged fresh threats on Sunday. (Trading Economics) US: Oil Holds Decline as Supply Concerns Ease Crude oil held below $96 per barrel on Tuesday after falling for four consecutive sessions, pressured by easing supply concerns in the Middle East and growing diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran war. President Donald Trump is scheduled to address the UN General Assembly in New York later today and could meet with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines. Trump is also expected to hold discussions with other Gulf nations and Chinese President Xi Jinping this week. (Trading Economics) US: AI adoption is driving hiring, but mostly for senior roles Companies using artificial intelligence are adding more jobs than those that are not but those gains sharply favour senior employees over junior workers, according to a new study spanning 41 countries. The number of employees in senior positions rose by 6.7% over five years at companies adopting AI while junior employment declined 3% in the same period, researchers Bharat Chandar of Stanford University and Bouke Klein Teeselink of King’s College London said in a paper released on Monday. (Bloomberg) US: Fed's Kashkari says inflation is still too high in 'all aspects' of US economy Minneapolis Federal Reserve president Neel Kashkari said on Sunday that inflation is too high across all sectors of the US economy, not just in rising oil prices. "So even if we strip out energy, which is really volatile, and strip out food — they matter a lot — but in terms of where the economy is going, inflation is still too high," Kashkari told Fox News' Sunday Morning Futures. (Reuters) US: Housing costs rise further out of reach ahead of mid-terms Barely six weeks out from the midterm elections, housing costs that many Americans have long said are too high are looking even more out of reach. The latest blow for consumers came Thursday, when Freddie Mac reported that rates for 30-year mortgages climbed to 6.95%, the highest since January 2025, when President Donald Trump returned to office. That report emerged after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in three years, crushing any hopes that borrowing costs will come down soon. (Bloomberg) US: New data centres worth US$68 billion disrupted in US, data show Opposition to data centres continues to mount in the US. title: 'Insider Moves: Cuscapi Bhd, Zetrix AI Bhd, Excel Force MSC Bhd, Formosa Prosonic Industries Bhd, MyMBN Bhd, RHB Bank Bhd, Gamuda Bhd
body:
'

This article first appeared in Capital, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 21, 2026 - September 27, 2026

Notable filings

During the week of Sept 7 to 11, notable changes in shareholding at Bursa Malaysia-listed companies included those at IT company Cuscapi Bhd (KL:CUSCAPI), where Datin Seri Lee Lan Moi and Jessie Lim Me Xian ceased to be substantial shareholders.

According to Bursa filings, Lee hived off 67.5 million shares or a 7.14% stake in an off-market deal, while Lim sold 58.5 million shares via a separate off-market transaction. Both transactions took place on Sept 3.

Separately, Cuscapi’s largest shareholder, Wong Thean Soon, saw his stake cut from 28.07% to 13.43%, as the share price tumbled from nine sen at end-August to close at six sen last Thursday, giving the company a market capitalisation of RM56.7 million.

Filings showed that the bulk of the shares Wong disposed of had been pledged, and were likely forced sold as the share price fell. There have also been a slew of boardroom changes at Cuscapi.

Following the transactions, Tan Boon Seng emerged as a substantial shareholder of Cuscapi after acquiring 100.33 million shares or a 10.62% stake on Sept 11. Wong had emerged as a substantial shareholder of Cuscapi in March 2022, with a 7.73% stake.

Apart from his shares in Cuscapi, Wong’s shares in his flagship Zetrix AI Bhd (KL:ZETRIX) and Excel Force MSC Bhd (KL:EFORCE) were also likely forced sold after their market prices plummeted.

During the week in review, Wong’s direct stake in Zetrix AI was slashed by 571.36 million shares to 525.27 million shares, or a 6.67% stake, while his indirect interest held via Asia Internet Holdings Sdn Bhd was substantially reduced after 632.05 million shares were sold, bringing the firm’s stake in Zetrix AI down to 5.56% or 438.17 million shares.

Wong now has 12.23% equity interest in Zetrix AI, in stark contrast to the 29.25% he held in early April this year. Meanwhile, his stake in Excel Force was reduced to 14.01% or 85.42 million shares after 104.21 million shares were disposed of.

At Formosa Prosonic Industries Bhd (KL:FPI), privately held OS Capital Sdn Bhd emerged as a substantial shareholder of the audio products manufacturer after acquiring 53.45 million shares or 20.01% equity interest on Sept 10. OS Capital is the vehicle of Gan Chun Hui, who also has a direct stake of 0.36% or 955,500 shares in Formosa Prosonic.

The shares acquired by Gan could have come from Taiwanese managing director Shih Chao Yuan, who sold 66.78 million shares or a 24.88% stake on Sept 10 and ceased to be a substantial shareholder. Another substantial shareholder of Formosa Prosonic, Singaporean Wu Swee Ngor, sold 44.18 million shares or a 16.46% stake in the company.

Formosa Prosonic’s share price closed at RM1.08 last Thursday, giving the company a market value of RM288.5 million.

Meanwhile, privately held Gentle Rainbow Sdn Bhd — the private vehicle of Fong Hew Chung and Hew Hong Thee — ceased to be a substantial shareholder of edible bird’s nest processor MyMBN Bhd (KL:MBN) after disposing of 28.8 million shares or a 7.46% stake in the company during the week in review.

While Fong ceased to be a substantial shareholder, Hew still has 129.6 million shares, or 33.58% equity interest, in MyMBN. Hew is the mother of Lavernt Chen Vun Wo, executive director and CEO of MyMBN.

In early September, MyMBN chairman Liw Chong Liong sold 43.2 million shares or an 11.19% stake in the company, halving his shareholding. It is not clear who acquired those shares.

From eight sen at end-June, MyMBN’s share price had doubled to 17 sen in the first week of September, before tapering off and finishing at 14.5 sen last Thursday, valuing the company at RM56 million.

Notable movements

Bursa filings during the week in review showed the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) accumulating shares in RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK). The provident fund acquired another 31.46 million shares to bring its equity interest to 35.47% or 1.55 billion shares. At end-June, it held 1.51 billion shares or a 34.54% stake in RHB.

RHB’s share price closed at a multi-year high of RM8.88 on Aug 10, having gained 11% since early April. However, it had since eased 12.05% from its high to close at RM7.81 last Thursday, giving the banking group a market capitalisation of RM34.09 billion.

Bourse filings also showed that EPF continued to accumulate Gamuda Bhd’s (KL:GAMUDA) shares and emerged as a net buyer during the week in review, having mopped up 20.92 million shares to bring its equity interest to 21.93% or 1.32 billion shares. In early July, the provident fund held a 20.83% stake or 1.24 billion shares in the construction giant.

Gamuda’s share price closed at RM4.74 last Thursday, having gained about 17% since early July.  This gave the group a market capitalisation of RM28.64 billion.

title: 'Diplomasi Sukan Anwar Letakkan Malaysia Kembali Di Persada Global – Penganalisis
body: 'Pendekatan Perdana Menteri Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yang memanfaatkan sukan sebagai platform diplomasi, aktiviti ekonomi dan penjenamaan negara membantu meletakkan semula Malaysia di pentas sukan global, menurut penganalisis. Felow Kanan Global Peace Institute Profesor Dr Mohd Mizan Mohammad Aslam berkata sejak beberapa bulan lepas, Malaysia telah menunjukkan betapa acara sukan global dapat dimanfaatkan bukan sahaja untuk menghiburkan orang ramai, tetapi juga memperkukuh hubungan antarabangsa, menjana aktiviti ekonomi dan mewujudkan rasa keterujaan di seluruh negara. “Sukan sering dianggap sebagai hiburan, tetapi bagi kerajaan, bidang itu juga boleh menjadi diplomasi, dasar ekonomi dan penjenamaan negara yang digabungkan menjadi satu,” katanya dalam kenyataan, hari ini. Formula Satu (F1) kembali ke Litar Antarabangsa Sepang (SIC) selepas sembilan tahun dan usaha Malaysia untuk memastikan akses kepada siaran Piala Dunia FIFA 2026 baru-baru ini, menunjukkan bahawa sukan juga dapat dimanfaatkan untuk memperkukuh penglibatan antarabangsa negara. Mohd Mizan berkata penganjuran F1 Grand Prix (GP) Gulf Air Bahrain di negara ini selama tiga hari hingga hari ini, menunjukkan dimensi antarabangsa diplomasi sukan, selepas GP Bahrain tidak dapat diteruskan di lokasi asalnya berikutan keadaan geopolitik di Asia Barat. Beliau berkata pengaturan itu melangkaui transaksi komersial yang melibatkan litar lumba kerana perkara itu dimudahkan dalam rangka hubungan antara Malaysia dengan Bahrain, dengan sokongan Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim dan Raja Bahrain Raja Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa. Putera Mahkota merangkap Perdana Menteri Bahrain Putera Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa turut berangkat ke Malaysia dan bertemu dengan Anwar pada hujung minggu perlumbaan berkenaan. Mohd Mizan berkata kehadiran Anwar pada sesi kelayakan di Sepang, melawat ke pit Mercedes-AMG Petronas dan penglibatan dalam majlis resepsi yang dianjurkan Putera Salman menunjukkan bahawa acara sukan itu dapat mewujudkan platform untuk penglibatan diplomatik. “Sukan mewujudkan platform diplomatik. Pemimpin bertemu, hubungan dua hala diperkukuh dan Malaysia diletakkan di hadapan khalayak global bukan melalui sidang kemuncak rasmi, tetapi menerusi satu daripada pertunjukan sukan yang paling dikenali di dunia,” katanya. Maklum balas orang ramai terhadap kembalinya F1 juga, katanya, sama penting dengan kira-kira 95,000 tiket tiga hari terjual pada akhir September dan SIC menjangkakan penjualan mencecah kira-kira 100,000 yang bakal menjadi jualan tiket tertinggi yang direkodkan untuk perlumbaan yang diadakan di litar tersebut. Beliau berkata acara itu juga menjana limpahan ekonomi yang ketara, dengan Kementerian Pelancongan, Seni dan Budaya (MOTAC) menganggarkan acara sukan tersebut mampu menarik kira-kira 300,000 pelancong termasuk sekitar 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa, manakala Hong Leong Bank Research mengunjurkan impak ekonomi kira-kira RM1.3 bilion melalui pelancongan sukan dan perbelajaan pelawat asing. “F1 tidak hanya memberikan manfaat kepada litar. Pengunjung berbelanja di hotel, restoran, pengangkutan, peruncitan dan pelancongan. Liputan televisyen membawa imej Malaysia ke seluruh dunia. Pasukan, penaja, wartawan dan pemimpin korporat global tiba di negara ini,” katanya. Berhubung sukan bola sepak, Mohd Mizan berkata keputusan kerajaan untuk memastikan Malaysia mempunyai akses kepada Piala Dunia FIFA 2026 mewakili dimensi domestik diplomasi sukan, berikutan bola sepak terus menjadi satu daripada sukan yang paling diikuti ramai di negara ini. RTM dan Unifi TV dilantik selaku penyiar rasmi, dengan kesemua 104 perlawanan dapat ditonton menerusi platform yang mengambil bahagian, manakala kerajaan memperuntukkan RM26.2 juta untuk memperoleh hak penyiaran, di samping kerjasama strategik dengan sektor swasta yang membantu meluaskan akses dan pengedaran, katanya. Beliau berkata akses kepada Piala Dunia melalui saluran yang sah dan mudah diakses mewakili satu bentuk keterangkuman sosial kerana acara sukan utama dapat mewujudkan pengalaman bersama merentasi kaum, umur, geografi dan pendapatan. “Semasa perlawanan bola sepak utama, restoran mamak, ruang tamu di rumah, dewan komuniti dan kawasan tontonan awam menjadi ruang yang dikongsi bersama-sama rakyat Malaysia,” katanya. Mohd Mizan berkata pendekatan Anwar menunjukkan bahawa diplomasi hari ini berlangsung jauh melangkaui bilik persidangan rasmi, dengan Malaysia menggunakan F1 dan FIFA untuk mendekatkan dunia dengan rakyatnya sambil memperkukuh kedudukan di pentas sukan antarabangsa. “Kadangkala, diplomasi berlaku melalui rundingan dua hala. Ada kalanya diplomasi terjadi menerusi bola sepak dan kadang-kadang, pada kelajuan 300 kilometer sejam di sekitar Sepang,” katanya. — BERNAMA.

Mohd Mizan berkata penganjuran F1 Grand Prix (GP) Gulf Air Bahrain di negara ini selama tiga hari hingga hari ini, menunjukkan dimensi antarabangsa diplomasi sukan, selepas GP Bahrain tidak dapat diteruskan di lokasi asalnya berikutan keadaan geopolitik di Asia Barat. Beliau berkata pengaturan itu melangkaui transaksi komersial yang melibatkan litar lumba kerana perkara itu dimudahkan dalam rangka hubungan antara Malaysia dengan Bahrain, dengan sokongan Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim dan Raja Bahrain Raja Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa. Putera Mahkota merangkap Perdana Menteri Bahrain Putera Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa turut berangkat ke Malaysia dan bertemu dengan Anwar pada hujung minggu perlumbaan berkenaan. Mohd Mizan berkata kehadiran Anwar pada sesi kelayakan di Sepang, melawat ke pit Mercedes-AMG Petronas dan penglibatan dalam majlis resepsi yang dianjurkan Putera Salman menunjukkan bahawa acara sukan itu dapat mewujudkan platform untuk penglibatan diplomatik. “Sukan mewujudkan platform diplomatik. Pemimpin bertemu, hubungan dua hala diperkukuh dan Malaysia diletakkan di hadapan khalayak global bukan melalui sidang kemuncak rasmi, tetapi menerusi satu daripada pertunjukan sukan yang paling dikenali di dunia,” katanya. Maklum balas orang ramai terhadap kembalinya F1 juga, katanya, sama penting dengan kira-kira 95,000 tiket tiga hari terjual pada akhir September dan SIC menjangkakan penjualan mencecah kira-kira 100,000 yang bakal menjadi jualan tiket tertinggi yang direkodkan untuk perlumbaan yang diadakan di litar tersebut. Beliau berkata acara itu juga menjana limpahan ekonomi yang ketara, dengan Kementerian Pelancongan, Seni dan Budaya (MOTAC) menganggarkan acara sukan tersebut mampu menarik kira-kira 300,000 pelancong termasuk sekitar 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa, manakala Hong Leong Bank Research mengunjurkan impak ekonomi kira-kira RM1.3 bilion melalui pelancongan sukan dan perbelajaan pelawat asing. “F1 tidak hanya memberikan manfaat kepada litar. Pengunjung berbelanja di hotel, restoran, pengangkutan, peruncitan dan pelancongan. Liputan televisyen membawa imej Malaysia ke seluruh dunia. Pasukan, penaja, wartawan dan pemimpin korporat global tiba di negara ini,” katanya. Berhubung sukan bola sepak, Mohd Mizan berkata keputusan kerajaan untuk memastikan Malaysia mempunyai akses kepada Piala Dunia FIFA 2026 mewakili dimensi domestik diplomasi sukan, berikutan bola sepak terus menjadi satu daripada sukan yang paling diikuti ramai di negara ini. RTM dan Unifi TV dilantik selaku penyiar rasmi, dengan kesemua 104 perlawanan dapat ditonton menerusi platform yang mengambil bahagian, manakala kerajaan memperuntukkan RM26.2 juta untuk memperoleh hak penyiaran, di samping kerjasama strategik dengan sektor swasta yang membantu meluaskan akses dan pengedaran, katanya. Beliau berkata akses kepada Piala Dunia melalui saluran yang sah dan mudah diakses mewakili satu bentuk keterangkuman sosial kerana acara sukan utama dapat mewujudkan pengalaman bersama merentasi kaum, umur, geografi dan pendapatan. “Semasa perlawanan bola sepak utama, restoran mamak, ruang tamu di rumah, dewan komuniti dan kawasan tontonan awam menjadi ruang yang dikongsi bersama-sama rakyat Malaysia,” katanya. Mohd Mizan berkata pendekatan Anwar menunjukkan bahawa diplomasi hari ini berlangsung jauh melangkaui bilik persidangan rasmi, dengan Malaysia menggunakan F1 dan FIFA untuk mendekatkan dunia dengan rakyatnya sambil memperkukuh kedudukan di pentas sukan antarabangsa. “Kadangkala, diplomasi berlaku melalui rundingan dua hala. Ada kalanya diplomasi terjadi menerusi bola sepak dan kadang-kadang, pada kelajuan 300 kilometer sejam di sekitar Sepang,” katanya. — BERNAMA.

title: 'Player fatigue threatens TNB campaign as MHL resumes
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: The second round of the Malaysian Hockey League (MHL) begins on Monday, and it has caused havoc for league leaders Tenaga Nasional (TNB) and their season campaign.   TNB will face the Armed Forces on Wednesday at the National Hockey Stadium in Bukit Jalil but 11 of their players will only be arriving on Monday from the Asian Games.    Malaysia were defeated 5-1 by defending champions India in the Asiad final in Nagoya on Saturday.    The first round of MHL ended on May 17 with TNB leading the standings on 19 points from six wins and a draw, followed by Maybank and Terengganu Hockey Team with 17 and 14 points respectively.

title: 'Syed Saddiq, Bella Astillah to hold wedding receptions in Muar & Kota Kinabalu, public invited to 'Kenduri Rakyat'
body: 'Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and Malaysian singer-actress Bella Astillah, who are set to marry on Oct 10, will celebrate their special occasion with the public through two receptions themed “Kenduri Rakyat”. The couple, who got engaged on March 28, will first exchange vows at Menara Merdeka Maybank in Kuala Lumpur. The celebrations will then continue in Muar, Johor, on Oct 25, before the couple heads to Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, on Oct 31. At a press conference in Kuala Lumpur today (Oct 2), Syed Saddiq said preparations for the receptions had been challenging, as the events were organised within a span of two months. Much of the difficulty came from finding enough vendors and a suitable venue within the limited timeframe. “We are expecting around 20,000 to 30,000 guests. We will do our best to accommodate everyone,” the former youth and sports minister said. Bella said about 10,000 special souvenirs would be prepared for guests attending the two public receptions, with the items distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. She clarified that the Sabah reception would be held in Kota Kinabalu instead of in her hometown of Sandakan due to certain limitations. Bella then went on to share more about her relationship with Syed Saddiq, revealing that it was the simple things he did that gave her the confidence to trust him. “Everything he does is big in my eyes. Just little things like opening the door for me, reminding me to sleep early and eat my meals or just telling me to exercise … Even though it’s basic stuff, I’m happy,” she said. Bella previously married Singaporean actor Aliff Aziz in 2016, but the relationship ended in divorce twice – once in 2019 and the second time in 2024. She has two children from her former marriage: Ayden, nine; and Ara, six.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Opens Higher On Positive Wall Street Momentum
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 – Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Tuesday morning, tracking positive overnight momentum on Wall Street as subdued crude oil prices—driven by a recovery in West Asia crude exports—helped offset a ongoing sell-off in US Treasuries. At 9:21 AM, the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) advanced 7.14 points, or 0.44 per cent, to reach 1,638.89 compared to Monday’s close of 1,631.75. The index had initially opened 4.63 points higher at 1,636.38. Across the broader market, advancing counters outpaced decliners 272 to 202, with 364 counters remaining unchanged, 1,944 untraded, and 13 suspended. Market turnover stood at 440.19 million units valued at RM164.76 million. Heavyweight Movements and Sector Performance Heavyweight banking and energy-linked stocks led the early morning gains, helping push all main index boards higher. Key market movements across categories during early trade included: - Heavyweight Performance: Maybank and Tenaga Nasional each gained four sen to RM10.04 and RM13.04, respectively, while CIMB rose three sen to RM7.76. IHH Healthcare added two sen to RM7.78, while Public Bank traded flat at RM4.71. - Active Counters: Zetrix AI inched up half a sen to seven sen, Divfex added one sen to 16.5 sen, and Ramssol rose 2.5 sen to 86 sen. Meanwhile, ACE Market debutant SLGC fell 3.5 sen to 24.5 sen, and Dagang NeXchange edged down half a sen to 50 sen. - Top Gainers: Plantation counters saw strong demand, led by Batu Kawan, which surged RM1.24 to RM20.22. Nestle and Kuala Lumpur Kepong gained 20 sen each to RM90.20 and RM21.06, respectively, followed by Petronas Dagangan (up 18 sen to RM19.38) and Genting Plantations (up 16 sen to RM5.82). - Top Decliners: HeiTech Padu dropped seven sen to 88 sen, while Thong Guan Industries, Sunway Construction Group, and Allianz Malaysia declined six sen each to RM1.44, RM7.55, and RM20.74, respectively. UMS Integration lost four sen to trade at RM9.36. - Index Breakdown: The Plantation Index posted significant gains, jumping 73.78 points to 9,004.81. The Financial Services Index surged 56.47 points to 19,196.61, the Energy Index gained 1.78 points to 831.72, and the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.16 of a point to 179.13. The FBM Mid 70 Index advanced 41.29 points to 17,584.78, the FBM Emas Index added 44.30 points to 12,234.65, and the FBM ACE Index rose 7.73 points to 5,614.34. –NMT

title: 'Scheduling boo-boo: Malaysian hockey league matches originally set for Deepavali rescheduled - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Coaches of Premier League hockey teams scheduled to play on Deepavali day are happy they will now battle it out on different dates, as the Malaysian Hockey Confederation (MHC) repeats its 2018 scheduling boo-boo. Two matches – Terengganu Hockey Team against Armed Forces Hockey Team and TNB Thunderbolts versus Maybank – were originally scheduled for Nov 8, the day Deepavali is celebrated in Malaysia. However, the matches will now be rescheduled, much to the delight of TNB Thunderbolts and Terengganu Hockey Team. Mohd Harfizi Baharom of Terengganu said he had been informed that the match against the soldiers would now be played on Nov 9. “It is good that we will not be playing on such an auspicious day. It gives those celebrating the festival time to spend with their families,” Mohd Harfizi told Twentytwo13. “Several of our players have only just returned from the Asian Games. Unfortunately, there is a packed international calendar and the national team will be off to the Asian Champions Trophy from Oct 27 to Nov 5. “As such, having an extra day to prepare for the match against the Armed Forces is welcome. We are third in the standings, but have not given up hope of winning the title. One day can make a difference.” However, the new dates are not reflected on MHC’s website as of publication time. TNB Thunderbolts coach Nor Saiful Zaini, who is also the national junior coach, said he has yet to receive official notice of the new date. “I know it is not easy for MHC to juggle the calendar, but we shouldn’t play on Deepavali or any other religious festival. I am waiting for confirmation regarding the change of date,” said Nor Saiful. In 2018, the Razak Cup was initially scheduled from Nov 3-11, with Deepavali falling on Nov 6 that year. After protests from teams, especially Negeri Sembilan, which threatened to pull out of the tournament, MHC eventually brought forward the tournament to Oct 26-Nov 3. The repeat of the episode raised eyebrows, as those in charge of scheduling the league should have been fully aware of the festive seasons in the country. Meanwhile, Nor Saiful said he would have his hands full as the national juniors will compete in the Sultan of Johor Cup (Oct 17-24), followed by the Murugappa Gold Cup (Oct 25-Nov 4) in India. Nor Saiful was instrumental in recently guiding the national team to next year’s Junior World Cup. “I will need to juggle my team selection carefully, as we have to consider the league matches as well as the two major tournaments. “Some of the teams may be reluctant to release their junior players, but on the bright side, I have the chance to test more players in Johor and India,” he added.

title: 'Bursa dibuka tinggi pada awal dagangan hari ini
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR,. Bursa Malaysia meningkat semula untuk dibuka tinggi pada Jumaat didorong oleh hasil Perbendaharaan Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang rendah da KUALA LUMPUR,. Bursa Malaysia meningkat semula untuk dibuka tinggi pada Jumaat didorong oleh hasil Perbendaharaan Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang rendah dan sentimen Rizab Persekutuan (Fed) yang berhati-hati memberikan kelegaan kepada pelabur. Pada 9.10 pagi, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 1.49 mata atau 0.09 peratus kepada 1,631.85 daripada 1,630.36 semasa ditutup pada Khamis. Indeks dibuka tinggi 3.51 mata kepada 1,633.87. Dalam pasaran secara menyeluruh, kaunter untung mengatasi kaunter rugi sebanyak 239 berbanding 137 manakala 270 kaunter tidak berubah, 2,127 tidak diniagakan dan 24 yang lain digantung. Jumlah dagangan sebanyak 173.94 juta saham bernilai RM95.98 juta. Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd Thong Pak Leng berkata penurunan terkini telah mendorong indeks kembali kepada keadaan terlebih jual, yang boleh menggalakkan aktiviti belian saham pada harga rendah. “Bagaimanapun, dengan situasi jualan asing yang dilaporkan, kami percaya sebarang peningkatan awal mungkin kekal sederhana. “Namun demikian, aliran penurunan membuka peluang untuk membeli secara terpilih saham yang mempunyai asas kukuh terutamanya dalam kalangan bank yang mapan, syarikat utiliti dan syarikat semikonduktor,” katanya kepada Bernama. Thong berkata pemulihan yang lebih mampan memerlukan penyertaan yang lebih baik daripada kaunter saham wajaran tinggi dan peningkatan jumlah saham daripada pelbagai sektor. Oleh itu, beliau menjangka dagangan berhati-hati hari ini dalam julat 1,625 hingga 1,640. Dalam kalangan saham wajaran tinggi, Maybank mendatar pada RM9.95, Public Bank dan CIMB, masing-masing menurun satu sen kepada RM4.66 dan RM7.68, Tenaga Nasional naik empat sen kepada RM12.94 dan IHH Healthcare meningkat satu sen kepada RM7.71. Dalam dagangan aktif, Zetrix AI, Jaks Resources dan Genetec, masing-masing kekal tidak berubah pada 16.5 sen, 18 sen dan 32.5 sen, V.S Industry naik satu sen kepada 28 sen, bagaimanapun Kinergy Advancement menurun setengah sen kepada 39.5 sen. Kaunter paling untung ialah Malaysian Pacific Industries meningkat 58 sen kepada RM41.70, Hengyuan Refining naik 19 sen kepada RM3.83, Petronas Chemicals menokok 15 sen kepada RM4.28 serta UWC dan MI Technovation, masing-masing menambah 10 sen kepada RM7.20 dan RM5.36. Kaunter paling rugi termasuklah MISC menurun 14 sen kepada RM7.54, LPI Capital, Hong Leong Industries, MNRB dan RHB Bank, masing-masing merosot empat sen kepada RM12.80, RM16.10, RM2.78 dan RM7.43. Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid 70 meningkat 75.93 mata kepada 17,434.91, Indeks FBM Emas naik 17.18 mata kepada 12,160.71 dan Indeks FBM Top 100 menokok 21.58 mata kepada 11,954.73. Indeks FBM Emas Shariah menambah 34.76 mata kepada 12,047.77 dan Indeks FBM ACE naik 18.61 mata kepada 5,501.58. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk Perindustrian dan Perkhidmatan meningkat 1.10 mata kepada 178.83, Indeks Tenaga naik 9.45 mata kepada 844.46, Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan menurun 26.33 mata kepada 19,034.58 manakala Indeks Perladangan menokok 2.75 mata kepada 9,029.32. — BERNAMA

title: 'IOI Properties now agrees to buy Shenton House from group CEO for S$1, settle S$217m advances
body: 'IOI Properties now agrees to buy Shenton House from group CEO for S$1, settle S$217m advances KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): IOI Properties Group Bhd (KL:IOIPG) has agreed to acquire Shenton 101 Pte Ltd, which owns Singapore's Shenton House, from its group chief executive officer and major shareholder Datuk Lee Yeow Seng for a nominal S$1.00. Under the deal, announced in a filing with Bursa Malaysia on Thursday, IOI Properties will also settle S$217.06 million (RM696.43 million) worth of shareholder advances (as at July 31, 2026) that Lee had injected into Shenton 101, the vehicle he incorporated to acquire the property. The final repayment sum will be determined on completion. The transaction marks a reversal by the group’s non-interested directors, who turned down an earlier offer from Lee in August 2024, citing heavy capital commitments following several asset acquisitions at the time. To manage potential conflicts of interest, IOI Properties had entered into project and property management agreements for the building instead. Shenton 101 acquired Shenton House — a 25-storey strata-titled commercial development completed in the mid-1970s sitting on a 3,377-sq-metre site — via tender for S$538 million in November 2023, with the purchase completed in June 2024. The vehicle secured S$376.23 million in bank borrowings to finance the acquisition, with the remainder of the purchase price, buyer's stamp duty (S$26.87 million), planning consultation fees and ongoing holding costs funded via interest-free advances from Lee. These existing bank borrowings will be consolidated into IOI Properties' accounts upon completion of the deal. No shareholder approval needed The acquisition, which will be funded through IOI Properties’ internal funds, does not require shareholder approval as its highest percentage ratio is 3.79% — below the 5% threshold under Bursa's listing rules. However, it will require Bank Negara Malaysia's green light as the foreign currency investment exceeds the group's permissible limit, as well as consent from Shenton 101's lenders and the Singapore Land Authority. IOI Properties said the acquisition will allow it to strengthen its presence in Singapore's Marina Bay precinct and unlock synergies with its existing asset portfolio, given Shenton House's walking distance to IOI Central Boulevard Towers and the recently acquired Asia Square Tower 2. The group said it is revisiting the deal, on the request of Lee, after its "circumstances and strategic position have evolved". It pointed out that IOI Central Boulevard Towers has achieved over 95% committed occupancy and is self-sustaining in debt servicing. It has also completed the acquisitions of the remaining 50.1% stake in Scottsdale Properties Pte Ltd — which owns South Beach Tower, South Beach Avenue and JW Marriott Hotel Singapore South Beach — and Asia Square Tower 2. It noted that its acquisitions in Malaysia have also continued to perform satisfactorily, and that shareholders had, on Sept 30, approved injecting W Kuala Lumpur hotel and Courtyard by Marriott Penang hotel into the upcoming IOI Properties REIT, in support of the group's capital recycling strategy. “Although the group’s gearing has increased, the increase is largely attributable to acquisitions of income-generating assets in Singapore that have enhanced the quality of the group's investment property portfolio and strengthened its position in key gateway markets,” it said. Plans for a 35-storey mixed-use landmark The group plans to redevelop Shenton House into a 35-storey mixed-use landmark featuring 12 floors of Grade-A offices, a 10-storey luxury hotel (165 keys), a retail basement and three carpark levels. This will expand its total net lettable area from 20,276 sq metres (218,246 sq ft) to 36,528 sq metres (393,185 sq ft). The underlying land tenure, which has a remaining lease of about 42 years, is expected to be renewed to a fresh 99-year term. Savills appraised the market value of Shenton House as a redevelopment site at S$585 million, with an estimated gross development value of S$1.61 billion against total redevelopment costs of S$973.65 million. Maybank Investment Bank is the principal adviser for the exercise. Although not mandated by listing rules, IOI Properties also appointed Affin Hwang Investment Bank as an independent adviser to advise non-interested directors on the deal's fairness and reasonableness. Lee and his brother Datuk Lee Yeow Chor, who is a non-independent non-executive director, are deemed interested parties and have abstained from all board deliberations and voting on the proposal. The deal is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of 2026. Shares of IOI Properties closed six sen or 1.73% lower at RM3.40 on Thursday, valuing the group at RM18.72 billion. title: 'Banks weather Middle East shock with asset quality intact
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's banking sector asset quality remains broadly resilient despite the economic impact of the conflict in the Middle East, according to RHB Research. The firm said any repayment strain remained confined to pockets of the economy rather than becoming systemic. Citing Bank Negara Malaysia's recent assessment and engagement session, the firm said the main transmission channels from the conflict were through the real economy and global financial markets rather than direct bank exposures. Higher input and logistics costs, coupled with softer demand, were putting pressure on business margins, particularly among small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in the wholesale and retail trade, construction and manufacturing sectors. However, domestic demand and electrical and electronics exports continued to support overall economic conditions, while business and system impairment ratios remained steady at 2.8 per cent and 1.4 per cent, respectively. RHB Research said Stage 2 loans had also eased, while household borrowers remained resilient. Meanwhile, the banking sector could withstand higher bond yields, although a 100-basis-point rise could reduce the sector's common equity Tier-1 (CET-1) ratio by about 46 basis points after mitigation measures. The firm said the impact would be manageable but banks would have thinner capital cushions compared with the 2021-2022 bond sell-off. It estimated that a 100-basis-point parallel shift in bond yields could reduce sector CET-1 capital by about RM8 billion at the group level. Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd, Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd and Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) were among the most sensitive to higher yields at group level, with estimated CET-1 reductions of 88, 62 and 57 basis points respectively. At the bank-entity level, Maybank was the most sensitive, with an estimated 104-basis-point reduction, followed by Bank Islam at 88 basis points and Alliance Bank at 70 basis points. RHB Research said banks using the standardised approach, including Public Bank Bhd, Hong Leong Bank Bhd, Alliance Bank, Affin Bank Bhd and Bank Islam, should benefit from capital releases under Basel III reforms, cushioning much of the mark-to-market impact. For banks using the internal ratings-based approach, corporate restructuring and dividend reinvestment plans (DRPs) could provide some capital relief. RHB Research said the sector's buffers were thinner than during the 2021-2022 bond sell-off, when the 10-year Malaysian Government Securities yield rose to 4.07 per cent at end-2022 from 2.69 per cent at end-2020. The firm estimated that banks incurred about RM16 billion in fair-value losses on securities classified as fair value through other comprehensive income (FVOCI) over the two years. Despite this, the sector's CET-1 ratio remained broadly within 14 to 15 per cent, supported by strong net profit growth, sizeable FVOCI reserve buffers and DRPs. Banks also shifted some new security purchases into held-to-maturity portfolios to reduce exposure to mark-to-market losses. This time, however, the sector's FVOCI revaluation reserve has fallen to about RM3.9 billion from around RM9.7 billion previously. RHB Research said AMMB Holdings Bhd (AmBank) was the only bank whose FVOCI reserves exceeded its estimated loss from higher bond yields, making it relatively more insulated from the risk. On funding conditions, Bank Negara was said to have played down concerns that rising KLIBOR reflected thinning liquidity in the instrument, although average funding costs had increased. RHB Research said regulatory liquidity ratios remained healthy, with the central bank comfortable with banks operating at lower levels rather than paying excessively to secure funding. The firm's top picks in the banking sector are AmBank, Maybank and Hong Leong.

title: 'HLB Islamic Berjaya Lonjak Pendapatan Usahawan Berpendapatan Rendah Langkawi Sebanyak 94%
body: 'Kuala Lumpur, 23 September 2026 – Selaras dengan komitmen untuk memperkasakan ekosistem perantaraan berasaskan nilai (“Value-based Intermediation” atau “VBI”), HLB Islamic (atau “Bank”) telah menyalurkan pembiayaan sebanyak RM138,600 kepada perusahaan sosial SURI Inspirasi (“SURI”) di bawah kerangka iTEKAD Bank Negara Malaysia (“BNM”). Inisiatif ini secara langsung menyumbang kepada peningkatan purata pendapatan bulanan sebanyak 94% serta menjana jumlah pendapatan baharu melebihi RM14,000 bagi usahawan yang menyertai program “Sustainable Reliable Income” (“SRI”) anjuran SURI. Program SRI memperkasakan komuniti berpendapatan rendah untuk mengitar semula sisa fabrik menjadi barangan fesyen yang unik, yang secara langsung mewujudkan peluang pekerjaan dan memupuk semangat keusahawanan di samping mempromosikan fesyen sifar sisa serta pemerkasaan komuniti. Usahawan yang terlibat, yang majoritinya ibu tunggal berpendapatan rendah, telah menghasilkan 1,000 pasang pakaian seragam sekolah untuk pelajar di lima buah sekolah di Langkawi, sekali gus menjana penjimatan sebanyak RM30,000 bagi keluarga tempatan. HLB Islamic meraikan pencapaian ini menerusi penyerahan mesin jahit berkualiti tinggi kepada para usahawan yang terlibat, menandakan peralihan daripada pembelajaran di dalam bilik darjah kepada pemilikan perniagaan secara aktif. Menurut Dafinah Ahmed Hilmi, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif HLB Islamic, “Visi kami tentang pengurusan kewangan berteraskan Hayat @ HLB Islamic, di mana pengurusan harta dilihat sebagai satu perjalanan yang bermula dengan Penciptaan Harta. Melalui kerjasama dengan SURI, kami menyediakan alat dan latihan asas yang diperlukan oleh komuniti untuk mencungkil potensi keusahawanan mereka. Kami berharap usaha ini akan menjadi pemangkin kepada perjalanan pembinaan kekayaan yang berterusan ke arah kebebasan kewangan yang bakal memperkayakan komuniti untuk generasi akan datang.” Kejayaan ini menandakan satu pencapaian penting dalam kerjasama berterusan antara HLB Islamic dan SURI, yang mula menyertai ekosistem Bank ini sebagai peserta inisiatif HLB Jumpstart. Diperkenalkan bagi memupuk perusahaan sosial Malaysia yang berimpak tinggi menerusi bimbingan komersial, penjenamaan, serta pembinaan kapasiti digital, HLB Jumpstart telah menyediakan kerangka awal kepada SURI untuk memperluas operasinya. Hal ini membuktikan strategi jangka panjang Bank dalam memupuk usaha sosial menjadi rakan pelaksana berdikari yang mampu memberikan impak yang lebih meluas. title: 'Maybank falls below RM10 for first time in nine months, rising bond yields hurt banking stocks
body: 'Maybank falls below RM10 for first time in nine months, rising bond yields hurt banking stocks KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK) fell below RM10 for the first time in nearly nine months and banking stocks mostly declined on Thursday amid rising bond yields. Higher yields generally hurt banks as they take larger paper losses from lower prices of the bonds they hold, which eats into capital and forces them to book losses if they sell. Banks will also have to increase their rates to attract depositors, leading to higher funding costs. That would weigh on banks’ near term non-interest income as well as their capital ratios, Affin Hwang Investment Bank flagged in a note on Thursday. Maybank, the country’s top bank in terms of assets, fell for the third straight day and closed down 0.4% at RM9.95. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) and Hong Leong Bank Bhd (KL:HLBANK) each declined over 1%. The Bursa Malaysia Financial Services Index, which also tracks non-bank firms such as insurers and stockbrokers, fell to its lowest level in 10 months. The US Federal Reserve raised interest rates earlier this month for the first time in three years, sending the yield on the 10-year benchmark Malaysian Government Securities to as high as 4.18% before moderating. A growing number of economists expect Bank Negara Malaysia to raise the overnight policy rate in November during the final scheduled monetary policy review for the year. Rising yields tend to lead to higher corporate bond yields, which also tie-in to capital raising decisions both for banks and other corporates and, subsequently, fee income to the banks, Affin Hwang said. Maybank and Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd (KL:ABMB) have on their books the longest bond duration — the length of time for a bond to repay its cost in cash flows while also being a measure of sensitivity to changes in interest rates — according to the research house’s analysis. Public Bank Bhd (KL:PBBANK) and Hong Leong Bank, meanwhile, have the shortest duration. In terms of capital ratios, Maybank, RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK) and CIMB could see the largest drops, while Public Bank and Hong Leong Bank would see the least due to their portfolios’ shorter duration, the house added. title: '100bps Bond Yield Rise Could Cut Banks’ CET-1 By 46bps
body: 'A further 100-basis-point rise in bond yields could reduce Malaysian banks’ aggregate Common Equity Tier-1 (CET-1) capital ratio by about 46 basis points, although the impact should remain manageable due to Basel III-related capital relief and other mitigating measures, according to RHB Research.  RHB said the estimated sector-wide mark-to-market impact would amount to around RM8 billion at group level, with Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd, Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd and Malayan Banking Bhd among the more sensitive banks.  At group level, RHB estimated a 100bps parallel shift in yields could reduce CET-1 ratios by 88bps for Bank Islam, 62bps for Alliance Bank, 57bps for Maybank and 52bps for CIMB.  At the bank-entity level, the estimated impact ranges from just 11bps for Affin Bank to 104bps for Maybank, with Bank Islam and Alliance Bank also relatively more exposed.  By comparison, AMMB Holdings Bhd and Public Bank Bhd are viewed as better insulated.  RHB maintained AMMB, Maybank and Hong Leong Bank as its top sector picks.  Smaller Capital Buffers Than 2021-2022  RHB noted that the banking system weathered the sharp bond sell-off in 2021 and 2022 relatively well.  During that period, the 10-year Malaysian Government Securities yield climbed to 4.07% at end-2022 from 2.69% at end-2020, while the sector recorded an estimated RM16 billion in fair-value losses on securities classified as fair value through other comprehensive income.  Despite this, sector CET-1 ratios largely remained within the 14%-15% range, supported by strong earnings growth, large FVOCI reserve buffers and dividend reinvestment plans.  Banks also shifted more new securities purchases into held-to-maturity portfolios to reduce mark-to-market volatility.  This time, however, RHB said the sector has thinner cushions. FVOCI revaluation reserves currently stand at only about RM3.9 billion, compared with approximately RM9.7 billion previously.  AMMB is the only bank where its FVOCI reserve is estimated to exceed the potential hit from higher bond yields.  Basel III Reforms To Help Standardised Banks  RHB said banks using the standardised approach, including Public Bank, Hong Leong Bank, Alliance Bank, Affin Bank and Bank Islam, should benefit from capital release arising from Basel III reforms, which could offset much of the near-term mark-to-market impact.  For banks using the Internal Ratings-Based approach, RHB said measures such as corporate restructuring and dividend reinvestment plans could provide additional capital support.  The impact from securities classified as fair value through profit or loss is expected to be considerably smaller. Based on previous Bank Negara Malaysia stress tests, RHB estimated a 100bps yield move could have an impact of up to only around 6bps, reflecting the smaller size of FVTPL portfolios relative to FVOCI and held-to-maturity books.  Middle East Conflict Risks Still Contained  RHB also highlighted Bank Negara’s assessment that risks from the Middle East conflict are being transmitted mainly through the real economy and financial markets rather than through banks’ direct exposure to the region.  Higher input and logistics costs, together with softer demand, are putting pressure on business margins, particularly among SMEs in wholesale and retail trade, construction and manufacturing.  However, RHB noted that overall asset quality remains stable, with business impairment at 2.8% and the system-wide impairment ratio at 1.4%, while stress remains concentrated in selected segments rather than becoming systemic.  On funding conditions, RHB said BNM had attributed the rise in KLIBOR partly to thinner liquidity in the benchmark itself, although average banking-sector funding costs have also increased.  Regulatory liquidity ratios remain healthy, while the central bank appears comfortable with banks operating at somewhat lower liquidity levels rather than aggressively competing for higher-cost funding.

title: 'RHB Pay simplifies how businesses manage digital payments
body: 'RHB Pay simplifies how businesses manage digital payments Malaysia’s first bank-owned unified payment platform helps businesses bring multiple payment channels together, with faster settlement and simpler reconciliation. For businesses, getting paid is only one part of the equation. Knowing where the money is, when it will reach the bank account and how to reconcile transactions can be just as important, particularly for businesses handling high volumes of digital payments. Launched by RHB Bank Berhad, RHB Pay is Malaysia’s first bank-owned unified online payment platform, bringing payment collection, settlement and reconciliation onto a single platform. Built on RHB’s banking infrastructure with bank-grade security, it is designed to give businesses greater control over their collections and cash flow. Digital payments have established themselves as an integral part of modern commerce. Malaysia recorded more than 18 billion electronic payment transactions in 2025, highlighting the growing role of digital payments in how businesses collect and manage money. For merchants, the proposition is straightforward: accept payments through cards, FPX, DuitNow and e-wallets through one integration, while having a consolidated view of transactions and settlement. But the move to digital payments can also bring its own set of operational headaches, particularly for mid-sized corporates and small and medium enterprises (SMEs) that have to manage separate systems, logins, settlement files and reconciliation processes across different payment methods. That fragmentation adds friction as businesses shift more volume away from cash handling and its associated costs. RHB Pay is designed to reduce that fragmentation by bringing the different payment channels into one integration layer. This means merchants do not have to build and maintain separate integrations for each payment method they offer. The unified platform also simplifies onboarding and verification across payment channels, reducing the time and effort required for merchants to get started. It is also designed to accommodate new digital payment channels as they emerge, without requiring merchants to build another integration each time. Getting cash into the business faster A payment platform’s value does not end when a customer completes a transaction. Settlement is where many merchants feel the biggest strain. How quickly funds reach their accounts can have a direct bearing on working capital and day-to-day cash flow. With some third-party payment arrangements, funds can take one to five days to reach the merchant’s bank account, depending on the payment method and settlement arrangement. By comparison, RHB Pay is designed to provide real-time or next-day settlement directly into the merchant’s RHB account, giving them faster access to their collections. For those operating on tight cash cycles, that can mean having funds available sooner for supplier payments, inventory replenishment and other operating expenses. Less time spent matching transactions Reconciliation is another area where payment fragmentation can create additional work. Traditionally, businesses spend considerable time and manual effort matching end-of-day sales across disparate e-wallet portals, card terminals and bank transfers. RHB Pay consolidates these transactions into a standardised report within its portal, which can be reconciled directly against the merchant's bank statement. This gives businesses a single view of their collections, rather than having to pull information from multiple payment platforms and match them manually. A consolidated view becomes more useful as payment volumes grow, giving businesses greater visibility over their cash position while reducing the administrative work involved in reconciliation. Built on banking infrastructure Security and reliability become increasingly important as more payment collections move online. RHB Pay is built on RHB’s banking infrastructure, operating within the bank’s governance and regulatory framework. This gives merchants added assurance over the handling of their funds and payment data. RHB Pay also leverages Malaysia’s wider payments infrastructure, including PayNet’s national payment rails such as FPX and DuitNow, alongside technology partners across the payments ecosystem. The platform’s roadmap will see further use of AI and data analytics, including in areas such as reconciliation, fraud management, cash flow forecasting and financial planning. More than a payment gateway For RHB, the strategic opportunity extends beyond payment processing fees. By bringing merchants’ payment collections into the bank, RHB can deepen its relationship with businesses through the transaction flows that run through their day-to-day operations. These flows can also support the bank’s broader transaction banking proposition, including deposits, working capital financing and other financial solutions. According to research by CIMB Securities, RHB’s enhanced transaction banking capability could lift the Group’s net interest margin (NIM) by about five basis points over time, equivalent to an estimated RM170 million in additional net interest income. Rather than focusing solely on generating payment gateway fees, RHB’s core strategy centres on capturing merchant transaction flows to build low-cost, sticky Current Account and Savings Account (CASA) deposits. These transaction-linked deposits are embedded in merchants’ daily cash flow cycles, which can make them stickier than deposits acquired primarily through interest rate pricing. The ability to better understand businesses’ transaction flows could also support more targeted working capital financing and other banking solutions as businesses grow, while creating opportunities for broader fee income and cross-selling. CIMB Securities maintains a “Buy” rating on RHB Bank with a target price of RM9.20, citing the potential for the bank to strengthen its CASA franchise and deliver capital-efficient earnings growth, alongside its dividend yield and Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital position. Building for the next phase of digital payments The immediate benefits are simpler payment collection, faster access to funds and less time spent on reconciliation. RHB also sees scope to build on this with AI and data analytics, with potential applications in cost management, cash flow planning, fraud management and other operational areas. The longer-term opportunity is to give businesses greater visibility into the money flowing through their operations, rather than simply providing another channel to accept payments. title: 'AHB kekalkan agihan pendapatan 5.00 sen seunit, pemegang unit terima RM236.41 juta bagi FY2026 - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 1 Okt - Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) mengekalkan jumlah agihan pendapatan termasuk bonus sebanyak 5.00 sen seunit bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 30 September 2026 (FY2026), dengan keseluruhan pembayaran RM236.41 juta yang memberi manfaat kepada lebih 82,000 pemegang unit. Pelaburan Hartanah Berhad (PHB) bersama pengurus dananya, PHB Asset Management Berhad (PHBAM), mengumumkan agihan pendapatan akhir sebanyak 2.10 sen seunit bagi tempoh enam bulan berakhir 30 September 2026, menurut kenyataan PHB bersama hari ini. PHB selaku penaja dana turut mengisytiharkan edaran bonus sebanyak 0.40 sen seunit, menjadikan jumlah agihan bagi tempoh tersebut sebanyak 2.50 sen seunit. Bonus itu diberikan kepada pegangan sehingga satu juta unit pertama bagi setiap pemegang unit. Selepas mengambil kira agihan pendapatan interim sebanyak 2.50 sen seunit yang diumumkan pada April 2026, jumlah agihan bagi FY2026 mencapai 5.00 sen seunit. Agihan akhir itu membabitkan pembayaran RM120.13 juta. Agihan pendapatan tersebut adalah bersih selepas cukai dan zakat, membolehkan pemegang unit menerima jumlah penuh tanpa sebarang potongan atau tanggungan tambahan. Pembayaran akan dibuat dalam bentuk unit AHB dan dikreditkan terus ke dalam akaun pemegang unit selewat-lewatnya pada 13 Oktober 2026. Pengarah Urusan Kumpulan PHB, Mazuki Abdullah @ Muhammad berkata agihan bagi FY2026 mencerminkan ketahanan berterusan AHB dan kekuatan portfolio hartanahnya, disokong pendekatan pengurusan aset serta pelaburan yang berdisiplin. “Prestasi AHB pada tahun ini membuktikan komitmen kami untuk terus memberikan pulangan yang kompetitif kepada pemegang unit,” katanya. Beliau berkata PHB terus memperkukuh kedudukan AHB sebagai instrumen pelaburan pilihan pelabur Bumiputera melalui pengurusan modal yang berhemat, strategi pelaburan dinamik dan pengoptimuman portfolio bagi memastikan pertumbuhan mampan serta penciptaan nilai jangka panjang. Menurut Mazuki, penawaran tambahan sebanyak 400 juta unit AHB yang diumumkan baru-baru ini memperluas peluang kepada lebih ramai pelabur Bumiputera untuk mengambil bahagian dalam pelaburan hartanah komersial utama. Beliau berkata AHB akan terus menyokong pembentukan kekayaan jangka panjang Bumiputera dan menjana nilai mampan kepada pemegang unit. Komitmen itu selaras dengan aspirasi Pelan Transformasi Ekonomi Bumiputera 2035 (PUTERA35) untuk memperkukuh penyertaan ekonomi, pemilikan dan pembentukan kekayaan Bumiputera. Agihan dilaburkan semula secara automatik Sementara itu, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif PHBAM, Zulkifli Ishak berkata pihaknya kekal komited menguruskan AHB secara bertanggungjawab supaya dana itu terus menjadi pilihan pelaburan yang mudah diakses oleh pelabur Bumiputera. Agihan pendapatan akan dilaburkan semula secara automatik, menambah pegangan unit pelabur dan membolehkan mereka berpotensi menikmati manfaat pengkompaunan dalam jangka panjang. Unit tambahan akan dikreditkan terus ke dalam akaun tanpa memerlukan permohonan berasingan. Pelabur Bumiputera boleh melanggan AHB pada harga tetap RM1.00 seunit, dengan pelaburan minimum RM100 dan maksimum RM1 juta. Langganan boleh dibuat di cawangan pengedar sah AHB seluruh negara, iaitu Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank), AmBank Berhad, AmBank Islamic Berhad, Bank Islam Malaysia Berhad dan Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia Berhad. Sejak ditubuhkan pada 2010, AHB telah mengagihkan sejumlah RM2.7 bilion pendapatan kepada pemegang unit Bumiputera.

title: 'Maybank Group Sustainability Week 2026 advances net zero ambitions through capacity building and collective action | Maybank
body: 'In its third year, MGSW 2026 recognised over 1000 certified sustainability practitioners & continues to inspire greater net zero action across the Group Maybank recently organised the Maybank Group Sustainability Week (MGSW) 2026, a three-day sustainability-focused programme held from 21 to 23 September 2026 at Menara Merdeka Maybank. Under the theme “Net Zero. From Commitment to Action”, MGSW 2026 focuses on advancing Maybank’s net zero journey through capacity building, deepening sustainability awareness and strengthening capabilities, in line with the Group’s ROAR30 sustainability ambitions. MGSW 2026 saw Maybankers across the Group participate in two key events; ‘Net Zero Week’, which featured a series of learning, engagement and experiential activities, and the ‘Maybank Sustainability Practitioner Certification (MSPC) Open Day’ and ‘Grand Conferment Ceremony’, which celebrated over 1,000 certified sustainability practitioners and inspiring Maybankers to advance in their sustainability journey. The event saw the attendance of Dato' Sri Khairussaleh Ramli, President & Group CEO Maybank, Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Group Chief Sustainability Officer Maybank, Board of Directors and Group EXCO members of Maybank, Dato’ Ir. Ts. (Dr.) Izwan Hasli Mohd Ibrahim, CEO PNB Merdeka Ventures, Muazzam Mohamad, Head of Corporate Sustainability & Stewardship PNB, Leo Pui Yong, Chief Sustainability Officer Tenaga Nasional Berhad and Edey Suresh Kumar Manikam, Board Director at Large UN Global Compact Network Malaysia, Brunei & Cambodia (UNGCMBC). Dato' Sri Khairussaleh Ramli said “As we advance in our sustainability journey, MGSW 2026 reflects our continued focus on enabling our people to support our customers' transition journeys to net zero through stronger knowledge and mindsets. Ultimately, our commitment to capacity building will in turn help our customers transition responsibly and sustainably, strengthen our communities and drive meaningful sustainability impact.” A key highlight of MGSW 2026 was the MSPC Grand Conferment Ceremony, which honoured 36 MSPC Level 3 Red Belt graduates from across the Group for their achievements and continued commitment in sustainability. Developed in partnership with UNGCMBC, the MSPC programme was introduced in 2023 with the vision of building a future-ready sustainability workforce. Through its four-tier certification pathway comprising Level 1 White, Level 2 Green, Level 3 Red and Level 4 Black Belt levels, the programme combines sustainability knowledge with practical application to equip Maybankers with the capabilities needed to drive sustainability initiatives across the organisation. Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli, President & Group CEO Maybank (Center in blue batik), Dato’ Ir. Ts. (Dr.) Izwan Hasli Mohd Ibrahim, CEO PNB Merdeka Ventures (In red tie) and Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Group Chief Sustainability Officer Maybank (In black blazer with glasses) posing with the MSPC Level 1 White Belt recipients at the MSPC Grand Conferment ceremony during the MGSW 2026. As the entry level of the MSPC programme, the certification equips Maybankers with the foundational knowledge and capabilities needed to drive sustainability initiatives across the Group. A key highlight of the MSPC ceremony was the recognition of the 36 MSPC Level 3 Red Belt graduates from across the Group. Since its inception, MSPC has grown into a network of sustainability practitioners across the Group, spanning more than 60 cohorts and expands beyond Malaysia to Singapore, Indonesia, the Philippines and Cambodia. To date, the programme has enrolled more than 2,300 participants and certified 1,755 practitioners. title: 'CIMB Securities lifts 2026 GDP growth forecast to 5pct on domestic strength
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: CIMB Securities Research has raised its forecast for Malaysia's 2026 gross domestic product (GDP) growth to five per cent from 4.8 per cent previously, backed by stronger-than-expected domestic activity. "Following the weaker-than-expected July Industrial Production Index (IPI) outturn, the third quarter (Q3) 2026 GDP nowcast has edged down to 5.0 per cent from 5.2 per cent," it said in a note. However, CIMB Securities said the weakening in domestic manufacturing assumed in its house forecast has so far not materialised. The firm noted that domestic-oriented production outside the motor vehicle segment strengthened in July, while overall manufacturing output continued to expand sequentially. "We therefore raise our Q3 2026 GDP growth forecast to 4.5 per cent from 4.0 per cent previously, and our full-year 2026 forecast to 5.0 per cent from 4.8 per cent previously. "This reflects stronger-than-expected resilience in domestic activity," it said. On the overnight policy rate, CIMB Securities said its outlook remained unchanged, with the inflation trajectory the key factor in determining the timing of a rate hike. Nevertheless, the firm said renewed escalation in the Middle East remained a downside risk to growth, while prospective US semiconductor tariffs could weigh on electrical and electronics manufacturing and exports if introduced.

title: 'Petros, Höegh Evi Tie Up to Develop Sarawak’s First LNG Regasification Terminal in Kuching
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Petroleum Sarawak Bhd (Petros) has partnered Norway-based maritime energy infrastructure group Höegh Evi to jointly develop Sarawak’s first liquefied natural gas (LNG) regasification facility in Kuching, with first gas targeted by end-2029. The two parties have signed a joint development agreement to develop, own and operate the Kuching LNG Terminal, which will form part of the Kuching Low-Carbon Hub (KLCH), Petros said in a statement on Thursday. The terminal will use a floating storage and regasification unit, essentially a vessel that receives LNG and converts it back into natural gas before it is supplied onshore. It will also include mooring facilities, subsea and onshore pipelines, as well as receiving facilities on land. Petros said the terminal would provide gas to Kuching and surrounding areas to meet growing energy demand and strengthen Sarawak’s energy security. The gas supply would initially support power generation while helping lay the groundwork for wider industrial development under the KLCH. “The Kuching LNG Terminal is a strategic investment to drive Sarawak’s next phase of economic development,” said Petros group chief executive officer Datuk Janin Girie. He said the project would provide the infrastructure needed to bring natural gas to Kuching while helping attract higher-value investments and new industries. Petros said the terminal could also support services such as small-scale LNG distribution, truck loading, bunkering, storage and reload activities. This would give the facility flexibility to supply gas beyond Kuching to other parts of Sarawak as demand grows. The KLCH was launched in November 2024 under the Sarawak Gas Roadmap. Petros had in May 2025 signed a strategic cooperation agreement with China Jiangsu International Economic and Technical Cooperation Group Ltd to support the hub’s master planning. Petros is Sarawak’s sole gas aggregator, with responsibilities covering gas procurement, distribution, import, regasification and supply. title: 'Maybank finalises RM2.5bil sukuk
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has completed the issuance of RM2.5bil additional tier 1 (AT1) sukuk mudharabah under its sukuk programme. In a Bursa Malaysia filing, the banking group said the perpetual sukuk comprises three series with nominal amounts of RM750mil, RM1.1bil and RM650mil, respectively. The RM750mil tranche carries a fixed distribution rate of 4.85% per annum until its first call date on Sept 29, 2031, while the RM1.1bil tranche carries a rate of 5.11% until its first call date on Sept 28, 2033. Meanwhile, the RM650mil tranche has a fixed distribution rate of 5.15% per annum until its first call date on Sept 26, 2036. The proceeds will be used for syariah- compliant purposes, including investments in ringgit- and foreign currency-denominated Islamic financial instruments approved by the syariah advisory councils of Bank Negara Malaysia or the Securities Commission. — Bernama Thank you for your report!
