title: 'PETRONAS Shuts Down Songkhla Pipeline Temporarily
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): PETRONAS said on Thursday the Songkhla export pipeline has been shut down temporarily after finding an issue during a routine inspection. The shutdown of the pipeline will have an impact on gas supply to customers in Malaysia and Thailand, the company officially known as Petroliam Nasional Bhd said in a statement. The pipeline will resume operations only once it has been confirmed safe to do so, PETRONAS noted. “Proactive measures are being taken to ensure continuity to customers in Malaysia,” the company said. “PETRONAS' integrated supply network provides the flexibility to sustain supply, and the company is working closely with its partners and customers to maintain system stability.” The exact nature of the issue identified was not disclosed. Trans Thai-Malaysia (Thailand) Ltd, PETRONAS’ joint venture with Thai state-owned PTT, operates the pipeline that connects natural gas production facilities in the Gulf of Thailand to processing plants in Thailand and Malaysia. title: 'Mplus Market Pulse - 06 Oct 2026
body: 'MY: Tracking Wall Street's positive performance last Friday, the local bourse kickstarted the week higher, buoyed by gains in the banking heavyweights including PBBANK and CIMB. Sector-wise, Technology (+1.74%) continued to outperform, led by gains in VITROX and UWC, while Construction (-1.46%) declined the most. US: Wall Street closed higher on Monday as muted oil prices following recovering Middle East crude exports offset a continued sell-off in U.S. Treasuries. The Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq advanced by 0.2%, 0.7% and 1.1% respectively, while the Brent crude and 10-year Treasury yield reached USD100.3 and 5.3%, respectively. US: Given the broadly in-line Services PMI and ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI data, attention will now shift towards the FOMC meeting minutes overnight Thursday. Stock-wise, we favour Amazon (AMZN), supported by its USD496bn AWS-related backlog and USD220bn 2026 CapEx outlook as it aggressively expands AI data-centre capacity amid strong cloud and AI demand. This should also benefit Astera Labs (ALAB), given its exposure to AWS's next-generation Trainium infrastructure through its Aries Retimers and Scorpio Smart Fabric Switches. Hence, AMZN's aggressive data-centre expansion should provide a strong demand tailwind for ALAB. Lastly, investors could also look at Arista Networks (ANET), supported by the rollout of its next-generation 1.6Tb networking platform for AI infrastructure. MY: Locally, we expect investors to remain selective ahead of the Budget 2027 announcement, with attention centred on potential beneficiary sectors. M&E players could continue to see buying interest, supported by the government's emphasis on AI infrastructure and TNB's 500kV National Grid Backbone project, favouring companies such as MNHLDG, SGCBHD and POWERWELL. Efforts to reduce non- revenue water could also remain in focus, potentially benefiting companies such as ISF and RANHILL. Lastly, 99SMART could see renewed buying interest on expectations of higher consumer assistance allocations under SARA and STR. Despite the rebound yesterday, the FBMKLCI is still trading below the MA lines, with technical indicators showing weak signals as the MACD histogram continued to hover in the negative territory while the RSI is oversold. Key resistance is pegged at 1,646-1,651, while support is seen at 1,611-1,616. Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook told reporters that the suspension of Zetrix AI Bhd (ZETRIX) and subsidiary MyEG stemmed from RM314m in unremitted Road Transport Department collections from May to September. The collections should have been transferred daily within one working day of each transaction. The company issued a RM231m cheque to clear earlier arrears but the payment failed on Sept 30 after it instructed the bank not to process it. Following Loke's press conference, Zetrix AI issued a statement vowing to settle the dues to the government, and that it had submitted a proposal to resolve the issue. (The Edge) eJamin, an online bail payment system operated by a unit of Practice Note 17 company Pertama Digital Bhd (PERTAMA), ran for five years without a formal contract, the Public Accounts Committee found. Bail funds were also deposited into a commercial bank account held by Dapat Vista Sdn Bhd, instead of the federal government's consolidated trust account, in contravention of the Federal Constitution and the Financial Procedure Act 1957. Dapat Vista is 80% owned by Television Airtime Services Sdn Bhd, a 51%-owned subsidiary of Pertama Digital. The remaining 20% is held by the technology outfit HeiTech Padu Bhd (HTPADU). The bail deposit balance stood at RM193.71m as at end-2024. However, the committee discovered that only RM62.3m was held in bank accounts with the remaining RM130.8m invested by Dapat Vista in instruments including sukuk, without government approval or legal authority. The investment allowed Dapat Vista to earn RM4m to RM5m in interest, which the company regarded as "service income". (The Edge) Yinson Holdings Bhd (YINSON) has secured about US$600m (RM2.5bn) in additional firm contract backlog following an amendment to its contract for the FPSO John Agyekum Kufuor offshore of Ghana. title: 'Bursa Malaysia Gains on Wall Street Lead as Weak US Payrolls Temper Fed Rate Hike Expectations - MCI Group
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Monday, tracking Wall Street’s gains after softer US payroll growth eased expectations of an immediate Federal Reserve rate increase. At 9.10 am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 5.01 points, or 0.31 per cent, to 1,635.88 from last Friday’s close of 1,630.87. The index opened 2.55 points higher at 1,633.42. On the broader market, gainers surpassed losers 224 to 158, with 337 counters unchanged, 2,054 untraded and 24 suspended. Turnover stood at 206.30 million shares worth RM98.78 million. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the US 10-year yield remained elevated at 5.28 per cent and Brent crude oil settled at US$102.25 per barrel, keeping sentiment sensitive to interest rates and West Asia developments. “Over in Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index slipped below 24,000 as financial and technology shares weakened. “Back home, following FBM KLCI’s higher close last Friday, we anticipate tentative stabilisation within 1,625-1,635 today, with bargain hunting offering some support amid a cautious market undertone,” he told Bernama. Among the heavyweights, Maybank, Public Bank, CIMB and Tenaga Nasional gained four sen each to RM10.06, RN4.70, RM7.69, and RM13.00, while IHH Healthcare decreased six sen to RM7.74. In active trade, VS Industry added three sen to 32 sen, Notion VTec increased four sen to 74.5 sen, GB Bond inched up half-a-sen to 23.5 sen, SFP Tech gained a sen to 28.5 sen, while Dagang NeXchange was flat at 51.5 sen. Among the top gainers, Samaiden put on 19 sen to RM3.03, UWC was 16 sen firmer at RM7.73, Critical Holdings perked up 15 sen to RM2.61, Mi Technovation strengthened nine sen to RM5.30, and Solarvest advanced eight sen to RM4.25. Nestle led the decliners, falling 32 sen to RM89.20, while Vitrox eased 14 sen to RM10.32, Kobay Technology was 12 sen lower at RM2.18, Kelington shed five sen to RM8.58, and YTL Power International edged down four sen to RM5.64. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index gained 28.14 points to 17,510.07, the FBM Emas Index appreciated 33.81 points to 12,204.38, the FBM Top 100 Index widened 32.24 points to 11,989.92, the FBM Emas Shariah Index advanced 22.28 points to 12,082.60, and the FBM ACE Index improved 31.41 points to 5,560.87. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index inched up 0.59 of-a-point to 179.11, the Energy Index gained 2.57 points to 835.60, the Financial Services Index jumped 97.59 points to 19,138.10, and the Plantation Index gained 2.23 points to 9,058.78.

title: 'Banking Sector - FBM KLCI 50: Lower Bank Weight, Limited Passive Impact
body: 'The FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) will expand from 30 to 50 constituents in December, reflecting the significant growth in Bursa Malaysia's market capitalisation and the broader depth of its listed universe. While the FBM KLCI remains the country's flagship equity benchmark, its current 30 constituents represent only about 60% of the market's total capitalisation, below the approximately 70% coverage typically achieved by major global large-cap indices. The expansion aims to provide a broader representation of the Malaysian equity market while enhancing sector diversification through greater exposure to Technology, Energy and Industrials. To facilitate a smooth transition and minimise potential market disruption, the 20 additional constituents will be introduced in two stages. In the first phase, effective 21 December 2026, the new entrants will be included at 50% of their eventual index weights. The selection cut-off date will be 23 November 2026, with the final list of constituents announced on 3 December 2026. The second phase, effective 21 June 2027, will increase these constituents to their full index weights, completing the transition. Concurrently, the FBM Mid 70 Index will be streamlined to 50 constituents and rebranded as the FBM Mid Cap Index, while the overall FBM Top 100 Index universe remains unchanged at 100 stocks. The expansion is expected to create a more diversified and less concentrated benchmark. Based on market data as at 30 June 2026, the weight of the largest constituent is projected to decline from 13.2% to approximately 11.1% upon completion of Phase 2. Similarly, the combined weighting of the top five constituents is expected to fall from 50.0% to 42.1%, while the top 10 stocks will account for 57.2% of the index versus 67.9% under the current composition. The expanded FBM KLCI will also better represent non-financial sectors. Technology stocks will enter the benchmark for the first time, with an estimated 2.4% weighting upon full implementation. Industrials is expected to increase from 6.2% to 9.1%, Consumer Discretionary from 0.9% to 2.9%, Real Estate from 3.1% to 4.0%, and Energy from 1.0% to 2.0%. For the banking sector, the key implication is a structural dilution in index representation rather than a change in fundamentals. Financials' weighting is expected to decline from 42.7% currently to 39.4% in Phase 1 and 36.6% after Phase 2 is completed. In contrast, financial stocks will be more represented in the revamped FBM Mid Cap Index, with the sector's weighting projected to increase from 8.8% to 14.3%. In this report, we assess the implications of the FBM KLCI expansion for financial stocks and the broader banking sector. The reduction in Financials' index weight could result in passive selling of existing banking constituents. However, we believe the actual flow impact should remain modest given the relatively small pool of assets tracking the FBM KLCI. Based on our estimate of approximately RM3.0bn in KLCI-tracking passive assets under management (AUM), we estimate gross passive selling of around RM202mn across the six existing banking constituents, partly offset by around RM22mn of potential passive buying into Alliance Bank if it is included in the expanded benchmark. This would result in net estimated passive outflows of approximately RM180mn from the seven affected banking stocks. Importantly, the estimated RM180mn net outflow represents only around 0.06% of the combined free-float market capitalisation of approximately RM280bn across the seven affected banks. This suggests that the headline reduction in the Financials weighting is unlikely to translate into material selling pressure on banking stocks. Rather, we view the rebalancing primarily as a potential source of temporary stock-specific volatility and portfolio repositioning around the implementation dates. The relatively modest flow impact is also supported by the phased implementation. Assuming the RM3.0bn passive AUM and underlying index weights remain unchanged, approximately half of the estimated flow would occur during Phase 1 in December 2026, with the remaining adjustment taking place when the new constituents reach their full weights in June 2027. This should reduce the immediate impact of the rebalancing on banking stocks. While we estimate KLCI-tracking passive AUM at approximately RM3.0bn, the actual pool could differ depending on how much is benchmarked to the index. To assess the sensitivity of our conclusion, we estimate the potential net banking-sector outflows under different passive AUM assumptions Even under a higher RM5.0bn passive-AUM assumption, estimated net selling would amount to approximately RM300mn, equivalent to only around 0.1% of the combined free-float market capitalisation of the affected banks. As such, we believe the conclusion that the index expansion represents a relatively modest direct flow event remains intact across a reasonable range of passive-AUM assumptions. Alliance Bank has been identified as one of the 20 indicative candidates for inclusion in the expanded FBM KLCI. If selected, we estimate that the bank could receive approximately RM21.8mn of incremental passive demand based on its potential 0.73% increase in index weighting and our RM3.0bn passive-AUM assumption. We believe the potential index inclusion provides an additional technical catalyst to an already supportive fundamental investment case. Alliance Bank's gross loans expanded by 9.5% YoY, significantly above the industry average of around 5%, supporting continued market-share gains. Asset quality also strengthened, with net credit cost falling to 0.3bps from 14.4bps a year ago, driven largely by recoveries from its corporate portfolio. Its 37.7% CASA ratio provides a relatively stable and low-cost funding base, which should help the bank manage ongoing deposit repricing pressures and preserve NIM. Hence, Alliance Bank offers both a fundamental and technical catalyst - stronger-than-industry loan growth and asset quality on the one hand, and potential incremental demand from KLCItracking passive funds on the other. If confirmed as an index constituent, greater benchmark visibility could also increase its relevance among institutional investors. With the estimated index-related flows relatively small, we believe earnings delivery, NIM trends, credit costs and capital returns will remain the key determinants of banking-sector valuations. The sector continues to benefit from steady loan growth, resilient non-interest income, sound asset quality, and healthy capital and liquidity buffers. We forecast sector earnings growth of 4.8% in CY26 and 5.1% in CY27, while average return on equity is expected to remain stable at approximately 10.2%-10.3%. Malaysian banks also remain a key source of dividend yield, with sector dividend yields expected to increase from an average of 4.8% in CY25 to 5.2% in CY26 and 5.4% in CY27. Against this backdrop, we view the FBM KLCI expansion primarily as a technical and portfoliopositioning event rather than a fundamental negative for the banking sector. While several largecap banks could experience modest passive selling, we believe the magnitude of these flows is insufficient to materially alter the sector's valuation outlook. Instead, share-price performance should continue to be driven predominantly by earnings growth, NIM trends, credit costs, dividend expectations and valuation. We maintain our NEUTRAL stance on the banking sector. The expansion of the FBM KLCI will structurally reduce Financials' representation from 42.7% to 36.6% upon full implementation, creating some passive selling pressure across existing large-cap banking constituents. However, based on our estimated RM3.0bn KLCI-tracking passive AUM, the resulting net outflow of approximately RM180mn appears modest relative to the banks' free-float market capitalisation. The two-phase implementation should further limit the immediate impact, with the index changes spread across December 2026 and June 2027. We therefore expect any flow-driven volatility to be temporary and stock-specific rather than a material sector-wide liquidity event. We reiterate our HOLD calls on CIMB and Hong Leong Bank, while maintaining our BUY recommendations on Alliance Bank and Affin Bank. We upgrade Public Bank, RHB Bank, AMMB, and Maybank to BUY from hold, as recent share price weakness has created a more compelling risk-reward opportunity. Our preferred exposure remains Alliance Bank, supported by its industry-leading loan growth, improving asset quality and resilient funding profile. Its potential inclusion in the expanded FBM KLCI provides an additional technical catalyst. Key downside risks to our sector outlook include further NIM compression, potential deterioration in asset quality and slower-than-expected loan growth. These risks could be exacerbated by escalating geopolitical tensions, weaker economic activity and softer business sentiment, which may weigh on credit demand and earnings growth across the sector. title: 'A Reformasi government that arrests reformasi activists?
body: 'Kua Kia Soong Malaysia now has a Reformasi government arresting Reformasi activists. On 22 September, Amir Hariri Abdul Hadi, executive director of youth-led NGO Mandiri, and Dobby Chew, its finance director, were arrested under the anti-money-laundering law Amla after voluntarily presenting themselves to police to assist an investigation. They were remanded for three days and released on 24 September. Police say the investigation concerns suspected unlawful funds and that five bank accounts have been frozen. No, they are not podcasters. The podcasters came earlier. On 6 August, Brian Kong of Let’s Get It Podcast and Shamsul Saad of The Gut Shot Podcast were arrested and remanded for two days over an episode ‘Malaysia introduced me to racism’, which police said raised racial and religious sensitivities. They were investigated under the Sedition Act, Penal Code and Communications and Multimedia Act. So here we are. Activists arrested. Podcasters arrested. Human rights defenders investigated. Civil society bank accounts frozen. And this is supposed to be the government born of Reformasi. Perhaps the slogan has undergone a little institutional reform itself: - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Reformasi – formerly a movement against the machinery of repression. Reformasi 2.0 – now operating the machinery. The joke would be complete if the government announced that the next Reformasi rally will be held at the nearest police lock-up. The question for the former reformers This is where I would particularly like to hear from those who once stood on the other side of the barricades. Adam Adli was a student activist who became a symbol of youthful dissent before entering government. He is now deputy higher education minister. Fahmi Fadzil, once associated with the Reformasi generation, is now communications minister – the very portfolio intimately connected with freedom of expression and the regulation of online speech. Parliament records him as the minister responsible for the communications and multimedia legislation. So, gentlemen, a simple question: Where are your red lines? Is there a point at which the arrest of activists becomes unacceptable? A point at which the detention of journalists or podcasters becomes intolerable? A point at which laws inherited from the old order are used so aggressively that you say: “Enough. This is not the Reformasi we fought for”? And if that point exists, what is it? Is there a line beyond which you would resign in protest rather than remain in office and defend the indefensible? Or has entering government produced a miraculous transformation in political eyesight – where the handcuffs that once looked oppressive from the outside suddenly look perfectly reasonable from the inside? This is not a question about party loyalty. It is a question of principle. The great Reformasi rinse cycle Malaysia has seen this movie before. First comes the noble language: Reform. Justice. Democracy. Freedom. Rule of law. Then comes power. Then comes the discovery that the laws used against one’s opponents are actually rather useful. And finally comes the most beautiful phrase in the administrative vocabulary: “Let the authorities do their job.” Of course, the authorities must investigate genuine criminal allegations. But democracy requires another job to be done as well: the government must restrain the machinery of the state when that machinery threatens legitimate civil society, freedom of expression and political dissent. The UN special rapporteur on human rights defenders has already urged the Malaysian authorities to halt measures that misuse anti-money-laundering or anti-terrorism laws to harass or unduly restrict human rights defenders. Several international rights organisations likewise raised due process and chilling effect concerns over the crackdow on Mandiri and Hayat. These are not trivial questions. In a democracy, remand is not conviction. But deprivation of liberty is still deprivation of liberty. Perhaps the greatest irony is that many of today’s government politicians once understood this perfectly. They knew that democracy was not simply about winning elections. They knew that civil society had to be free to criticise the government. They knew that dissent was not treason. They knew that activists were not enemies of the state. So what happened? Did Reformasi finally succeed – only to discover that the former rebels had become the establishment? Or did the establishment simply swallow Reformasi whole? There is an old political warning: Power does not necessarily corrupt. Sometimes it merely reveals whether your principles were conditional on not having power. That is why the question to the former Reformasi activists now in government is so simple: What are your red lines? If an activist is arrested, what will make you speak? If a podcaster is detained, what will make you act? If freedom of expression is curtailed, what will make you resign? If the laws once used against you are now being used against the next generation of activists, how many arrests will it take before you say: “This is no longer Reformasi”? If there are no red lines, perhaps Malaysians should stop calling this a Reformasi government. Perhaps it is simply another government that has discovered the comfortable side of power. And perhaps the most appropriate Reformasi slogan for Malaysia in 2026 is: ‘Reformasi – please report to the lock-up.’ Dr Kua Kia Soong, a former MP, is the director of human rights group Suaram. title: 'UOB Malaysia, RHB Banking and Maybank execute landmark MYOR-based transaction
body: 'PETALING JAYA: UOB Malaysia, RHB Banking Group and Malayan Banking (Maybank) recently executed the first Malaysia Overnight Rate-based three-month interbank money market transaction in the country, incorporating a two-day lookback calculation convention through an interbank money market broker. The landmark transaction was anchored by UOB Malaysia and executed with RHB and Maybank, marking a significant milestone in the evolution of Malaysia’s money market and supporting industry efforts towards the adoption of risk-free rate-based market conventions. The transaction enhances transparency and price discovery by making funding levels and spreads visible to a broader network of market participants. This contrasts with bilateral transactions, where pricing information is limited to the counterparties involved. By helping establish a transparent Malaysia Overnight Rate (MYOR) funding curve and an observable reference point for three-month interbank funding, the transaction improves visibility into funding spreads over MYOR and banks’ cost of borrowing, supporting more efficient pricing across the wider market. UOB Malayia corporate and investment banking country head Christina Cheah said, “The successful execution of this money market transaction reflects the strong collaboration between UOB Malaysia, RHB and Maybank in supporting the evolution of the country’s financial markets. By establishing a transparent benchmark for MYOR-based funding, we are contributing to greater price discovery and helping to build confidence in the adoption of risk-free rate conventions. “As a leading foreign bank in the country, UOB Malaysia remains committed to partnering local market participants, sharing regional expertise and supporting initiatives that strengthen market resilience and align the domestic financial ecosystem with global standards.” The transaction references MYOR compounded in arrears with a two-day lookback mechanism, providing operational certainty in interest calculations while remaining anchored to actual market transactions. RHB Banking Group wholesale banking managing director Nurjesmi Mohd Nashir said, “This transaction demonstrates how market participants can work together to put MYOR-based conventions into practice and support the continued development of Malaysia’s money market. “As the industry progresses towards the transition from KLIBOR to MYOR, it is important that we build practical market experience and develop conventions that can be adopted more widely. RHB is committed to supporting Bank Negara Malaysia’s efforts to develop a deeper and more efficient MYOR market, and to playing an active role in the continued development of Malaysia’s financial markets.” Farid Kairi, deputy group CEO of global banking and managing director of global markets said: “Maybank is pleased to have played an integral role in this inaugural MYOR-based money market transaction. It marks an important first step in establishing the foundation for deeper liquidity, while setting the stage for widening the aperture for more MYOR-linked solutions and supporting robust price discovery for market participants. “This achievement reflects the collective efforts of industry participants and Bank Negara Malaysia in strengthening Malaysia’s financial market infrastructure.” Bank Negara Malaysia introduced MYOR in September 2021 as Malaysia’s Alternative Reference Rate (ARR). MYOR is calculated as the volume-weighted average rate of actual unsecured overnight ringgit interbank transactions, providing a robust benchmark grounded in deep and liquid overnight funding markets. The transition towards MYOR aligns Malaysia with other major financial markets that have adopted overnight risk-free rates including Singapore, Japan, Switzerland, the United States and the United Kingdom.

title: 'New Hilux catches fire after 40 days, son and mother awarded RM427,000
body: 'KUALA KUBU BARU: The Sessions Court has awarded more than RM427,000 in damages to a man and his mother after their new Toyota Hilux caught fire 40 days after it was registered, with the blaze spreading to their house.   Judge Norhayati Johar found that the fire was caused by electrical arcing at the vehicle's battery terminal connection and ruled that the Hilux did not meet the safety, durability and quality reasonably expected of a new vehicle.   She ruled in favour of plaintiffs V. Thiagarajan and V.C. Kamalam in their suit against Maybank Islamic Bhd and Toyota dealer Telagamas Motors Sdn Bhd.

title: 'High Court Dissolves Genneva, Paving Way for Victims to Settle Claims
body: 'SHAH ALAM (Sept 30): Genneva Sdn Bhd, the company behind a massive gold investment scam, has been wound up by the High Court here, which could see victims recouping their losses. In her brief judgment on Wednesday, judge Wan Fadhilah Nor Wan Idris found that the company, which had been convicted for unlawful deposit-taking, had lost its foundation as it had ceased operations for many years and lacked the licences and permits to resume its original business. The court also noted the deficiencies in its records and that the company did not have a functioning board of directors. The court granted the winding-up order and confirmed interim liquidator Wong Weng Foo to his role in dissolving the firm. Ng Wan Yee, who holds a major stake of 750,000 shares in the company, had moved to wind up the company in August 2024, to prevent other company directors from removing more than RM21 million in released company assets. The move follows a Sessions Court order on June 28, 2024, that revoked seizure orders under anti-money laundering laws on millions of ringgit and approximately 28.3kg of gold bars. In her petition, Wan Yee said there was a "high likelihood" that functional directors or other relevant parties might dissipate these assets for personal benefit rather than settling claims of thousands of investors. She claimed that some directors had already attempted to "siphon monies" under the guise of paying professional fees. An opposing creditor, Liew Chio Chuan, a 25% shareholder of Genneva, had challenged the appointment of Wong, arguing there was "material non-disclosure" by Wan Yee and that there was "no real danger" of assets being lost before a formal hearing before the court. Central to the dispute was the movement of funds just days before the petition was filed. Records show that following the release of the seizure orders, Genneva's directors had authorised the transfer of RM11,659,661.20 from accounts at Maybank and Public Bank to a stakeholder account held by the company’s long-time solicitors, Messrs Gooi & Azura. The solicitors and Maybank have justified the transfers, citing a board resolution dated June 26, 2024, and "letters of authorisation" dating back to 2016. They maintain the bank was unaware of the pending winding-up petition at the time. Genneva and its top executives were found guilty in August 2020 of illegally taking tens of million in deposits. The company was fined RM450 million and various executives were also jailed and slapped with fines amounting to hundreds of millions of ringgit. Former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad launched Genneva's "syariah-compliant" gold trading scheme on Dec 15, 2010. title: 'Foreign investors flee as KLCI slides 2.44pct
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Foreign investors stepped up their selling of Malaysian equities last week, while local institutions and retail investors increased their buying, as the FBM KLCI fell 2.44 per cent week-on-week (WoW) to 1,630.87 points. According to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd, foreign investors remained net sellers for a second consecutive week, with net outflows rising 65 per cent WoW to RM791.5 million from RM479.6 million previously. This brought their year-to-date (YTD) net outflow to RM6.71 billion. The heavier foreign selling came amid a worsening global bond sell-off, with US Treasury yields climbing to multi-decade highs. The 30-year US Treasury yield rose above 5.6 per cent, while the 10-year yield reached 5.34 per cent, with both at their highest levels since 2002. Selling also spread across global bond markets, while the Indonesian rupiah weakened past Rp18,000 to the US dollar as higher yields, oil prices and geopolitical tensions pressured Asian currencies. However, the International Monetary Fund said global bond markets continued to function in an orderly manner. Local institutional investors turned net buyers last week, recording RM301.2 million in net inflows, although this was 18 per cent lower WoW. Their YTD net buying position rose to RM4.35 billion. Local retail investors remained net buyers, with their net buying rising 4.44 times WoW to RM440.1 million, bringing their YTD net buying position to RM1.52 billion. Proprietary investors also remained net buyers, with net buying rising to RM50.2 million from RM13.8 million previously, lifting their YTD net buying position to RM839 million. At the sector level, foreign selling was concentrated in financial services and healthcare, with net outflows of RM367.1 million and RM173 million, respectively. Foreign buying was concentrated in technology and energy, which recorded net inflows of RM92.9 million and RM55.1 million, respectively. Their top net sells were Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB), Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) and Sunway Healthcare Group Bhd, while their top net buys were Southern Cable Group Bhd, Gamuda Bhd and Vitrox Corp Bhd. Domestic institutional investors focused their buying on utilities, construction and plantations, which recorded net inflows of RM252.1 million, RM182.8 million and RM111.7 million respectively. Their net selling was concentrated in technology, property and financial services, with outflows of RM89.5 million, RM75.7 million and RM53.3 million, respectively. Their top net buys were TNB, Gamuda and Sunmed, while their top net sells were Maybank, IOI Properties Group Bhd and MI Technovation Bhd. Retail investors' net buying was concentrated in financial services and property, with inflows of RM369.4 million and RM88.4 million, respectively. They were net sellers of construction and energy, with outflows of RM229 million and RM57.8 million, respectively. Their top net buys were Maybank, IOI Properties Group Bhd and RHB Bank Bhd, while their top net sells were Gamuda, Solavest Holdings Bhd and IJM Corp Bhd. Despite the broader market weakness, construction, real estate investment trusts (REITs) and technology were the top-performing sectors, while energy, property and industrial products underperformed. Average daily trading value was relatively unchanged WoW at RM2.9 billion. Meanwhile, Malaysia's Producer Price Index rose 10.7 per cent year-on-year in August 2026 from 9.7 per cent in July, driven by higher mining and manufacturing prices. Attention this week is expected to turn to the tabling of the 2027 budget on October 9, alongside developments surrounding a potential minimum wage adjustment and the Melaka state election. The Election Commission is scheduled to hold a special meeting on October 7 to determine key election arrangements, including the election writ, nomination and polling dates. CIMB Securities also highlighted geopolitical tensions, higher energy prices and El Niño as continuing global inflation risks. Three oil tankers were reportedly struck while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, while the US signalled the possibility of intensified military strikes against Iran and Saudi Arabia and reportedly prepared a new offensive against Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen.

Domestic institutional investors focused their buying on utilities, construction and plantations, which recorded net inflows of RM252.1 million, RM182.8 million and RM111.7 million respectively. Their net selling was concentrated in technology, property and financial services, with outflows of RM89.5 million, RM75.7 million and RM53.3 million, respectively. Their top net buys were TNB, Gamuda and Sunmed, while their top net sells were Maybank, IOI Properties Group Bhd and MI Technovation Bhd. Retail investors' net buying was concentrated in financial services and property, with inflows of RM369.4 million and RM88.4 million, respectively. They were net sellers of construction and energy, with outflows of RM229 million and RM57.8 million, respectively. Their top net buys were Maybank, IOI Properties Group Bhd and RHB Bank Bhd, while their top net sells were Gamuda, Solavest Holdings Bhd and IJM Corp Bhd. Despite the broader market weakness, construction, real estate investment trusts (REITs) and technology were the top-performing sectors, while energy, property and industrial products underperformed. Average daily trading value was relatively unchanged WoW at RM2.9 billion. Meanwhile, Malaysia's Producer Price Index rose 10.7 per cent year-on-year in August 2026 from 9.7 per cent in July, driven by higher mining and manufacturing prices. Attention this week is expected to turn to the tabling of the 2027 budget on October 9, alongside developments surrounding a potential minimum wage adjustment and the Melaka state election. The Election Commission is scheduled to hold a special meeting on October 7 to determine key election arrangements, including the election writ, nomination and polling dates. CIMB Securities also highlighted geopolitical tensions, higher energy prices and El Niño as continuing global inflation risks. Three oil tankers were reportedly struck while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, while the US signalled the possibility of intensified military strikes against Iran and Saudi Arabia and reportedly prepared a new offensive against Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen.

title: 'Maybank Turned Its Cash Back Card Perks Into A Playground At Mid Valley
body: 'Last week, we dropped by Mid Valley Megamall to check out the Maybank Cash Back Mastercard Platinum showcase. Held at Centre Court from 23 to 27 September, the five-day event had a little bit of everything, from interactive activities to a closer look at the card’s features.  Five Stops To Explore The Card  The showcase was set up like a stamp-card journey. We picked up a journey card at the start and worked our way through five stations. The first four were More To Discover, Stream For More, More To Enjoy and More To Unwind. Once we had collected all four stamps, we could head to the final stop, Maybank Cafe, and redeem either a ZUS Coffee or a Krispy Kreme doughnut.  The activities at each station were also designed around the card’s benefits. One had a touchscreen game where you had to catch groceries in a basket, a playful take on the card’s 8% cash back on digital lifestyle spending. There were also photo spots with airplane window backdrops featuring destinations like Singapore, Thailand, Japan and South Korea, which are among the countries where the card charges no foreign exchange mark-up fee.  Visitors who applied for the card on-site could unlock three additional activities. These included a Flight Simulator and a Merchandise Redemption station with goodies such as a Maybank tumbler and Lilo & Stitch tote bag. Applicants could also try their luck at a giant Gashapon machine for prizes including a Nintendo Switch 2, Setel vouchers and Grab vouchers.  Card Benefits At A Glance  The Event Has Ended, But You Can Still Win  If you missed the showcase, you can still catch Maybank’s upcoming contest for cardholders, which runs from 1 October to 31 December 2026.  You’ll earn entries by spending at least RM1,000 a month on the card, giving you a chance to win one of these prizes:  To find out more about the Maybank Cash Back Mastercard Platinum and see how it compares with other cashback cards, visit our credit card page.

title: 'From F1 to the World Cup: How Anwar is using sport as diplomacy to put Malaysia on the world stage - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s approach of leveraging sports as a platform for diplomacy, economic activity and nation branding is helping position Malaysia back on the global sporting stage, according to an analyst. Global Peace Institute, London senior fellow Prof Dr Mohd Mizan Mohammad Aslam said Malaysia had, in recent months, demonstrated how global sporting events could be used not only to entertain the public but also to strengthen international relationships, generate economic activity and create a sense of shared national excitement. “Sport is often treated as entertainment, but for governments it can also be diplomacy, economic policy and nation branding rolled into one,” he said in a statement today. Formula 1’s return to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after nine years and Malaysia’s efforts to ensure access to the 2026 Fifa World Cup broadcasts demonstrated how sports could be used to strengthen the country’s international engagement. Mohd Mizan said Malaysia’s hosting of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix from Oct 2–4 demonstrated the international dimension of sports diplomacy, after the Bahrain Grand Prix could not proceed at its original venue due to geopolitical conditions in West Asia. He said the arrangement went beyond a commercial transaction involving a racetrack, as it was facilitated within the wider relationship between Malaysia and Bahrain, with the support of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Bahrain’s King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa. Bahrain’s Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa also travelled to Malaysia and met Anwar during the race weekend. Mohd Mizan said Anwar’s attendance at the qualifying session at Sepang, visit to the Mercedes-AMG Petronas pit and participation in a reception hosted by Prince Salman further demonstrated how the sporting event created a platform for diplomatic engagement. “Sport had therefore created a diplomatic platform. Leaders met, bilateral relations were reinforced and Malaysia was placed before a global audience not through a formal summit but through one of the world’s most recognisable sporting spectacles,” he said. Mohd Mizan said the public response to F1’s return was equally significant, with around 95,000 three-day tickets sold by late September and SIC expecting sales to reach about 100,000, which would be the highest ticket sales recorded for races held at the circuit. He said the event also generated significant economic spillovers, with the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture estimating that it could draw around 300,000 tourists, including about 50,000 international visitors, while Hong Leong Bank Research projected an economic impact of approximately RM1.3 billion through sports tourism and foreign visitor spending. “Formula 1 does not benefit only the circuit. Visitors spend on hotels, restaurants, transport, retail and tourism. Television coverage carries images of Malaysia around the world. International teams, sponsors, journalists and corporate leaders arrive in the country,” he said. Turning to football, Mohd Mizan said the government’s decision to ensure Malaysians had access to the 2026 Fifa World Cup represented the domestic dimension of sports diplomacy, with football remaining one of the country’s most widely followed sports. RTM and Unifi TV were appointed official broadcasters, with all 104 matches made available through the participating platforms, while the government allocated RM26.2 million to secure the broadcasting rights and strategic cooperation with the private sector helped widen access and distribution, he said. Mohd Mizan also said that access to the World Cup through legitimate and accessible channels represented a form of social inclusion, as major sporting events could create shared experiences cutting across race, age, geography and income. “Few things temporarily dissolve Malaysia’s normal social divisions as effectively as sport. During major football tournaments, mamak restaurants, living rooms, community halls and public viewing areas become shared national spaces,” he said. He said Anwar’s approach showed that diplomacy today operated far beyond formal conference rooms, with Malaysia using F1 and Fifa to bring the world closer to its people while strengthening its position on the global sporting stage. “Sometimes diplomacy happens through bilateral negotiations. Sometimes it happens through football and sometimes, at 300 kilometres per hour around Sepang,” he said. — Bernama

title: '马股随隔夜美股反弹，但投资者仍保持谨慎，综指仅微幅收高
body: '马股周五随隔夜美股反弹，由于市场对美债收益率和油价的担忧挥之不去，投资者仍保持谨慎并采取选择性投资策略，综合指数收盘仅微幅走高。 截至下午闭市，综合指数涨0.51点或0.03%，至1,630.87点。 市场整体表现平衡，全场上涨股592只，下跌股554只，562只平盘，另1041只股无交易。全天成交量42.59亿股，总成交额27.11亿令吉。 综指成分股涨跌互见，IHH医疗保健集团（IHH，5225，主板保健股）涨10仙至7.80令吉，国油贸易（PETDAG，5681，主板能源股）、PPB集团（PPB，4065，主板消费股）和国油石化（PCHEM，5183，主板工业股）各涨8仙，分别收在19.20令吉、9.15令吉和4.21令吉。 下跌股，雀巢（NESTLE，4707，主板消费股）跌48仙至89.52令吉，吉隆坡甲洞（KLK，2445，主板种植股）跌42仙至21.00令吉，马国际船务（MISC，3816，主板交通与物流股）跌15仙至7.53令吉，国油气体（PETGAS，6033，主板公用事业股）跌12仙至17.20令吉。 银行股，马银行（MAYBANK，1155）涨7仙至10.02令吉，大众银行（PBBANK，1295）跌1仙4.66令吉，联昌国际（CIMB，1023）跌4仙至7.65令吉，兴业银行（RHBBANK，1066）跌4仙至7.43令吉，丰隆银行（HLBANK，5819）跌20仙至22.64令吉，大马银行（AMBANK，1015）持平于6.30令吉。 热门股方面，Zetrix AI（ZETRIX，0138，主板科技股）跌5仙至11.5仙，捷硕科技（JAKS，4723, 主板建筑股）持平于18仙，JCY国际（JCY，5161，主板科技股）涨10.5仙至66仙，威铖（VS，6963，主板工业股）涨2仙至29仙，迪耐（DNEX，4456，主板科技股）涨2仙至51.5仙。 其他重要股项，马太平洋（MPI，3867，主板科技股）涨1.28令吉至42.40令吉，UWC公司（UWC，5292，主板科技股）涨47仙至7.57令吉；ENRA集团（ENRA，8613，主板产业股）跌25.5仙至72.5仙，安联保险（ALLIANZ，1163，主板金融股）跌20仙至20.80令吉。 亚太主要股指，新加坡海峡时报指数跌 0.58% 至 5,634.83 点，香港恒生指数跌 2.60% 至 23,972.29 点，日本日经指255数跌 0.94% 至 68,309.46 点，韩国首尔综合指数起 0.46% 至 7,003.74 点。中国股市适逢国庆长假期休市。

title: 'CIMB Could Raise RM2 Bil Capital Return Commitment, Says MBSB Research
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) could potentially raise its RM2 billion capital return commitment to increase the chances of its share buyback programme garnering investor acceptance, according to MBSB Research. A higher capital-return commitment could help offset potential disappointment among investors who are expecting a larger portion of the RM2 billion to be returned via special dividends, the research house said. “To increase its chances of success, we think there is a likelihood of CIMB positively revising to the RM2.0 billion figure, and that CIMB is confident enough on its ability to garner sufficient capital before signalling to the market via share buybacks,” MBSB Research said in a note on Thursday. “We would not put it past CIMB’s management to pull off such a manoeuvre — they’ve surprised us positively multiple times in the past,” it added. MBSB Research noted that share buybacks have historically not been successful in Malaysia. CIMB’s share buybacks make up a portion of its RM2 billion capital return scheme, of which RM700 million has already been returned via special dividends. The primary purpose of the share buybacks is for CIMB to further drive its earnings per share, return on equity (ROE) and dividend per share figures, MBSB Research noted, particularly as the bank is slightly behind on its ROE target for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (FY2026). The research house noted CIMB has been buying back shares every day, tallying up to 20.76 million shares for RM163 million since Sept 21 thus far. CIMB’s share buyback programme is also being watched for its potential implications on other banks, according to MBSB Research. The research house described the programme as the first major share buyback scheme by a Malaysian bank for capital management purposes in many years, and said a successful outcome could encourage other large banks to consider similar measures. It listed Public Bank Bhd (KL:PBBANK) and RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK) as possible candidates. full_text: 'CIMB Could Raise RM2 Bil Capital Return Commitment, Says MBSB Research. 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) could potentially raise its RM2 billion capital return commitment to increase the chances of its share buyback programme garnering investor acceptance, according to MBSB Research. A higher capital-return commitment could help offset potential disappointment among investors who are expecting a larger portion of the RM2 billion to be returned via special dividends, the research house said. “To increase its chances of success, we think there is a likelihood of CIMB positively revising to the RM2.0 billion figure, and that CIMB is confident enough on its ability to garner sufficient capital before signalling to the market via share buybacks,” MBSB Research said in a note on Thursday. “We would not put it past CIMB’s management to pull off such a manoeuvre — they’ve surprised us positively multiple times in the past,” it added. MBSB Research noted that share buybacks have historically not been successful in Malaysia. CIMB’s share buybacks make up a portion of its RM2 billion capital return scheme, of which RM700 million has already been returned via special dividends. The primary purpose of the share buybacks is for CIMB to further drive its earnings per share, return on equity (ROE) and dividend per share figures, MBSB Research noted, particularly as the bank is slightly behind on its ROE target for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (FY2026). The research house noted CIMB has been buying back shares every day, tallying up to 20.76 million shares for RM163 million since Sept 21 thus far. CIMB’s share buyback programme is also being watched for its potential implications on other banks, according to MBSB Research. The research house described the programme as the first major share buyback scheme by a Malaysian bank for capital management purposes in many years, and said a successful outcome could encourage other large banks to consider similar measures. It listed Public Bank Bhd (KL:PBBANK) and RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK) as possible candidates. body: 'US: Trade deficit widens as imports hit record high. The US trade deficit widened more than expected in August as strong domestic demand drove imports to an all-time high, suggesting trade could again weigh on third-quarter economic growth despite higher tariffs. The deficit increased 13.7% to USD105.6bn, the largest since March 2025, compared with economists' expectations of USD102.0bn. (Reuters) EU: High yields may dampen energy inflation pass-through, ECB's Rehn says. Rapid energy inflation in the euro zone has yet to spread significantly into other goods and services, while higher bond yields could restrain growth and reduce the transmission of energy costs into broader prices and wages, ECB policymaker Olli Rehn said. Euro-zone inflation remains well above the ECB's 2% target, but policymakers are weighing persistent energy-driven price pressures against tighter financial conditions. Long-term yields have risen to more than decade highs amid higher US yields and European debt concerns. Financial markets currently price another two to three ECB rate increases during the tightening cycle, including around an 80% probability of a move by December. (Reuters) UK: High inflation has become embedded, BoE's Mann says. Inflation above the BoE's 2% target appears to have become embedded in the UK economy and could become further entrenched through wage negotiations early next year, BoE policymaker Catherine Mann said. Unlike the Fed and ECB, the BoE has kept rates unchanged since the outbreak of the Iran war, although markets now expect a rate increase in November. Mann highlighted the risk of inflation reaching around 4% near year-end, coinciding with the period when many employers negotiate annual pay increases. She said demand remained positive but not particularly strong, while businesses were adapting to elevated energy costs. (Reuters) China: Zinc exports surge as weak domestic demand leaves excess supply. China is on course to become a net exporter of refined zinc this year as soft domestic construction demand coincides with tight supply conditions in Western markets. Zinc exports jumped to 40,668 tonnes in August, the second-highest monthly level in almost two decades, while China recorded net exports of 4,388 tonnes during the first eight months of the year. Muted construction activity has weakened demand for galvanised steel, leaving Shanghai zinc inventories elevated, while an arbitrage opportunity created by tight London Metal Exchange supply has encouraged Chinese exports. (Reuters) Japan: BOJ signals readiness for further rate hikes to anchor inflation. BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda said it was becoming increasingly important to anchor underlying inflation around the central bank's 2% target, signalling readiness to continue raising interest rates to prevent inflation from overshooting. Economic and price developments remain broadly consistent with BOJ forecasts, while the Tankan survey points to solid business sentiment. Rising raw-material costs are feeding into wholesale and consumer inflation, while long-term inflation expectations continue to rise. Ueda also cited risks from the Iran war, strong AI-related demand and a weak yen, adding that financial conditions remain accommodative even after September's rate increase. (Reuters) India: Markets price RBI hike, with risk of larger move. The RBI could tighten monetary policy more aggressively than expected as policymakers face broadening price pressures and sharply higher global bond yields. The one-month overnight indexed swap was around 5.55%, about 30bps above the current 5.25% repo rate, implying a 25bps hike is fully priced in while leaving some probability of a 50bps increase. Most economists polled by Reuters expect a 25bps hike, which would be the RBI's first rate increase since early 2023. Bankers estimate markets may be assigning roughly a 25% probability to a larger move.(Reuters) CIMB (Outperform, TP: RM8.70): Considers selling Philippine business. CIMB Group Holdings is exploring a sale of its business in the Philippines as part of efforts to streamline and focus on bigger markets for growth, according to people with knowledge of the matter. (Bloomberg) Comments: According to Bloomberg, the deal could value the business at USD200m. While historically CIMB Philippine's contribution to the group is minimal and has swung into losses in 2025, we think that the potential sale is in-line with the group's strategy to redeploy capital into higher-return segments, which could potentially support ROE expansion. We maintain our Outperform call with an unchanged TP of RM8.70. Dialog (Neutral, TP: RM2.10): JV bags onshore O&G concession in Thailand. Dialog Group said its 50.01%-owned joint venture company has been awarded concession rights and operatorship for the L8/66 exploration block onshore Thailand. (The Edge) Comments: We view the L8/66 concession award positively, given its proximity to Dialog's producing L53/48 fields and the ability to leverage existing facilities and operating expertise to optimise development costs. The USD14.3m minimum work commitment over six years provides measured exposure to potential reserve and production growth, with management indicating a low-to-mid-teens projected IRR. However, we leave our earnings forecasts unchanged as the project remains at a preliminary stage. We maintain our Neutral call with an unchanged TP of RM2.10. Zetrix: Says still finalising amount owed to JPJ after Loke reveals RM314m arrears. Zetrix AI said the exact amount it owes the Road Transport Department (JPJ) is still being finalised between the two parties, a day after Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the company had accumulated RM314m in unpaid remittances. (The Edge) Samaiden: Reveals RM238m contract value for LSS5+ solar project. Samaiden Group said its contracts to undertake works for a 99.99-megawatt (MW) Large Scale Solar 5+ (LSS5+) project are worth RM238m. Samaiden's had on Oct 2 entered into a works contract and a contract for the supply of solar components with Syarikat Pembenaan Yeoh Tiong Lay SB (YTL Construction), the construction unit of YTL Corporation. (The Edge) Mesiniaga: Wins two-year RM32.3m contract extension from Customs Dept. Mesiniaga has won a RM32.3m contract from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMDC) for the maintenance and licence renewal of its MyGST System. The contract marks a continuation of the information technology product and service provider's earlier MyGST system agreement with RMCD that first started in Nov 2023. (The Edge) OCK: Taps Phu Quoc infrastructure opportunities. OCK Group has signed a tripartite in-principle agreement with Southern Star Telecommunication Equipment Joint Stock Company (SPN), a subsidiary of JTOWER, and Sun Phu Quoc, a subsidiary of Sun Group, to deploy telecommunications infrastructure across designated Sun Group projects in Phu Quoc. (StarBiz) The KLCI might open stronger today as the S&P 500 climbed 0.6% Tuesday to a record after topping its prior all-time high set in August. Despite worries about everything from war to high inflation to pressure from the bond market, the index at the heart of many 401(k) accounts has soared 23% since hitting a bottom in late March. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 253 points, or 0.5%, while the Nasdaq composite tacked 0.4% onto its own all-time high set the day before. The record-high stock prices are helping investors feel better about their finances, or at least less bad, when Americans are generally feeling discouraged about keeping up with the fast-rising cost of living. Many of the fears that sent the US stock market to its bottom in March have indeed come true. Oil prices are high because of the war with Iran, which has made inflation worse. Yields have cranked higher in the bond market, which threatens to slow the economy by making it more expensive for everyone to borrow money. And Americans broadly say they're feeling more pessimistic about the economy and where it's heading. But one vital source of support has remained resolute for the US stock market throughout: the relentless ability for companies to make more money. AI stocks have been a huge force driving the US market to records, including Nvidia's 28.3% surge so far this year. That's roughly double the broad market's gain. Constellation Energy jumped 12.2% for one of Tuesday's biggest gains in the S&P 500 because it's also riding that rising tide. Bond yields offered some slack on Tuesday after falling back from their highest levels in years or even decades. The yield on the 10-year Treasury, which is the focal point of the US bond market, eased to 5.28% from 5.31% late Monday. It fell after oil prices steadied themselves somewhat. The price for a barrel of Brent crude oil, the international standard, dropped to roughly $97 in the morning before pulling back to settle at $100.58. While that was up 0.3% from Monday's settlement price, it's still below the nearly $110 it was at a few weeks ago. In stock markets abroad, indices ticked higher in Europe as yields continue to swing in their bond markets amid concerns about high government debts and tight budgets. In France, tens of thousands of demonstrators marched in support of protests by students demanding more funding for schools. In Asia, Japan's Nikkei 225 jumped 1.1%, and Hong Kong's Hang Seng climbed 1%, but South Korea's Kospi dropped 0.9%. Back home, the KLCI added 1.6 points or 0.1% to 1,633.35. title: '[VIDEO] ‘Baru Hendak Tulis Muka Surat Pertama’ – Syed Saddiq & Bella Astillah Akui Tak Layak Disamakan Dengan Tun M & Allahyarhamah Tun Hasmah
body: 'Ahli Parlimen Muar, Syed Saddiq dan bakal isterinya, Bella Astillah tidak bersetuju dengan kenyataan yang menyamakan kisah cinta mereka dengan pasangan negarawan, Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad dan Allahyarhamah Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali. Artikel Berkaitan: Bella Astillah Kongsi Keadaan Syed Saddiq – ‘Dia Tak Mampu Teruskan Apa Yang Telah Dirancang Hari Ini’ Artikel Berkaitan: [VIDEO] ‘Berdebar? Tidak, Saya Gembira’ – Syed Saddiq Tak layak disamakan Dalam satu sesi temu bual, Saddiq menegaskan perbandingan itu terlalu jauh, malah merasakan mereka tidak layak apabila persamaan tersebut dibuat. Saya rasa kami tidak layak untuk dibandingkan dengan Allahyarhamah dan juga Tun Dr. Mahathir. Tidak dekat pun, malah tidak sampai satu peratus kerana kalau kita lihat jasa mereka, ia memang luar biasa. Saddiq berkata demikian pada sidang media Walimatulurus Bella Astillah & Syed Saddiq di Kuala Lumpur pada Jumaat. Mengulas lebih lanjut, Saddiq berkata Allahyarhamah Tun Dr Siti Hasmah merupakan tokoh yang wajar dicontohi khususnya dalam bidang perubatan. Tun Dr Siti Hasmah salah seorang doktor wanita terawal yang memberikan inspirasi kepada wanita. Beliau satu-satunya doktor wanita dalam kelompoknya ketika itu di Singapura dan mendapat biasiswa. Bila pulang untuk berkhidmat, pada awalnya beliau berada di kota, tetapi apabila diberikan ujian dan cabaran untuk dihantar ke kawasan luar bandar, beliau tidak mengeluh. Beliau pergi membantu dan mendidik keluarga serta anak-anak di sana untuk menerima pendidikan moden. Beliau adalah antara yang terawal dan perintis. Sementara itu, Saddiq menyifatkan Tun Mahathir sebagai tokoh yang banyak memberi sumbangan kepada negara. Tun Dr Mahathir lagilah. Saya rasa saya tidak perlu menyenaraikan satu per satu pencapaian dan jasa beliau kepada negara yang sehingga hari ini kita masih menerima manfaatnya. Jadi, sejujurnya, bagi mereka yang berkongsikan perkara ini, saya tahu ia datang daripada niat yang baik. Tetapi jawapan kami, kita tidak layak untuk disamakan kerana mereka jauh lebih ke hadapan daripada kami. Kata Saddiq, kisah percintaan mereka juga tidak setara untuk disamakan dengan pasangan negarawan itu memandangkan ikatan hubungan mereka sedang dibina dan masih berada di peringkat awal. Saya tahu mungkin ada yang kata, ‘Oh, tetapi bukan daripada sudut sumbangan kepada negara, mungkin daripada sudut cinta.’ Itu pun saya rasa kami tidak layak. Kerana kami ini baru hendak berkahwin, hendak menghalalkan hubungan. Mereka ini sudah 70 tahun meraikan cinta dan kebijaksanaan bersama. Kami belum sampai pun 25 tahun, baru hendak membuka bab atau buku yang pertama. Kalau kita ibaratkan seperti sebuah buku, kami baru hendak menulis muka surat pertama. Mereka bukan sekadar menulis muka surat pertama, mungkin mereka sudah mempunyai perpustakaan sendiri yang boleh berkongsikan kisah cinta mereka. Bukan satu buku, tetapi sudah beribu-ribu buku. Dalam perkembangan lain, Saddiq dan Bella akan disatukan sebagai suami isteri pada sebuah majlis di Kuala Lumpur pada 10 Oktober depan. Majlis pernikahan mereka akan berlangsung di aras 118, Menara Merdeka Maybank dengan konsep serba putih disulami elemen Arab atau Islamik atas permintaan keluarga. Saya rasa kami tidak layak untuk dibandingkan dengan Allahyarhamah dan juga Tun Dr. Mahathir. Tidak dekat pun, malah tidak sampai satu peratus kerana kalau kita lihat jasa mereka, ia memang luar biasa. Saddiq berkata demikian pada sidang media Walimatulurus Bella Astillah & Syed Saddiq di Kuala Lumpur pada Jumaat. Mengulas lebih lanjut, Saddiq berkata Allahyarhamah Tun Dr Siti Hasmah merupakan tokoh yang wajar dicontohi khususnya dalam bidang perubatan. Tun Dr Siti Hasmah salah seorang doktor wanita terawal yang memberikan inspirasi kepada wanita. Beliau satu-satunya doktor wanita dalam kelompoknya ketika itu di Singapura dan mendapat biasiswa. Bila pulang untuk berkhidmat, pada awalnya beliau berada di kota, tetapi apabila diberikan ujian dan cabaran untuk dihantar ke kawasan luar bandar, beliau tidak mengeluh. Beliau pergi membantu dan mendidik keluarga serta anak-anak di sana untuk menerima pendidikan moden. Beliau adalah antara yang terawal dan perintis. Sementara itu, Saddiq menyifatkan Tun Mahathir sebagai tokoh yang banyak memberi sumbangan kepada negara. Tun Dr Mahathir lagilah. Saya rasa saya tidak perlu menyenaraikan satu per satu pencapaian dan jasa beliau kepada negara yang sehingga hari ini kita masih menerima manfaatnya. Jadi, sejujurnya, bagi mereka yang berkongsikan perkara ini, saya tahu ia datang daripada niat yang baik. Tetapi jawapan kami, kita tidak layak untuk disamakan kerana mereka jauh lebih ke hadapan daripada kami. Kata Saddiq, kisah percintaan mereka juga tidak setara untuk disamakan dengan pasangan negarawan itu memandangkan ikatan hubungan mereka sedang dibina dan masih berada di peringkat awal. Saya tahu mungkin ada yang kata, ‘Oh, tetapi bukan daripada sudut sumbangan kepada negara, mungkin daripada sudut cinta.’ Itu pun saya rasa kami tidak layak. Kerana kami ini baru hendak berkahwin, hendak menghalalkan hubungan. Mereka ini sudah 70 tahun meraikan cinta dan kebijaksanaan bersama. Kami belum sampai pun 25 tahun, baru hendak membuka bab atau buku yang pertama. Kalau kita ibaratkan seperti sebuah buku, kami baru hendak menulis muka surat pertama. Mereka bukan sekadar menulis muka surat pertama, mungkin mereka sudah mempunyai perpustakaan sendiri yang boleh berkongsikan kisah cinta mereka. Bukan satu buku, tetapi sudah beribu-ribu buku. Dalam perkembangan lain, Saddiq dan Bella akan disatukan sebagai suami isteri pada sebuah majlis di Kuala Lumpur pada 10 Oktober depan. Majlis pernikahan mereka akan berlangsung di aras 118, Menara Merdeka Maybank dengan konsep serba putih disulami elemen Arab atau Islamik atas permintaan keluarga. body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Malayan Banking Bhd (KL: MAYBANK) fell below RM10 for the first time in nearly nine months and banking stocks mostly declined on Thursday amid rising bond yields.  Higher yields generally hurt banks as they take larger paper losses from lower prices of the bonds they hold, which eats into capital and forces them to book losses if they sell. Banks will also have to increase their rates to attract depositors, leading to higher funding costs.  That would weigh on banks’ near term non-interest income as well as their capital ratios, Affin Hwang Investment Bank flagged in a note on Thursday.  Maybank, the country’s top bank in terms of assets, fell for the third straight day and closed down 0.4% at RM9.95. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL: CIMB) and Hong Leong Bank Bhd (KL: HLBANK) each declined over 1%.  The Bursa Malaysia Financial Services Index, which also tracks non-bank firms such as insurers and stockbrokers, fell to its lowest level in 10 months.  The US Federal Reserve raised interest rate earlier this month for the first time in three years, sending the yield on the 10-year benchmark Malaysian Government Securities to as high as 4.18% before moderating.  A growing number of economists expect Bank Negara Malaysia to raise the overnight policy rate in November during the final scheduled monetary policy review for the year.  Rising yields tend to lead to higher corporate bond yields, which also tie-in to capital raising decisions both for banks and other corporates and subsequently, fee income to the banks, Affin Hwang said.  Maybank and Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd (KL: ABMB) have on their books the longest bond duration — the length of time for a bond to repay its cost in cash flows while also being a measure of sensitivity to changes in interest rates — according to the research house’s analysis.  Public Bank Bhd (KL: PBBANK) and Hong Leong Bank, meanwhile, have the shortest duration. In terms of capital ratios, Maybank, RHB Bank Bhd (KL: RHBBANK) and CIMB could see the largest drops, while Public Bank and Hong Leong Bank would see the least due to their portfolios’ shorter duration, the house added.

title: 'Dialog JV Bags Onshore O&G Concession in Thailand
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Dialog Group Bhd (KL:DIALOG) said its 50.01%-owned joint venture company has been awarded concession rights and operatorship for the L8/66 exploration block onshore Thailand. The joint venture company, Pan Orient Energy (Siam) Ltd (POES), was notified by the Thai government on Monday (Oct 5) that it had been awarded the concession following a joint bid with CanAsia Energy Corp in Thailand’s 25th Onshore Bid Round, according to Dialog's Bursa Malaysia filing on Tuesday. POES will operate the concession with a 70% participating interest, while Canada-listed CanAsia will hold the remaining 30% non-operating interest. The development of L8/66 carries a minimum work commitment of US$14.3 million (RM58.4 million). The award remains subject to the finalisation and execution of the concession agreement and the fulfilment of its conditions precedent, with physical work expected to begin immediately after the agreement is signed. POES is a joint venture between Dialog’s wholly-owned Pan Orient Petroleum Pte Ltd and Thailand-based Sea Oil Energy Ltd, which holds the remaining 49.99%. Dialog, through POES, already operates the producing L53/48 onshore concession in Thailand, which is adjacent to the L8/66 block. L8/66 was previously part of the L53/48 concession before being relinquished to the Thai government under concession terms requiring portions of undeveloped acreage to be surrendered over time. Dialog said the new block has similar geological characteristics to L53/48 and gives POES access to additional acreage surrounding its existing producing fields. “The award of Concession L8/66 to POES further strengthens Dialog’s upstream portfolio and creates operational synergies by leveraging on the group’s integrated technical services across its diversified business model,” the company said. "Dialog will remain focused and steadfast in the pursuit of diversification across the upstream, midstream and downstream energy sector as well as the sustainable and renewable sector, to strategically position the group to weather different economic and oil price cycles, which is in line with the group's strategy of generating long term recurring income," it added. For the financial year ended June 30, 2026 (FY2026), Dialog’s net profit surged 95.4% to RM593.55 million from RM303.83 million a year earlier, as revenue grew 15.3% to RM2.88 billion from RM2.5 billion. The stronger FY2026 performance was driven by positive contributions across the group’s businesses, particularly its Malaysian operations, while its international businesses also recorded higher profit contributions on increased sales of specialist products and services. Dialog proposed a final dividend of three sen per share, bringing its total dividend for FY2026 to 4.7 sen per share or about RM265.93 million. Dialog shares closed two sen or 1.08% higher at RM1.87 on Tuesday, valuing the group at RM10.56 billion. Year to date, the counter has gained over 6%. title: 'Pelabur asing jual RM799.9 juta ekuiti Bursa Malaysia untuk minggu kedua - MBSB Research - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 5 Okt – Pelabur asing terus mengurangkan pegangan dalam pasaran saham Malaysia apabila mencatatkan jualan bersih RM799.9 juta bagi minggu berakhir 2 Oktober 2026, menurut MBSB Research. Jualan bersih itu menjadikan aliran keluar dana asing di Bursa Malaysia berterusan untuk minggu kedua berturut-turut dengan pelabur asing menjadi penjual bersih pada kesemua lima hari dagangan sepanjang minggu berkenaan. “Jualan paling tinggi direkodkan pada Rabu sebanyak RM228.4 juta, diikuti Khamis RM187.9 juta, Selasa RM172.4 juta, Isnin RM142.1 juta dan Jumaat RM69.1 juta,” kata MBSB Research dalam nota kajiannya. Pelabur tempatan ambil peluang Berbeza dengan pelabur asing, institusi tempatan meneruskan trend pembelian bersih untuk minggu kedua berturut-turut dengan aliran masuk RM352.4 juta. Pelabur runcit pula meneruskan pembelian bersih bagi minggu keenam berturut-turut dengan jumlah aliran masuk sebanyak RM447.5 juta. Ini menunjukkan tekanan jualan daripada pelabur asing sebahagiannya diimbangi oleh penyertaan pelabur tempatan. Dari segi aktiviti dagangan, purata dagangan harian pelabur runcit meningkat 3.7%, manakala institusi tempatan susut 7.9%. Penyertaan pelabur asing pula meningkat 8.6%. Sektor teknologi, tenaga jadi pilihan pelabur asing Walaupun pelabur asing secara keseluruhan mencatatkan jualan bersih, terdapat beberapa sektor yang masih menerima aliran masuk dana. Sektor teknologi menerima aliran masuk asing tertinggi sebanyak RM131 juta, diikuti sektor tenaga sebanyak RM93.2 juta dan pembinaan sebanyak RM78.4 juta. Sebaliknya, sektor perkhidmatan kewangan mencatatkan aliran keluar asing terbesar sebanyak RM460.6 juta, diikuti utiliti RM339.8 juta dan penjagaan kesihatan RM163.1 juta. Dari sudut saham pula, antara kaunter yang menerima aliran masuk bersih asing tertinggi ialah Gamuda sebanyak RM86.2 juta, Solarvest Holdings RM65.4 juta, Westports Holdings RM55.1 juta dan Southern Cable Group RM53.4 juta. Dalam tempoh sama, Tenaga Nasional Berhad mencatatkan aliran keluar asing terbesar sebanyak RM278.1 juta, diikuti Malayan Banking RM159.3 juta dan RHB Bank RM135.9 juta. September turut menyaksikan jualan pelabur asing Trend tersebut turut dapat dilihat sepanjang September apabila pelabur asing menjual bersih saham Malaysia sebanyak RM1.69 bilion. Dalam tempoh sama, institusi tempatan mencatatkan pembelian bersih RM205.7 juta, manakala pelabur runcit membeli bersih RM1.48 bilion. Bagi September, sektor perladangan menjadi penerima aliran masuk asing terbesar sebanyak RM290.6 juta, diikuti tenaga RM230.2 juta serta pengangkutan dan logistik RM204.4 juta. Sebaliknya, sektor perkhidmatan kewangan merekodkan aliran keluar terbesar sebanyak RM1.48 bilion, diikuti utiliti RM642.2 juta dan produk serta perkhidmatan perindustrian RM310.8 juta. Aliran dana Asia kembali negatif Trend jualan asing di Malaysia berlaku ketika pelabur asing secara keseluruhan kembali mengeluarkan dana dari pasaran saham Asia. MBSB Research berkata, kesemua lapan pasaran Asia yang dipantau mencatatkan aliran keluar asing pada minggu berkenaan dengan jumlah keseluruhan AS$10.89 bilion, selepas mencatatkan pembelian bersih pada minggu sebelumnya. Korea Selatan merekodkan aliran keluar terbesar sebanyak AS$6.20 bilion, diikuti India AS$2.91 bilion dan Thailand AS$796.4 juta. Ekonomi Malaysia turut beri isyarat bercampur Dalam perkembangan ekonomi domestik, Indeks Pengurus Pembelian sektor pembuatan Malaysia susut kepada 49.9 pada September daripada 50.2 pada Ogos, menunjukkan kemerosotan keadaan operasi buat kali pertama sejak Mei 2026. MBSB Research berkata tempahan baharu merosot buat kali pertama dalam tempoh empat bulan, manakala pertumbuhan pengeluaran perlahan ke paras terendah dalam tempoh tujuh bulan. Keyakinan perniagaan turut jatuh ke paras terendah dalam tempoh lima bulan. Pada masa sama, inflasi harga pengeluar Malaysia meningkat 10.7% tahun ke tahun pada Ogos, iaitu peningkatan bagi bulan keenam berturut-turut dan kadar tertinggi sejak Jun 2022. Pasaran global kekal berhati-hati Di Amerika Syarikat, pertumbuhan pekerjaan yang lebih perlahan serta kadar inflasi yang masih melebihi sasaran menimbulkan ketidakpastian terhadap hala tuju dasar monetari negara itu. Dalam tempoh sama, dolar Amerika Syarikat meningkat 0.3% berbanding ringgit kepada RM4.0842, manakala harga minyak mentah Brent turun 2% kepada AS$102.25 setong dan minyak sawit mentah susut 2.9% kepada RM4,535 setan. Weekly Fund Flow-Week Ended 2 O… Secara keseluruhan, laporan MBSB Research menunjukkan Bursa Malaysia masih berdepan tekanan daripada pengeluaran dana asing, namun aktiviti pembelian oleh pelabur tempatan dan runcit membantu mengimbangi sebahagian tekanan tersebut ketika sentimen pelabur serantau turut dipengaruhi oleh perkembangan ekonomi global dan petunjuk ekonomi domestik yang bercampur. - DagangNews.com

title: 'Star-studded field set for Maybank Championship 2026 – ParGolf
body: 'Defending champion Miyuu Yamashita, World No. 2 Jeeno Thitikul and former winner Ruoning Yin will headline a strong international field at the Maybank Championship 2026. The fourth edition of the LPGA Tour event will be held at Kuala Lumpur Golf & Country Club (KLGCC) from 29 October to 1 November, with players competing for the Tiger Trophy and a US$3 million prize purse. Yamashita will return to Malaysia seeking to become the tournament’s first back-to-back champion. The Japanese Major winner claimed last year’s title following a three-way playoff and has continued her strong form this season. She recorded a dominant nine-stroke victory at the CPKC Women’s Open in Canada in August before winning the Sony JLPGA Championship in a playoff in September. Thailand’s Thitikul will make her fourth consecutive appearance at the tournament after narrowly missing out on the title in previous editions. She has won three LPGA Tour events in 2026, taking her career total to 10. China’s Yin, the 2024 Maybank Championship winner, also returns after capturing the FM Championship in August. Another leading contender is South Korea’s Haeran Ryu, who is second in the LPGA Tour’s Race to the CME Globe standings after winning consecutive Majors at the KPMG Women’s PGA Championship and Amundi Evian Championship. Three-time Major winner Lydia Ko will add further strength to the field. The New Zealander, who is also the reigning Olympic champion, was inducted into the LPGA Hall of Fame in 2024 at the age of 27. Australians Hannah Green and South Korea’s Hye-Jin Choi, who joined Yamashita in last year’s playoff, will return for another opportunity to claim the title. The field also includes 2023 champion Céline Boutier of France, who defeated Thitikul in a nine-hole playoff during the inaugural edition of the tournament. England’s Lottie Woad and Charley Hull, together with Japanese twins Akie and Chisato Iwai, are among the other leading international players confirmed for the championship. Five Malaysians in the field Malaysia will be represented by Liyana Durisic, Mirabel Ting, Jeneath Wong, Natasha Oon and Kelly Tan. Durisic secured her place through the Maybank Championship ASEAN Qualifier, held over 36 holes at KLGCC’s West Course in August. She claimed the fifth qualifying spot after finishing at one-under-par 143. She enters the championship in strong form after winning four PGM Tour titles in 2026, as well as the Women’s World Sand Greens Championship in Australia in March. Ting, Wong, Oon and Tan will compete through sponsor invitations. Ting secured two Epson Tour victories during her first full season as a professional, moved to the top of the Race for the Card standings, and earned her LPGA Tour card for 2027. The 2025 Annika Award winner also holds the record for the best finish by a Malaysian at the Maybank Championship after placing tied for 12th as an amateur in 2024. Wong, Malaysia’s highest-ranked female amateur at World No. 59, will return with an increasingly strong international résumé. She became the first Malaysian to win the Women’s Amateur Asia-Pacific Championship in 2025, earning starts in several Major championships. She had previously qualified for the 2023 U.S. Women’s Open. Oon will make her first Maybank Championship appearance since 2023. The former Epson Tour winner and 2023 Epson Tour Rookie of the Year is rebuilding her momentum after an injury kept her out for much of the 2024 and 2025 seasons. Completing the Malaysian line-up is two-time Olympian Tan, the country’s most successful LPGA Tour player. Tan recorded her best LPGA Tour results with runner-up finishes at the Dow Great Lakes Bay Invitational in 2022 and 2023. She will make her third appearance at the Maybank Championship, bringing more than a decade of professional experience and extensive knowledge of KLGCC’s West Course. ASEAN qualifiers earn their places Five Southeast Asian players earned invitations through the Maybank Championship ASEAN Qualifier, which provides a merit-based route into the LPGA Tour event. Thai professional Pimnipa Panthong finished tied at the top of the qualifier at four-under-par 140 alongside compatriots Sarisa Pojanalai and Achiraya Sriwong. Sriwong, who competed in the qualifier as an amateur, has since turned professional. Thai amateur Marisa Tojai secured the fourth qualifying place at two-under-par 142, while Durisic completed the group at one-under 143. Introduced in 2024, the ASEAN Qualifier gives leading regional players an opportunity to compete against established international professionals at the Maybank Championship. Tickets for the Maybank Championship 2026 are now on sale through the tournament’s official website.
