title: 'Bjak Founder Weighs IPO as Malaysian Insurtech Expands Abroad
body: '(Dec 16): Bjak Sdn Bhd, Malaysia’s largest online insurance aggregator, is mulling an initial public offering (IPO) within the next two years as it seeks to enter Europe. Bjak is eyeing new markets in Spain and Germany in 2026 following its recent expansion in Japan, Taiwan and Thailand, Wei Low, the firm’s founder said in his first-ever media interview. The firm’s gross written premiums increased 20% to 30% this year and are set to grow at a faster pace in the future as Bjak expands into new markets, the 36-year-old told Bloomberg News. The business has been profitable since its inception in 2019 and has “very minimal” debt, he said, declining to disclose further financial details. “We are still very young as a company,” Low said. “If you look at our other peers in other markets that are large, in China or the UK, it takes about 20 years to really maximise the potential or increase the penetration.” The IPO will help fund further overseas expansion and provide employees with liquidity through stock grants. Bjak is shifting its focus to Spain and Germany, which have well-established auto insurance markets, Low said. Low plans to double his team across the world by the end of 2026 from almost 200 people currently. The success of Ant Group Co, the operator of China’s ubiquitous financial services app Alipay, inspired Low to start Bjak in 2019. While insurance technology is well established in markets like the UK, it is at different stages of maturity across Asia, he said. In Malaysia, RAM Ratings forecasts moderating growth this year in new business for both life and non-life insurers, including those that comply with Islamic principles. Non-life premium gains are seen slowing to 5% in 2025 from 7.3% last year. Still, the potential upside for the nation’s insurance industry “remains healthy”, according to RAM Ratings analyst Loh Kit Yoong. Increasing awareness of the importance of coverage protection and significant numbers of Malaysians who are uninsured and underinsured, especially among lower income households, underpin business opportunities, she said. Online insurance platforms improve insurers’ reach to some of these segments, given the high smartphone and internet access rates in the country, the analyst said. Bjak has seven million users and 16 insurance brands, including Germany’s Allianz SE and Japan’s Tokio Marine, on its platform. Low’s entrepreneurial journey began at age 20 when his family’s financial woes forced him to drop out of a pre-university programme. Before founding Bjak, he was involved in aluminium trading and two other e-commerce ventures that stalled. He cited Warren Buffett as his idol and has read all of Berkshire Hathaway Inc’s annual letters the billionaire investor has written since 1965. Like Buffett, Low wants to embrace a business philosophy focused on more than just monetary success. “He has this quote that he emphasised a lot that I practice: You find out who your role models are and copy them,” he said. title: 'Felda’s Road Ahead in the Spotlight
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Seven years after Malaysians were made aware of the problems confronting the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda), the institution is once again at a crossroads. Felda, which has the largest plantation footprint in the country and has helped improve the livelihoods of more than 100,000 original settlers and their families, is undergoing another strategic review amid concerns over its long-term sustainability. An interim report on the Felda Group Strategic Roadmap 2025-2030 (HTF 30) was submitted last month by the Special Committee on the Strategic Plan for Felda Group to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Among the proposals under consideration is a redefinition of Felda’s mandate, including a review of the Land Development Act that governs the agency, as the committee monitors actions taken following the 2019 Felda White Paper, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The review comes as the highly indebted entity grapples with crucial replanting costs that could reach RM900 million annually, on top of more than RM900 million in financing costs currently borne by the government. Felda oversees some 870,000ha of land, of which 490,000ha was allocated to settlers, 330,000ha to Felda’s commercial plantations — later placed under FGV Holdings Bhd — and another 50,000ha for village development. Fragmented and ineffective management of the land and operations, together with questionable transactions and investments, resulted in heavy losses despite Felda receiving billions of ringgit from the listing of its commercial arm, then known as Felda Global Ventures Holdings Bhd. By 2017, Felda’s borrowings had ballooned to RM12.1 billion from just RM100 million in 2007. In 2023, the government guaranteed and agreed to service Felda’s RM9.9 billion sukuk, issued to fund the RM3.7 billion privatisation of FGV to consolidate its estate operations, as well as Felda and settlers’ debt. But more needs to be done before those efforts bear fruit. In 2012, Felda raised RM6 billion through the offer for sale of FGV shares during the latter’s initial public offering, while FGV itself raised RM4.5 billion from investors. In total, the exercise raised RM10.5 billion. Instead of directing more of those proceeds towards critical needs such as replanting, the 2019 Felda White Paper found that RM4.6 billion, or 76% of Felda’s IPO proceeds, went towards what it described as “unproductive spending”, while another RM1.4 billion was channelled into investments that failed to generate returns. The spending included RM1.69 billion in special payments to settlers, RM550 million in one-off contributions to state governments, RM400 million in loans for settlers’ house extensions, RM406 million to redeem FGV shares and RM177 million in listing expenses. FGV, meanwhile, spent RM3.3 billion, or 73% of its RM4.5 billion in IPO proceeds, on investments and developments that did not generate satisfactory returns. FGV, which leased Felda’s plantation land, also failed to achieve the yields Felda had projected, leaving the agency with an earnings shortfall. Following FGV’s privatisation, Felda is looking at consolidating the management of its commercial estates and settlers’ land. But that alone will not resolve the underlying balance-sheet problem, particularly the heavy capital requirements needed to keep the estates productive. Beyond its plantation operations, Felda bears significant social obligations to settlers, including spending on housing, infrastructure and income support for up to five years during the replanting cycle. Today, the families of Felda settlers span as many as six generations and number about 2.8 million people. In many respects, Felda has fulfilled its original mandate of opening up rural land and developing communities alongside settlers, about 95% of whom have received titles to their land. Without a clear framework for its future model, the institution’s role and the financial obligations that come with it risk continuing to be shaped by factors beyond its core mandate, particularly when political considerations intersect with policy during periods of adjustment. Any new roadmap will therefore have to define more clearly where Felda’s commercial responsibilities end and its social obligations begin, and how each should be funded. Felda was in better shape before the mismanagement that followed the windfall from FGV’s listing, when the institution was earning around RM3 billion a year. There are also arguments that greater provisions should have been made for replanting, which is central to sustaining its core operations. Poor investment decisions, however, turned Felda’s fortunes upside down in less than a decade. A forensic audit found RM2.2 billion in asset impairments from eight transactions undertaken by Felda and Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC) between 2010 and 2018 — equivalent to half of their initial RM4.4 billion investment value. Among them were PT Eagle High Plantations Tbk, the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project and several London properties. One of the largest was Felda’s US$505.4 million acquisition of a 37% non-controlling stake in Eagle High Plantations in 2016 at a premium, resulting in an impairment loss of RM1.576 billion in 2017. Its London property purchases also came under scrutiny over discrepancies between reported acquisition prices and amounts received by vendors, while some properties saw their values fall sharply soon after acquisition. KLVC, meanwhile, remains the subject of a legal dispute between Felda and developer Synergy Promenade Sdn Bhd (SPSB) over the development of Felda land along Jalan Semarak. Former FIC chief executive officer Mohd Zaid Abdul Jalil has also been charged with two counts of cheating the company’s board, which allegedly resulted in the ownership of 16 land parcels being transferred from Felda to SPSB. Source: TheEdge - 6 Oct 2026

title: 'The socialist tinge running through Malay society and politics
body: 'By Murray Hunter A CONSISTENT thread of light, humanitarian socialism, the social-democratic and developmental variety, has long run through Malay society and politics in Malaysia. It appears in traditional cultural traits, interpretations of Islamic social ethics, the policies of major Malay parties including UMNO and PAS, and the structure of the modern economy. This form of socialism today is focused on mutual help, social justice, state intervention for equity, and protection of the community, especially the Malay majority. Private ownership, markets and individual enterprise remain, but they operate within a framework of collective responsibility and guided redistribution, through both the New Economic Policy (NEP) and reserved Malay land. Several deep-rooted Malay cultural traits help explain why such ideas found fertile ground throughout Malaya’s contemporary history. Almost forgotten traditions in the traditional kampong, gotong royong was a practical expression of communal cooperation. Villagers regularly came together to build or repair houses, plant and harvest rice, clear drains and paths, maintain the surau or cemetery, and assist with weddings, funerals and other life-cycle events. The familiar proverb “berat sama dipikul, ringan sama dijinjing” captured the expectation that burdens should be shared. More broadly, Malay society has tended to favour communalism rather than strong individualism. Group harmony, collective responsibility, loyalty to kin and community, and the avoidance of open confrontation often take precedence over assertive personal autonomy or pure self-interest. This cultural orientation creates a natural affinity for policies that stress mutual support, shared welfare and the idea that the community’s well-being is more important than unchecked individual gain. This is partly explained by Malaysia’s high power-distance score on widely used cultural dimensions such as those developed by Geert Hofstede. In high power-distance societies, hierarchy is accepted as normal, and people are generally more willing to follow authority without extensive public questioning. Among many Malays, this has historically translated into relatively high deference to traditional leaders, the state, religious figures and those in positions of formal power. When government programmes are presented as serving the uplift of the Malay community, this readiness to accept direction from above has made large-scale state intervention more readily accepted than it might be in strongly individualistic, low power-distance cultures. The combination of communalism and hierarchical acceptance helped legitimise ambitious top-down social and economic programmes. Islamic teachings have reinforced the same outlook for many. Obligatory zakat functions as a structured redistribution of wealth from those with surplus to the poor, the needy, debtors and other designated categories. The duty to care for orphans, widows and the vulnerable, the prohibition of riba (usury), and the repeated Qur’anic emphasis on adl (justice) have been interpreted by some Muslim thinkers as containing important socialist elements. Early PAS leader Burhanuddin al-Helmy explicitly combined Islamist, nationalist and socialist ideas in the struggle against colonialism and inequality. Malaysian sociologist Syed Hussein Alatas, in his work Islam and Socialism, argued that Islam’s principles of anti-exploitation and social justice made it compatible with non-Marxist forms of socialism focused on fairness and community welfare rather than atheistic materialism or the abolition of private property. In formal politics, the pattern is clear. Early Malay leftist and populist groups drew on ideas of uplifting ordinary people (marhaen). Within UMNO, the decisive shift came after the 1969 racial riots under Tun Abdul Razak. Razak, who had been exposed to British Labour Party and Fabian socialist thought during his studies, spoke of a form of “nationalist socialism” suited to a developing multi-ethnic nation. The New Economic Policy (NEP) that followed introduced large-scale state intervention with two main prongs: the eradication of poverty regardless of race, and the restructuring of society so that Malays and other Bumiputera could participate more fully in the modern economy and no longer be identified primarily with subsistence agriculture. This was deliberate social engineering aimed at equity and national unity. Key institutions created or expanded in the Razak era still shape Malaysia today. FELDA (Federal Land Development Authority) organised large-scale land settlement schemes that moved hundreds of thousands of rural Malay families onto new agricultural plots, complete with housing, infrastructure, technical support and a structured pathway out of poverty. It was a classic state-led redistributive and developmental programme. MARA (Majlis Amanah Rakyat) was established to advance Bumiputera participation in education, skills training, business and entrepreneurship through scholarships, loans, commercial ventures and institutional support. Together with other agencies, these bodies embodied the belief that the state had a positive duty to correct economic imbalances and uplift the Malay community through organised collective effort. There was an assumption that those privileged leaders would always take the interests of the people into action. PAS has contributed its own version of this tinge. Although primarily an Islamist party, it has at various times emphasised welfare provision, rural development, anti-elite rhetoric and social justice framed through Islamic ethics. In the states it has governed for long periods, PAS has pursued policies with clear redistributive and protective elements that appeal to lower-income and rural Malays who value collective support and moral economy over pure market outcomes. That is partly the reason PAS has been in government there for a long period of time. Today’s economy is reflective of this history The contemporary Malaysian economy continues to reflect the Razak-era model and retains strong features of a light socialist or developmentalist system. Government-linked companies (GLCs) play a dominant role in strategic sectors. The public bureaucracy remains large and central in directing economic activity, allocating resources and implementing preferential policies. Equity ownership targets, subsidies, public education and housing programmes, and extensive state involvement in the economy persist. FELDA and MARA continue to operate alongside a wider network of agencies dedicated to Bumiputera economic advancement. Markets and private enterprise function, freehold land ownership is secure, and individual initiative is encouraged, yet they operate within a framework of heavy government guidance and redistributive goals aimed at social and ethnic equity. This is a mixed economy with a pronounced interventionist and welfare character. The Malaysian economy is not laissez-faire capitalism, nor is it Soviet-style central planning. The focus has always been practical and humanitarian, aimed at reducing poverty, correcting historical imbalances, fostering mutual support, and using the state as an instrument of community uplift. Cultural communalism, acceptance of hierarchy, Islamic ethics of justice, and the institutional legacy of Tun Razak’s era have all sustained this approach. The light socialist colouring remains one of the quieter but durable features of Malay society and politics. It can be traced from the kampong practices of gotong royong and communalism, through the cultural readiness to accept authoritative direction for the common good, the ethical teachings of Islam on justice and redistribution, the ambitious nation-building of Tun Razak’s time with institutions such as FELDA and MARA, and the continuing role of GLCs and state guidance in today’s economy. Unfortunately, many politicians today appear to have forgotten this deeper aspect of the Malay political psyche. Too often they have become focused primarily upon their own personal wellbeing, status and material advancement rather than the broader communal and redistributive responsibilities that once animated Malay political culture. When the ethic of shared burden and collective uplift is neglected in favour of private gain, the original spirit that helped shape both society and policy risks being hollowed out. Recovering an awareness of that older communal and humanitarian strand may be necessary if Malay politics is to remain connected to the values that long gave it meaning. – September 4, 2026

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Stays Lower at Mid-Morning Trailed by Heavyweight Selling
body: 'Bursa Malaysia remained firmly in negative territory at mid-morning on Thursday, October 1, 2026, dragged down by selling pressure across key blue-chip counters, primarily in healthcare, industrial products, and utilities sectors. At 11:00 AM, the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) slid 11.73 points to 1,639.44 compared to Wednesday’s close of 1,651.17. The index had opened 1.30 points lower at 1,649.87. Market breadth was negative, with decliners outpacing gainers 484 to 273, while 460 counters traded unchanged, 1,556 untraded, and 12 suspended. Total turnover stood at 1.18 billion shares valued at RM769.76 million. Sectoral Pressure and Heavyweight Performance Heavyweight stocks across multiple sectors experienced selling pressure during the morning session: - Healthcare: IHH Healthcare dropped 13 sen to RM7.70. - Industrial Products: Petronas Chemicals shed 11 sen to RM4.07, Press Metal Aluminium slipped 9 sen to RM7.36, and Sunway fell 2 sen to RM4.40. - Utilities: YTL Power lost 6 sen to RM5.81, Tenaga Nasional dropped 2 sen to RM12.94, and YTL Corporation edged down 1 sen to RM2.27. - Financials: Banking stocks saw broad-based softness with Public Bank down 3 sen to RM4.67, while Maybank and CIMB eased 2 sen each to RM9.97 and RM7.77, respectively. Active Stocks and Top Gainers and Losers In active trade, ACE Market debutant GB Bond shed 2.5 sen to 22.5 sen, while Dagang Nexchange gained 2 sen to 50.5 sen. V.S Industry added 1 sen to 29 sen, Zetrix AI rose half a sen to 16.5 sen, and Jaks Resources dropped half a sen to 20 sen. Technology stocks featured among the session’s top gainers: - Malaysian Pacific Industries: Up 62 sen to RM41.02. - Malayan Cement: Up 12 sen to RM5.57. - MI Technovation & Hengyuan Refining: Gained 10 sen each to RM5.30 and RM3.66, respectively. - Vitrox: Advanced 8 sen to RM9.99. On the decliners’ chart, Kuala Lumpur Kepong led losses, falling 74 sen to RM21.46. Other notable pullbacks included Allianz Malaysia (down 68 sen to RM20.94), Nestle (down 40 sen to RM89.60), United Plantations (down 30 sen to RM31.26), and Hong Leong Bank (down 28 sen to RM22.86). Broad Market and Sectoral Indices All major sectoral indices recorded declines at mid-morning, led by plantations and financials: - The Plantation Index tumbled 104.26 points to 9,092.41. - The Financial Services Index shed 87.09 points to 19,129.40. - The Energy Index eased 5.43 points to 840.27. - The Industrial Products and Services Index fell 1.24 points to 179.17. Across the broader index boards: - The FBM Top 100 Index fell 76.32 points to 12,008.12. - The FBM Emas Index dropped 72.18 points to 12,219.83. - The FBM Emas Shariah Index weakened 71.61 points to 12,104.73. - The FBM Mid 70 Index lost 71.17 points to 17,503.50. - The FBM ACE Index trimmed 22.64 points to 5,511.64. –NMT

title: 'Daily Newswatch - 25 Sep 2026
body: 'The FBM KLCI ended 0.2% lower to 1,672.3 points on Thursday, as renewed oil-price gains and elevated global bond yields pressured investor sentiment, offsetting intermittent buying interest in selected counters. Telecommunications & Media (-2.0%), Technology (-1.8%) and Consumer Product and Services (-0.4%) led sectoral losses, with Press Metal Aluminium (-1.7%), YTL Power International (-1.9%) and Petronas Gas (-0.6%) among the key laggards. Market breadth, however, was negative, with losers outnumbering gainers 677 to 436, and 542 counters unchanged. Asian markets ended mostly lower on Thursday as sentiment turned more cautious amid rising sovereign bond yields, despite positive developments surrounding US-China trade relations and US-Iran ceasefire talks. Japan’s 10- year JGB yield rose to nearly 3.1%, its highest level since 1996, while US Treasury yields also edged higher during Asian trading. The Hang Seng Index fell 0.3% to 24,761.1, the TAIEX declined 0.3% to 48,024.6, and the Shanghai Composite dropped 1.2% to 3,888.4. In contrast, Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained 0.8% to 65,514.0. In China, notable laggards included Kweichow Moutai (-1.14%), Foxconn Industrial Internet (-3.14%), and China Life Insurance (-3.03%). South Korea’s KOSPI was closed for the Chuseok holiday. European stocks closed lower on Thursday as soaring energy prices lifted benchmark rates. The Euro STOXX 50 fell 0.4% to 6,273, and the STOXX Europe 600 fell 0.5% to 637. Fuel and natural gas prices surged amid signs that the naval blockade in the Persian Gulf could be prolonged, in addition to signals from the US presidential administration that diesel exports could be banned. Sovereign yields extended their surge this week, weighing on the corporate sector. Infineon sank 4.2% and Siemens Energy dropped 1.7%, tracking the negative AI trade in North America. US stock indices closed mixed on Thursday amid renewed volatility in bond yields and oil prices. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq CI ended broadly flat, while the Dow Jones fell 162 points. The 10-year US Treasury yield briefly rose above 5.15% before easing to around 5.1%, remaining near its highest level since 2007, while the 30-year yield climbed to its highest level since 2004. Rising oil prices and heightened US-Iran tensions contributed to the increase in borrowing costs. However, sentiment was supported by reports that US and Iranian negotiators were moving closer to an agreement to restore tanker flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Among AI hyperscalers, Alphabet gained 1.3% and Meta rose 4.5% following positive feedback on its AI agent software and latest gadget releases, while Microsoft declined 0.5% and Amazon was broadly flat. US: Global bond selloff rolls on, US 30-year yield at highest since 2004 US long-dated Treasury yields rose to their highest in more than 20 years on Thursday, extending a global selloff that has accelerated on worries that high energy costs, resilient economic growth and increased government spending will keep inflation elevated Bond markets worldwide have been under pressure for months, sending yields to multi-decade highs as the Iran war raised energy prices and as investors fret about government spending. Rising yields mean bond prices are falling. (Reuters) US: Oil Halts Rally on Talks of a Phased Deal Crude oil steadied near $94 per barrel on Friday, pausing its recent rally amid reports that the US and Iran were considering a phased deal that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz and lift a US blockade on Iranian ports. Efforts to reach a breakthrough were reportedly underway on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, with Qatari officials mediating the talks. (Reuters) US: To either reform IEA on climate issues or leave group, energy secretary says The US might consider leaving the International Energy Agency (IEA) if there is no alignment on climate issues, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on Wednesday. "We are either going to reform the IEA or we will leave the IEA. My strong preference is that we reform it," Wright said at an event in New York hosted by The Wall Street Journal. The Paris-based IEA has provided research and data to industrialised governments for more than half a century to help guide policy around energy security, supply and investment. (Reuters) US: New home sales jump to eight-month high in August Sales of new US single-family homes surged to an eight-month high in August as buyers took advantage of price cuts and other incentives, but rising mortgage rates stemming from the war in the Middle East remain a drag on the housing market. New home sales increased 6.4% to a seasonally adjusted annualised rate of 684,000 units last month, the highest level since December 2025, the Commerce Department's Census Bureau said on Thursday. (Reuters) US: Current account deficit widens sharply in second quarter The US current account deficit widened sharply in the second quarter amid a surge in imports of goods, government data showed on Thursday. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis said the current account deficit, which measures the flow of goods, services and investments into and out of the country, increased US$33.4 billion (RM136.1 billion), or 15.7%, to US$246.0 billion last quarter. (Reuters) US: Gold slips as rising oil prices, Treasury yields dent appeal Gold prices eased on Thursday, pressured by rising oil prices and US Treasury yields, while expectations the US Federal Reserve (Fed) could tighten monetary policy further weighed on sentiment. Spot gold fell 0.6% to US$4,261.55 (RM17,409.71) per ounce, by 1206 GMT, having hit its lowest since Sept 17. US gold futures for December delivery eased 0.5% to US$4,296.30. (Reuters) US: Weekly jobless claims near 57-year lows as labour market regains footing The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits fell last week, pointing to a firming labour market. Initial claims for state unemployment benefits slipped 1,000 to a seasonally adjusted 197,000 for the week ended Sept 19, the Labor Department said on Thursday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast 201,000 claims for the latest week. (Reuters) UK: Consumer Confidence Hits More Than 2-Year High The UK GfK Consumer Confidence Index rose to -13 in September 2026 from -14 in the previous month, unexpectedly reaching its highest level since August 2024 as households became more optimistic about their personal finances and the economic outlook. The reading came above the Reuters poll forecast of -16, adding to recent signs of resilience in the UK economy. (Reuters) CN: Busiest-ever week for China ports gives glimpse of tariff unease Chinese ports had their busiest week in history ahead of the approaching summit between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, extending a boom in shipments abroad in a possible sign exporters were rushing goods out of the country as uncertainty hovered over tariffs. A record 7.3 million containers passed through Chinese terminals in the seven days through Sept 20, an increase of 9% from a year ago, according to data released by the Ministry of Transport. (Bloomberg) JP: 10-year yield climbs to 1996 high as global rout deepens Japan’s 10-year government bond yield climbed to its highest since 1996, joining a deepening global sell-off as the market reopened after the Silver Week holidays. The yield rose 10 basis points to 3.075% on Thursday after the three-day break. Yields across the curve also climbed, with the five-year rate rising 9.5 basis points to 2.37%. (Bloomberg) JP: Manufacturing Growth at 7-Month Low Japan’s 10-year government bond yield climbed to its highest since 1996, joining a deepening global sell-off as the market reopened after the Silver Week holidays. The yield rose 10 basis points to 3.075% on Thursday after the three-day break. Yields across the curve also climbed, with the five-year rate rising 9.5 basis points to 2.37%. (S&P Global) HK: Seeks up to US$2.6 bil in record digital bond sale - Bloomberg Hong Kong is seeking to raise HK$15 billion to HK$20 billion (US$1.9 billion to US$2.6 billion or RM7.81 billion to RM10.41 billion) through a multi-currency digital green bond offering that would be the world’s largest of its kind, according to people familiar with the matter, as the city pushes to become a fixed-income hub. The bonds, denominated in US dollars, Hong Kong dollars, euros and offshore yuan, could be priced as early as Monday, the people said, who asked not to be identified discussing private information. (Bloomberg) MY: Palm oil under near-term pressure as rising stocks outweigh El Niño fears Palm oil prices are poised to remain under pressure as rising inventories in Malaysia and sluggish buying by the world's biggest importer India weigh on the market and the impact of El Niño has yet to be felt, industry officials told Reuters. Malaysia, the world's second-biggest producer, has been receiving below-normal rainfall due to El Niño, but palm oil output rose month-on-month in September. (Reuters) MY: 2026 GDP growth could hit 5.7% on stronger manufacturing, investments - economists Malaysia’s economy could expand by an average 5.7% in 2026, exceeding official forecasts, driven by stronger manufacturing, construction and investments, said two economists. Asia Strategic Consulting Sdn Bhd founder Professor Paolo Casadio and Williams Business Consultancy Sdn Bhd founder Professor Geoffrey Williams also projected growth to reach 5.9% in the fourth quarter of 2026. (Bernama) RHBBANK: Oct 23 ruling on bid to restrain RHB from closing Maritime Network's accounts The High Court here on Thursday fixed Oct 23 to rule on a shipping company's bid to restrain RHB Bank Bhd from closing two of its longstanding accounts, pending the disposal of its full suit. Judicial Commissioner Elesabet Paya Wan set the date after hearing submissions from P Taneswaran, acting for Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, and the bank's counsel, Gan Khong Aik. (The Edge) MYNEWS: Net profit down 40% in 3Q on higher operating expenses Convenience store chain operator MyNews Holdings Bhd saw its net profit fall 40.5% to RM3.83 million for its third quarter ended July 31, 2026 (3QFY2026), compared with RM6.43 million a year earlier. Higher administrative, selling and distribution expenses weighed down the bottom line despite revenue for the quarter growing 9% to RM251.76 million from RM230.94 million. (The Edge) SUPERLN: Posts decade-high quarterly profit on record revenue, appoints new CEO Superlon Holdings Bhd reported its highest quarterly net profit in a decade as revenue hit a record on higher contribution from its manufacturing division and better margins. Net profit for the first quarter ended July 31, 2026 (1QFY2027) surged 77.56% year-on-year to RM5.48 million from RM3.08 million, the thermal insulation solution maker’s bourse filing on Thursday showed. (The Edge) INFOM: Bags RM63 mil contract to provide tech refresh, maintenance for financial institution Infomina Bhd said on Thursday that it accepted a RM63 million contract to provide technology refresh supply and maintenance to a financial institution. According to a bourse filing on Thursday, the contract entails the supply, delivery, installation, configuration, integration, testing, commissioning, implementation, support, maintenance and other works and services applicable to the hardware, equipment, software and other items. (The Edge) AJI: Shareholders approve parent's RM20 privatisation offer Ajinomoto (Malaysia) Bhd shareholders have approved the RM20 per share offer from its parent, Ajinomoto Co Inc, to take the company private via a selective capital reduction (SCR). According to a filing with Bursa Malaysia, at an extraordinary general meeting on Thursday, 216 shareholders holding 7.85 million shares, or 92.8% of the voted shares, backed the deal, while 56 shareholders holding about 605,653 shares, or 7.2%, voted against it. (The Edge) INTA: Bags RM221 mil construction contract in Klang from Mitraland Inta Bina Group Bhd said on Thursday it has secured a RM221.08 million contract to undertake the main building works for an apartment and office development in Klang. 'The FBM KLCI ended 0.2% lower to 1,672.3 points on Thursday, as renewed oil-price gains and elevated global bond yields pressured investor sentiment, offsetting intermittent buying interest in selected counters. Telecommunications & Media (-2.0%), Technology (-1.8%) and Consumer Product and Services (-0.4%) led sectoral losses, with Press Metal Aluminium (-1.7%), YTL Power International (-1.9%) and Petronas Gas (-0.6%) among the key laggards. Market breadth, however, was negative, with losers outnumbering gainers 677 to 436, and 542 counters unchanged. Asian markets ended mostly lower on Thursday as sentiment turned more cautious amid rising sovereign bond yields, despite positive developments surrounding US-China trade relations and US-Iran ceasefire talks. Japan’s 10- year JGB yield rose to nearly 3.1%, its highest level since 1996, while US Treasury yields also edged higher during Asian trading. The Hang Seng Index fell 0.3% to 24,761.1, the TAIEX declined 0.3% to 48,024.6, and the Shanghai Composite dropped 1.2% to 3,888.4. In contrast, Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained 0.8% to 65,514.0. In China, notable laggards included Kweichow Moutai (-1.14%), Foxconn Industrial Internet (-3.14%), and China Life Insurance (-3.03%). South Korea’s KOSPI was closed for the Chuseok holiday. European stocks closed lower on Thursday as soaring energy prices lifted benchmark rates. The Euro STOXX 50 fell 0.4% to 6,273, and the STOXX Europe 600 fell 0.5% to 637. Fuel and natural gas prices surged amid signs that the naval blockade in the Persian Gulf could be prolonged, in addition to signals from the US presidential administration that diesel exports could be banned. Sovereign yields extended their surge this week, weighing on the corporate sector. Infineon sank 4.2% and Siemens Energy dropped 1.7%, tracking the negative AI trade in North America. US stock indices closed mixed on Thursday amid renewed volatility in bond yields and oil prices. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq CI ended broadly flat, while the Dow Jones fell 162 points. The 10-year US Treasury yield briefly rose above 5.15% before easing to around 5.1%, remaining near its highest level since 2007, while the 30-year yield climbed to its highest level since 2004. Rising oil prices and heightened US-Iran tensions contributed to the increase in borrowing costs. However, sentiment was supported by reports that US and Iranian negotiators were moving closer to an agreement to restore tanker flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Among AI hyperscalers, Alphabet gained 1.3% and Meta rose 4.5% following positive feedback on its AI agent software and latest gadget releases, while Microsoft declined 0.5% and Amazon was broadly flat. Rising yields mean bond prices are falling. title: 'All You Need To Know About The BTS Arirang x Maybank Visa Card That’s Now Available In Malaysia
body:
'

BTS World Tour Arirang x Maybank Visa

It’s finally a Spring Day for Malaysian fans of BTS. Not literally – all we’ve got is summer over here – but fans can have a spring in their step after a drought of being left out of tour schedules and merch release lists.

Besides 2 concert dates scheduled in Malaysia, the latest merch drop from BTS on our shores comes in the form of an Arirang-themed Visa debit card, with the group’s name on a plastic card we can not leave home without.

What is the BTS World Tour Arirang Visa card for?

As the Worldwide Tour Sponsor for BTS World Tour Arirang – which unites the formidable 7-member group at 82 shows in 34 cities in five continents – Visa has been partnering with card issuers around the globe for limited-edition BTS Arirang debit cards. These cards are recognised as official merchandise by the group’s agency, HYBE, which means another merch item to cop and use in your daily life.

Each country gets its own special Arirang Visa card design, inspired by the colours and motifs of the BTS album and tour – it’ll feel a bit like getting your hands on an exclusive photocard, except this one carries your moolah.

How to get the card? 


Image credit: Lizzy

In Malaysia, Visa has collaborated with Maybank to launch the Arirang-themed Visa card: a slick, all-black matte card with the BTS tour name in shiny lettering and the Arirang red logo on the top right.

There are two ways to get it from the Malaysian bank: offline and online. Here’s how:

Offline

From 23rd September 2026 onwards, fans can head to 12 Maybank branches nationwide to get their hands on the BTS World Tour Arirang Maybank Visa card.

The branches all open at 9.30am on weekdays, with card replacements and applications for new Maybank accounts to secure the card all done over the counter.

To ensure there are enough cards to go around, each branch has a strict daily 60-card issuance rule – in other words, each bank will only grant 60 BTS Visa cards per day to 60 customers. Expect queues even before opening hours because of this.


Image credit: Lizzy

Once you’re through the bank doors as one of 60 lucky fans of the day, it’ll be time to cheer. Look forward to fast service from bank staff who’ll hand you a queue number, and proceed to take your MyKad or passport, current debit card if not lost, and a thumbprint for application when your number is called. At the end of the process, you’ll be issued the BTS Visa card along with an envelope containing a sticker and celebratory message.

There’s a small “replacement” fee of RM12 to get the card, which will be deducted from your Maybank account funds.

Image credit: Lizzy

Here are the locations where you can process your application in person:

  1. Bukit Bintang
  2. Mid Valley City
  3. KL Main Branch (Menara Tun Perak)
  4. Dataran Maybank
  5. Petaling Jaya Main Branch
  6. Shah Alam Main Branch
  7. Penang Main Branch (Lebuh Union)
  8. Ipoh Main Branch (Jalan Sultan Idris Shah)
  9. Kuantan Main Branch (Jalan Sultan Abdullah)
  10. Johor Bahru Main Branch (City Square)
  11. Karamunsing (Bangunan Maybank)
  12. Kuching Main Branch

Online

Opt to skip the physical queues altogether if you’re an existing Maybank debit cardholder. You can get the BTS World Tour Arirang card online through the bank’s Maybank2u website, with online replacement requests accepted from 28th September onwards.

There’s also a RM12 replacement fee for this option, but it’ll be free if you have just 12 months left before your card’s expiry date.

Here’s how to submit a replacement request online:

  1. Log in to Maybank2u
  2. Go to Settings, select ‘Cards’
  3. Select ‘Manage Debit Cards’, then ‘Debit Card – Replace, Activate & Block’
  4. Click the three dots next to your debit card, select ‘Replace/Renew Card’
  5. Find the BTS World Tour Arirang debit card as your design of choice, and then click Next
  6. Fill in your delivery address, acknowledge the Terms & Conditions, and click ‘Submit’
  7. Verify your request with an SMS TAC or Secure 2U via the Maybank2U app
  8. Voilà, the replacement has been processed

Guide to get the BTS World Tour Arirang Visa card in Malaysia

Not every fan can say they have a Visa card with their favourite group on it. If you identify as an ARMY, the limited-edition BTS World Tour Arirang Visa card will be one to get, even if the process to get them might feel a little like the war for tickets.

Cover image adapted from: @votingbrigade via X, Lizzy

title: 'SLGC Mitigates Rising Construction Costs Through Value-engineering
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Construction firm service SLGC Bhd (KL:SLG) said on Tuesday that it has undertaken value-engineering measures to cushion the impact of rising construction material costs amid geopolitical tensions. Value engineering is the process of adjusting a project with a client to achieve the same performance, while identifying alternatives to materials or specifications. “We have experienced construction material costs [having] increased recently, but we have managed this by proposing various value-engineering exercises to our clients,” its managing director Yong Zheng Lin told reporters after the company’s debut on Bursa Malaysia’s ACE Market on Tuesday. “For instance, we have suggested changes in specifications or brands to our clients as part of these exercises as a way for us to offset the rising cost,” he added. Construction costs have continued to rise in line with higher oil prices, exerting cost pressure on the group’s margins, though Yong did not indicate any specific figure for the percentage of costs increase. To mitigate the impact, the group said it is also negotiating with subcontractors and locking in material prices early with its suppliers. According to Yong, the group currently has a tender book of over RM1 billion, with an estimated success rate of 10% to 15%. As at Aug 12, the total unbilled contract value of its ongoing construction projects stood at RM1 billion, to be recognised progressively over the next five financial years until FY2030. On potential data centre contracts, Yong said: "We’re still exploring and discussing the opportunities but the group hasn't had any successful deal yet". For the financial year ended Dec 31, 2025 (FY2025), SLGC’s net profit dropped to RM13.99 million, compared with RM16.03 million a year earlier, but revenue rose to RM324 million from RM229.64 million. The group has two revenue segments, which residential segment contributed 74.95% out of total revenue for FY2025 and non-residential segment made up the remaining 25.05%. The company is mainly involved in design and building construction services for residential and non-residential works. SLGC’s customers include property developers and building owners in Malaysia. SLGC shares settled three sen or 10.7% lower at 25 sen on its maiden trading day on Tuesday, valuing the company at RM140 million. title: 'Maybank 2Q FY26 Net Profit Rises 2.4% to RM2.69 Billion
body: 'Maybank reported a 2.4% year-on-year increase in net profit to RM2.69 billion for the second quarter of FY2026, supported by stronger core fee income, tighter cost control and lower impairment provisions. The banking group also recorded profit before tax of RM3.64 billion, representing a 3.7% increase from the corresponding quarter last year. Return on equity improved to 12.0%, compared with 11.6% a year earlier, while net operating income reached RM7.51 billion. For the first six months of FY2026, Maybank generated RM5.17 billion in net profit. First-half return on equity stood at 11.6%, slightly above the 11.5% recorded during the same period last year. Core Fees Support Maybank Earnings Fee-based businesses provided one of the strongest contributors to Maybank’s quarterly performance. Wealth management fees increased 61.5% year-on-year, while investment banking fees climbed 58.4%. Banking-related fees rose by a more moderate 2.6%. Net fund-based income increased 1.9% over the same period. The stronger fee contribution helped offset softer markets-related income, while Maybank’s Insurance and Takaful operations benefited from improved equity market conditions. Net interest margin also expanded by 10 basis points to 2.10% during the quarter. For the first half, Maybank maintained a net interest margin of 2.12%. Core fees rose 12.1% during the six-month period, with wealth management fees increasing 48.4%. The group attributed the improvement partly to stronger investment and bancassurance income. Investment banking fees also benefited from stronger equity capital markets and related activity. Costs Fall as Maybank Maintains Spending Discipline Maybank reduced overhead expenses by 2.5% year-on-year to RM3.69 billion during the second quarter. The decline brought its cost-to-income ratio to 49.1%. Personnel costs fell 6.9%, while marketing expenses declined 21.9%. However, establishment costs increased as Maybank continued investing in technology initiatives. For the first half of FY2026, total overhead expenses declined 3.9% year-on-year. Lower costs combined with substantially reduced impairment provisions helped support the group’s overall profitability. Net impairment provisions declined 51.6% year-on-year during the first half. Maybank Loan Book Reaches RM695.9 Billion Maybank’s group loans expanded 2.7% year-on-year to RM695.9 billion. Growth strengthened during the second quarter, with loans increasing 1.7% from the previous quarter. Malaysia remained the strongest of Maybank’s major home markets, with loans growing 5.5% year-on-year. Indonesia recorded 4.3% growth, while Singapore loans increased 3.4%. Within Malaysia, Community Financial Services loans grew 5.3%. Consumer lending increased 5.7%, while SME loans expanded 2.7%. Singapore Community Financial Services loans increased 7.4%. title: 'Court allows temporary release of Shamsul Iskandar’s passport
body:
'

The Sessions Court has granted the temporary release of former PM’s political secretary Shamsul Iskandar’s passport for travel to Germany and London.

KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Shamsul Iskandar Mohd Akin, the former senior political secretary to the Prime Minister,  has obtained the Sessions Court’s approval for the temporary release of his international passport to enable him to attend several overseas programmes this month.

The passport had been surrendered to the court as an additional bail condition after he was charged with five counts of corruption.

According to his supporting affidavit obtained by the media, Shamsul Iskandar applied for the permanent return of his passport to facilitate overseas travel in connection with his duties.

He said he intended to travel to Frankfurt, Germany, to attend the Frankfurt Book Fair organised by Rex Education from Oct 7 to Nov 11.

“Based on my involvement with the Madani Community Leadership Academy, my participation in the book fair aims to foster synergy between organisations and provide mutual benefits to both entities.

“Therefore, this participation will provide valuable international exposure to support and strengthen ongoing grassroots initiatives aimed at empowering civil society in line with the MADANI principles, particularly through the promotion of literacy, leadership and knowledge,” he said in the affidavit.

Shamsul Iskandar also said he had registered to attend the fifth AlBaraka Summit, themed Ethics in Action: Rebuilding Foundations and Advancing the Global Impact of the Islamic Economy, in London scheduled for Oct 13 and 14.

He said the summit aimed to strengthen ethical foundations for Islamic financial and non-financial institutions, governance systems and market practices.

Shamsul Iskandar also said he planned to attend programmes in Ireland, as well as Bosnia and Herzegovina, in November and December.

During today’s proceedings, lawyer Yusmadi Yusoff, representing Shamsul Iskandar, told Sessions Court Judge Suzana Hussin that his client had filed an application on Sept 30 for the permanent return of his passport.

He also sought its temporary release to enable Shamsul Iskandar to attend programmes in Frankfurt and London this month.

Deputy Public Prosecutor Julaila Jamaludin objected to the application for the permanent return of the passport, saying the supporting documents consisted only of an invitation letter and that the discussions could be conducted online.

However, she did not object to the application for its temporary release.

Judge Suzana subsequently allowed the temporary release of Shamsul Iskandar’s passport, effective today, on condition that it be returned to the court on or before Oct 16.

The court also ordered the prosecution to file an affidavit in reply to the application for the permanent return of the passport by Oct 19, with the decision on the application set for Dec 8.

Shamsul Iskandar, 51, faces two charges of agreeing to accept RM140,000 in cash from businessman Tei Jiann Cheing, also known as Albert Tei, as an inducement to assist a company owned by Tei in obtaining approval for a mineral exploration licence in Sabah.

He also faces two charges of obtaining furniture and electrical appliances worth RM14,580.03 and RM22,249, respectively, from Tei for the same purpose.

The offences were allegedly committed at premises in Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya, and a hotel car park in Jalan Sultan Hishamuddin, as well as at Jalan P14A 1/1, Precinct 14, Putrajaya, between Nov 24, 2023, and March 5, 2024.

In a separate charge, Shamsul Iskandar is accused of obtaining gratification amounting to RM64,924 from Tei, allegedly deposited into a CIMB Bank account belonging to Rahmalidya Buyong to cover the rental of a house in Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya, in exchange for assisting Tei’s company in securing approval for a mineral exploration licence in Sabah.

All five charges were brought under Section 17(a) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009 (Act 694) and are punishable under Section 24(1) of the same Act, which provides for a maximum prison sentence of 20 years and a fine of at least five times the amount or value of the gratification, or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Opens Higher Amid Bargain Hunting
body: 'Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia's key index opened higher on Wednesday, driven by bargain hunting following recent losses, despite negative signals from Wall Street. According to BERNAMA News Agency, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) increased by 4.34 points, or 0.26 percent, reaching 1,648.30 at 9.10 am, recovering from Tuesday's close of 1,643.96. The index began the day 2.53 points higher at 1,646.49. In the broader market, decliners outnumbered gainers 214 to 174, with 293 counters remaining unchanged, 2,174 untraded, and 95 suspended. The turnover was recorded at 265.65 million shares valued at RM151.82 million. Thong Pak Leng, vice-president of equity research at Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, noted that the market is becoming increasingly oversold, presenting opportunities for selective accumulation in fundamentally strong blue-chip stocks. He added that any recovery might be limited unless foreign selling decreases and banking heavyweights receive more support. Thong also pointed out that energy, renewable infrastructure, and certain defensive stocks could perform well, whereas technology stocks remain vulnerable due to high global yields. He predicted a cautious trading session, with bargain hunting around 1,640, keeping the index within the 1,635-1,655 range. Among heavyweights, Maybank rose three sen to RM10.02, Public Bank gained two sen to RM4.74, while CIMB fell two sen to RM7.76. Tenaga Nasional increased by 10 sen to RM12.82, and IHH Healthcare remained steady at RM7.87. In active trading, Zetrix AI added half a sen to 17 sen, V.S Industry gained 1.5 sen to 25 sen, Visdynamics expanded 10 sen to 52 sen, while Cuscapi stayed at five sen, and Gamuda gained 13 sen to RM5.11. Leading gainers included Allianz Malaysia and MISC, both advancing 14 sen to RM21 and RM7.74, respectively. Hong Leong Industries moved up 10 sen to RM16.60, while MI Technovation and UMS Integration both increased by nine sen to RM5.48 and RM8.70. Eurospan led the losers, dropping 29 sen to RM2.95, followed by Petronas Dagangan, which lost 28 sen to RM19.04. Aeon Credit edged down 14 sen to RM5.05, while Dutch Lady and Hong Leong Bank decreased by 12 sen each to RM29.88 and RM23.16, respectively. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index fell 21.36 points to 17,588.72, while the FBM Emas Index rose 19.22 points to 12,284.69. The FBM Top 100 Index improved by 19.81 points to 12,071.35, and the FBM Emas Shariah Index increased by 25.02 points to 12,152.63. The FBM ACE Index decreased by 4.12 points to 5,524.46. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index slipped 0.36 of a point to 180.50, while the Energy Index fell 4.42 points to 864.28. The Financial Services Index gained 10.43 points to 19,271.29, and the Plantation Index added 1.86 points to 9,218.20.

title: 'Maybank Now Lets MAE Users Invest From RM10 With Savings+
body: 'Maybank customers can now invest in a Shariah-compliant money market fund through the MAE app from RM10. The new Savings+ feature provides access to the fund, which is managed by Maybank Asset Management. It aims to maintain liquidity by investing in relatively short-term and liquid assets. Potential returns stood at up to 3.32% per annum as of 30 June 2026. Returns are calculated daily and credited monthly. They are not guaranteed and may vary depending on market conditions and fund performance. Users can complete the required onboarding and suitability assessment, monitor their investment performance and set up automatic monthly investments within the app. Savings+ has no lock-in period. Investments and withdrawals are processed within an average of two business days. Mohd Amri bin Mohd Sofian, Head, Community Financial Services Malaysia said, “At Maybank, we believe investing should be as simple and accessible as everyday banking. With Savings+, customers can start their investment journey from just RM10 and manage their money seamlessly within the MAE app they already use daily. This reflects our commitment to humanising financial services by making wealth-building more accessible, convenient and relevant to every Malaysian.” The launch expands MAE’s range of investment products, which includes the Maybank Islamic Gold Account-i, Maybank Goal-Based Investment and ASNB Investment. Maybank Savings+ is available to new and existing customers. Savings+ is an investment product rather than a savings or deposit account. Customers should review the relevant product documents for details on fees, risks and processing times. Featured image: Edited by Fintech News Malaysia, based on image by graphic_library via Magnific

title: 'Smoky Singapore Gears Up to Talk Money Ahead of F1
body: 'SINGAPORE (Oct 5): Regional, business, cryptocurrency and sports leaders are meeting in Singapore for a slew of finance-focused conferences ahead of this weekend's Grand Prix as haze continues to shroud the city state. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, famed investor Ray Dalio and Eric Trump, a co-founder of the family-backed cryptocurrency business, are expected, while hundreds of thousands of Formula One (F1) fans will converge on the island. The night race through the city streets and some 40 sideline events are typically a global showcase for Singapore and hotel room rates have soared. The Fullerton Bay Hotel next to the race track is charging S$5,030 (US$3,933 or RM16,054) a night for a room that typically costs US$1,460. This year, the pall from Indonesia's most intense fires in more than a decade will probably form part of the backdrop. Air quality was forecast at the "high moderate to low unhealthy" range on Monday by Singapore's environment agency. No longer-range forecast was provided for Sunday's Grand Prix. Singapore's tourism board said F1 and its surrounding events had "strong momentum" reflecting confidence despite economic and geopolitical uncertainty. Jitters in financial markets where bond prices are slumping and sentiment around artificial intelligence is shifting from euphoric to cautious will occupy investors and business chiefs at the Forbes Global CEO Conference and Milken Asia Summit, which runs from Wednesday. Trump, a co-founder of crypto venture World Liberty Financial, is due to speak at the TOKEN2049 cryptocurrency event with digital asset markets fragile following a bruising 12 months. A hoped-for regulatory framework failed last month to clear the US Senate, in part as President Donald Trump's personal crypto dealings became a flashpoint for Democrats. Despite a recent bounce, the total value of the cryptocurrency market is down about a quarter over the last 12 months to US$3 trillion, according to data aggregator CoinGecko. Still, organisers say their event is nearly sold out with 25,000 attendees expected, the same as last year. The Straits Times reported that about 90,000 "c-suite", or top-ranking, executives will be in town. F1 generates around S$145 million in incremental tourism receipts for Singapore each year, according to official estimates. Maybank economist Chua Hak Bin expects it to hit S$160 million this year, along with "wider economic benefits" from deals struck at sideline events.
